Pair 3 — wrong: **bet land** = flood plain while floodwater stays on it; land between two rivers = **doab**.
xa: **Chambal valley** badlands (**APPSC 2022**).
Lacustrine plains = **filled lake beds**.
**Prayag** = confluence (e.g. **Devprayag**).

13.s: Which one of the following statements regarding plains is correct?
o: Lacustrine plains are found only along active volcanoes.
Plains are generally situated below 200 metres.
All plains are formed exclusively by river deposition.
Till plains are formed by marine waves alone.
13.x: Plains are generally below 200 metres in elevation. They may be alluvial, flood plain, lacustrine, peneplain or till plains and therefore have different origins.
13.tq: Test the general quantitative characteristic while rejecting overgeneralised alternatives.
xs: **Plains are generally situated below 200 metres** — option **(2)**.
Plains have varied origins — **alluvial**, **flood plain**, **lacustrine**, **peneplain**, **till plains** — so not all are river-built.
**Lacustrine** = filled lake beds; **till plains** = **glacial** deposits, not waves.
xa: Alluvial plain (Indo-Gangetic) = **most densely populated**, India's **youngest** division.
Peninsular plateau = **rejuvenated peneplain**.
Kashmir **Karewas** = lacustrine deposits.

13.s:
Consider the following landforms:
1. Horn
2. Esker
3. U-valley
4. Moraine
Which of the above are associated with glacial activity?
13.x: Horn, esker, U-valley and moraine are all glacial landforms or deposits.
13.tq: Use group classification to identify the common geomorphic agent.
xs: **All four** — horn, esker, U-valley and moraine — are glacial — option **(4)**.
**Horn**: pointed peak where cirques cut back from several sides (**Matterhorn**).
**Esker**: winding ridge of **stratified** sediment; **U-valley**: glacier-widened valley; **moraine**: unsorted debris.
xa: Glacier landforms also include **cirque**, **hanging valley**, **till**.
⚠ **Moraine** = unsorted; **esker** = **stratified**.
**APPSC-G2 2023**: Cirque — glaciers; Delta — running water; Cliffs — waves and currents; Sand dunes — winds.

13.s: Till, moraine and boulder clay are deposits associated with which geomorphic process?
13.x: Till, moraine and boulder clay are deposits of glacial activity.
13.tq: Test the agent behind a closely related group of depositional terms.
xs: Till, moraine and boulder clay = **glacial activity** — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2017**).
**Waves** make cliffs and stacks; **wind** makes dunes and loess; **groundwater solution** makes sinkholes and stalactites.
xa: Moraine types: **lateral** (edges), **terminal** (snout), **medial**, **ground**.
**Drumlin** = oval hill of till; drumlin fields = "**basket of eggs**".
**Outwash plain** = sand and gravel spread by meltwater.

13.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Glacial landform)
a. Cirque
b. Arete
c. Horn
List-II (Description)
i. Knife-edge ridge between two cirques
ii. Pointed peak where cirques cut back from several sides (e.g. Matterhorn)
iii. Armchair-shaped, scooped-out hollow at the valley head
Select the correct answer:
13.x: A cirque is the armchair-shaped hollow at the valley head (iii); an arete is the knife-edge ridge between two cirques (i); a horn is the pointed peak formed when cirques cut back from several sides, like the Matterhorn (ii). The other codes swap these descriptions.
13.tq: Cirque = chair, arete = edge, horn = peak.
xs: Correct code: **a-iii, b-i, c-ii** — option **(1)**.
**Cirque** = armchair-shaped hollow at the valley head (iii); **arete** = knife-edge ridge between two cirques (i).
**Horn** = pointed peak where cirques cut back from several sides, e.g. **Matterhorn** (ii).
xa: **U-shaped valley**: glacier deepens and widens a river valley.
**Hanging valley**: tributary left high; stream enters as a **waterfall** (**UKPSC 2024**).
**Fjord**: glacial valley drowned by the sea (**Norway**, Greenland, New Zealand).

13.s:
Consider the following statements regarding a U-shaped valley:
1. It is formed when a glacier deepens and widens a river valley.
2. Ice generally moves faster in the centre than near the sides.
3. It is characteristically produced by wind erosion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. A U-shaped valley is a glacial, not an aeolian, landform, so statement 3 is false.
13.tq: Find the one statement that belongs to a different geomorphic agent.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 — correct: a **glacier deepens and widens** a river valley.
Statement 2 — correct: **ice moves faster in the centre**.
Statement 3 — wrong: the U-valley is a **glacial**, not wind, landform.
xa: **Hanging valley**: tributary valley left high above the deepened main valley.
**Fjord** = glacially carved valley drowned by the sea.
V-shaped valley = **running water** (river).

13.s: A tributary valley that remains high above a deeply eroded main glacial valley and commonly enters it through a waterfall is called a
13.x: A hanging valley is a tributary valley left at a higher level than the deepened main valley, often producing a waterfall at its junction.
13.tq: Apply the relative-height description to identify the landform.
xs: This is a **hanging valley** — option **(4)**; its stream enters the main valley as a **waterfall** (agent = glacier, **UKPSC 2024**).
A **blind valley** ends where its stream vanishes underground (karst); a **playa** is a seasonal desert salt lake.
xa: **U-shaped valley**: glacier deepens and widens the main valley.
**Cirque** = armchair-shaped hollow at the valley head.
**Fjord** = glacial valley drowned by the sea.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about glacial deposits:
1. Moraine or till consists of unsorted glacial debris.
2. An esker is a long, winding ridge of stratified sediment marking a sub-glacial tunnel.
3. A terminal moraine is deposited along the edges of a glacier.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: moraine/till is unsorted glacial debris. Statement 2 is correct: an esker is a winding ridge of stratified sediment from a sub-glacial tunnel. Statement 3 is wrong: a terminal moraine forms at the snout; deposits along the edges are lateral moraines. Hence 1 and 2 only.
13.tq: Till is unsorted, esker is stratified; lateral = edges, terminal = snout.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 — correct: **moraine/till** = **unsorted** glacial debris.
Statement 2 — correct: an **esker** is a winding ridge of **stratified** sediment marking a **sub-glacial tunnel**.
Statement 3 — wrong: a **terminal** moraine forms at the **snout**; at the edges = **lateral** moraine.
xa: Other moraines: **medial**, **ground**.
**Drumlin**: oval hill of till; long axis parallel to ice flow.
Also glacial: **kettle holes**, **outwash plain**.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about drumlins:
1. A drumlin is an oval, egg-shaped hill of till.
2. The long axis of a drumlin lies at right angles to the direction of ice flow.
3. A field of drumlins gives 'basket of eggs' topography.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: a drumlin is an oval, egg-shaped hill of till. Statement 2 is wrong: its long axis is parallel to ice flow, with the blunt end facing the ice. Statement 3 is correct: drumlin fields give 'basket of eggs' topography. Hence 1 and 3 only.
13.tq: Drumlins line up with the ice flow like eggs in a basket.
xs: **Statements 1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 — correct: a **drumlin** is an **oval, egg-shaped hill of till**.
Statement 2 — wrong: the long axis is **parallel to ice flow**, with the **blunt end facing the ice**.
Statement 3 — correct: drumlin fields give "**basket of eggs**" topography.
xa: Some notes attach "basket of eggs" to **boulder deposits**.
**Esker** = stratified ridge from a sub-glacial tunnel.
Till, moraine and boulder clay = **glacial activity** (**APPSC 2017**).

13.s: Which one of the following is formed by sand and gravel spread by meltwater streams beyond a glacier?
13.x: An outwash plain consists of sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams issuing from a glacier.
13.tq: Match the depositional material with the responsible process.
xs: Sand and gravel spread by **meltwater streams** form an **outwash plain** — option **(4)**.
**Hanging valley**, **cirque** and **horn** are **erosional** glacial forms, not meltwater deposits.
xa: ⚠ **Moraine** = unsorted debris; **esker** = **stratified** sediment.
**Kettle holes** are also glacial features.
**Loess** of the **Plain of Normandy** comes from **glacial outwash**.

13.s: A fjord is best described as a
o: ridge of rock parallel to wind direction
desert basin containing a seasonal salt lake
sand ridge joining an island to the mainland
glacially carved valley drowned by the sea
13.x: A fjord is a glacially carved valley subsequently submerged by the sea. Norway, Greenland and New Zealand are associated with fjords.
13.tq: Distinguish a drowned glacial valley from coastal depositional landforms.
xs: A **fjord** is a **glacially carved valley drowned by the sea** — option **(4)**.
Examples: **Norway**, **Greenland**, **New Zealand**.
A ridge parallel to the wind is a **yardang**; a seasonal desert salt lake is a **playa**; a bar joining an island to the mainland is a **tombolo**.
xa: Coast types: **Ria** = drowned river valley (NW Spain), ranges at **right angles** to the shore.
**Dalmatian** = ranges **parallel** to the coast (Adriatic, Croatia).
**U-shaped valley**: glacier deepens and widens a river valley.

13.s: A depression formed when wind removes loose fine particles from the ground is called a
13.x: A deflation hollow is produced by the wind lifting and removing loose fine particles, leaving a depression.
13.tq: Match the wind process with the resulting surface feature.
xs: A depression left when wind lifts away loose fine particles is a **deflation hollow** — option **(3)**.
**Yardang** = streamlined ridge parallel to the wind; **zeugen** = table-like ridge; **playa** = seasonal salt lake.
xa: Wind transport: **deflation**, **saltation** (bouncing), **surface creep**.
**Mushroom rock**: base abraded more than the top.
**Loess** = fine wind-blown silt carried far.

13.s: A mushroom rock develops mainly because
o: the base is abraded more intensively by wind than the top
the top is dissolved by rainfall while the base is protected
the rock is submerged by a rising sea
the rock is deposited by meltwater
13.x: Wind-driven sand is concentrated near the ground and abrades the base more than the upper part, producing an undercut mushroom rock.
13.tq: Infer the landform from the differential intensity of erosion.
xs: A mushroom rock forms because **the base is abraded more intensively by wind than the top** — option **(1)**.
The rock is **undercut at the base**.
xa: Other wind-erosion forms: **zeugen**, **yardang**.
⚠ A "table-like" ridge is a **zeugen**; a **yardang** is a ridge parallel to the wind.
**Inselberg**: isolated residual hill, e.g. **Uluru**.

13.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a yardang from a zeugen?
o: A yardang is a ridge parallel to wind direction, whereas a zeugen is a table-like ridge with a hard cap over soft rock.
A yardang is an isolated residual hill, whereas a zeugen is a glacial ridge.
A yardang is a shallow lake, whereas a zeugen is a deflation hollow.
A yardang is a crescent dune, whereas a zeugen is a salt lake.
13.x: Yardangs are streamlined, steep-sided ridges parallel to wind direction. Zeugen are tabular ridges in which a hard cap protects softer rock beneath.
13.tq: Compare similar-looking aeolian features by structure and orientation.
xs: A **yardang** is a **ridge parallel to wind direction**; a **zeugen** is a **table-like ridge with a hard cap over soft rock** — option **(1)**.
An isolated residual hill is an **inselberg**; a crescent dune is a **barchan**; a shallow salt lake is a **playa**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: a "table-like" yardang description fits the **zeugen**.
Yardang ridges are of **soft rock**, long, steep-sided and streamlined.
**Mesa** → **butte** (smaller remnant).

13.s:
Consider the following statements about sand dunes:
1. A barchan is a crescent-shaped dune.
2. The horns of a barchan point upwind.
3. Seif dunes are long, narrow longitudinal dunes found in groups where sand is scarce.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: a barchan is crescent-shaped. Statement 2 is wrong: its horns point downwind. Statement 3 is correct: seifs are long, narrow longitudinal dunes in groups where sand is scarce. Hence 1 and 3 only.
13.tq: Barchan horns run ahead with the wind - downwind.
xs: **Statements 1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 — correct: a **barchan** is **crescent-shaped**.
Statement 2 — wrong: barchan horns point **downwind**.
Statement 3 — correct: **seifs** are long, narrow longitudinal dunes in groups where **sand is scarce**.
xa: Wind transport: **deflation, saltation, surface creep**.
**Erra Matti Dibbalu** = late-Quaternary **red dunes**, Visakhapatnam (UNESCO Tentative List, Sep 2025).
**Playa** = seasonal salt lake in a desert basin.

13.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Loess is fine wind-blown silt carried far and deposited.
2. The loess of the Plain of Normandy is derived from glacial outwash silt.
3. The loess of Manchuria is derived from dust from the Sahara.
4. Uluru is an example of an inselberg.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: loess is fine wind-blown silt carried far. Statement 2 is correct: Normandy's loess is periglacial silt blown from Ice Age glacial outwash. Statement 3 is wrong: Manchuria's loess comes from Mongolia. Statement 4 is correct: Uluru is an isolated residual hill (inselberg). Hence 1, 2 and 4 only.
13.tq: Normandy - glacial outwash; Manchuria - Mongolia; China - Loess Plateau.
xs: **Statements 1, 2 and 4 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 — correct: **loess** = fine wind-blown silt carried far.
Statement 2 — correct: **Plain of Normandy** loess is from **glacial outwash**.
Statement 3 — wrong: **Manchuria**'s loess comes from **Mongolia**; statement 4 — correct: **Uluru** is an **inselberg**.
xa: Largest loess example: **Loess Plateau of China**.
**Mesa** (wide flat-topped table hill) → **butte** (smaller remnant).
Wind-blown landforms: sand dunes, yardang, mushroom rock, loess.

13.s: Which sequence represents the usual order from a mesa to its smaller erosional remnant?
13.x: A mesa is a broad, flat-topped table hill; continued erosion may reduce it to a smaller butte.
13.tq: Apply the erosional reduction sequence from larger remnant to smaller remnant.
xs: **Mesa → butte** — option **(2)**.
A **mesa** is a wide flat-topped table hill; erosion leaves a smaller remnant, the **butte**.
An **inselberg** is an isolated residual hill (Uluru); a **playa** is a seasonal salt lake.
xa: **Zeugen** = tabular ridge, hard cap over soft rock.
**Mushroom rock** = undercut at the base by wind.
**Deflation hollow** = depression from wind lifting fine particles.

13.s:
Wind transports sand grains through which of the following mechanisms?
1. Deflation
2. Saltation
3. Surface creep

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: Wind movement of grains includes deflation, saltation or bouncing, and surface creep along the ground.
13.tq: Recognise all the listed modes of aeolian sediment movement.
xs: Wind moves grains by **deflation, saltation and surface creep** — all three, option **(4)**.
**Saltation** = bouncing; **deflation** lifts away loose fine particles; **surface creep** rolls grains along the ground.
xa: Deflation leaves a **deflation hollow**.
Fine dust carried far = **loess**.
Dunes: **barchan** (crescent), **seif** (longitudinal).

13.s: Karst topography develops most characteristically in regions underlain by:
13.x: Karst landscapes are carved mainly by groundwater dissolving limestone or dolomite.
13.tq: Use the rock-type association to identify the landscape-forming process.
xs: Karst forms where groundwater dissolves **limestone or dolomite** — option **(3)**.
Granite/gneiss weather to **red soils** and basalt to **black soils**; they do not form karst.
xa: Named after the **Karst** region on the **Adriatic coast** (Slovenia).
Sequence: **sinkhole → doline → uvala → polje**.
Cave deposits = **speleothems** of **calcium carbonate**.

13.s: The term ‘Karst’ is derived from the name of a region located on the:
13.x: The term Karst is derived from the Karst region on the Adriatic coast in Slovenia.
13.tq: Discriminate between similar coastal locations using the exact regional association.
xs: "Karst" comes from the Karst region on the **Adriatic coast of Slovenia** — option **(3)**.
Karst = landscape carved by groundwater dissolving **limestone/dolomite**.
xa: Longest caves: India = **Krem Liat Prah** (Meghalaya); world = **Mammoth Cave** (USA).
**Polje** = large depression from collapse of an underground cave.
**Dalmatian coast** is also on the **Adriatic** (Croatia).

13.s:
Arrange the following karst features in ascending order of their usual scale or stage of development:
A. Polje
B. Sinkhole
C. Uvala
D. Doline
13.x: A sinkhole is a small depression; several sinkholes may form a doline, several dolines may merge into a uvala, and a polje is a much larger depression often related to cave collapse.
13.tq: Use the progression from small individual depression to large collapsed depression.
xs: Ascending order **B, D, C, A** — **sinkhole → doline → uvala → polje** — option **(1)**.
**Sinkhole**: small, no surface outlet; **doline**: joined sinkholes; **uvala**: merged dolines; **polje**: large depression from **cave collapse**.
xa: Clay can seal a doline into a **doline lake**.
**Blind valley**: valley ending where its stream vanishes into a **swallow hole**.
**Sinking creek**: stream lost through cracks; open-topped ones = **bogas**.

13.s: What distinguishes a boga from an ordinary sinking creek?
o: A boga is a closed depression formed by cave collapse
A boga is a stream flowing over a glacier
A boga is an open-topped sinking creek
A boga is a cave formed by marine erosion
13.x: Bogas are sinking creeks that are open at the top. They are a specific form of sinking creek in karst terrain.
13.tq: Separate two closely related karst terms by their defining structural feature.
xs: A **boga** is **an open-topped sinking creek** — option **(3)**.
A **sinking creek** is a stream lost through cracks; a closed depression from **cave collapse** is a **polje**.
xa: **Blind valley**: valley ends where the stream vanishes into a **swallow hole**.
Karst sequence: **sinkhole → doline → uvala → polje**.
Karst rock: **limestone/dolomite**.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about cave deposits in karst regions:
1. Stalactites hang from the roof of a cave.
2. Stalagmites hang from the roof of a cave.
3. When a stalactite and a stalagmite meet, they form a pillar or column.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: stalactites hang from the cave roof. Statement 2 is wrong: stalagmites rise from the floor. Statement 3 is correct: when they meet they form pillars/columns. Hence 1 and 3 only; '1 only' misses the pillar fact, and options with 2 are wrong.
13.tq: Stalac-T-ite holds Tight to the ceiling; stalaG-mite rises from the Ground.
xs: **Statements 1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 — correct: **stalactites** hang from the cave roof (**APPSC 2022**).
Statement 2 — wrong: **stalagmites rise from the floor**.
Statement 3 — correct: when they meet they form **pillars/columns**.
xa: Speleothems are of **calcium carbonate**.
**Belum** (Nandyal) and **Borra** (ASR) caves have stalactites and stalagmites.
**Arwah** caves (Meghalaya, Sohra): limestone caves with fossils (**APPSC 2018**).

13.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the longest natural cave systems mentioned?
o: India — Krem Liat Prah; World — Mammoth Cave
India — Mammoth Cave; World — Krem Liat Prah
India — Belum; World — Krem Liat Prah
13.x: Krem Liat Prah in Meghalaya is identified as India’s longest natural cave, while Mammoth Cave in the USA is identified as the world’s longest natural cave.
13.tq: Compare the national and global rankings without reversing the two levels.
xs: **India — Krem Liat Prah; World — Mammoth Cave** — option **(1)**.
**Krem Liat Prah** is in **Meghalaya**; **Mammoth Cave** is in the **USA**.
**Belum** is India's **2nd-longest** natural cave system; **Borra** is in the Ananthagiri hills.
xa: **Belum**: **Nandyal** district, black limestone; first discovered **1884** by **Robert Bruce Foote**.
Belum declared a **Geo-Heritage Site by GSI** (Jun 2025).
**APPSC-G1 2017**: karst among Bojjannakonda, Undavalli, Belum, Erravaram = **Belum**.

13.s: Which of the following set contains only the caves identified as karst caves in the material?
13.x: Belum and Borra are karstic limestone caves. Undavalli, Bojjannakonda and Erravaram are identified as not karst in this context.
13.tq: Separate the karst caves from the rock-cut or non-karst cave sites.
xs: **Belum and Borra** are the karst caves — option **(1)** is correct.
**Belum** (Nandyal): **black limestone**, stalactites and stalagmites; **Borra** (ASR): limestone karst caves with stalactites and stalagmites.
**Undavalli** and **Bojjannakonda** are **rock-cut** caves, and **Erravaram** is not karst (APPSC key).
xa: **APPSC-G1 2017**: karst among Bojjannakonda, Undavalli, Belum, Erravaram = **Belum**.
Karst = groundwater dissolving **limestone/dolomite**.
Belum = **2nd-longest** natural cave system in India, after **Krem Liat Prah** (Meghalaya).

13.s: Belum Caves are primarily characterised by:
o: Black limestone with stalactites and stalagmites
13.x: Belum Caves are developed in black limestone and contain stalactites and stalagmites, reflecting their karst nature.
13.tq: Identify the cave from its rock type and internal formations.
xs: Belum Caves are **black limestone with stalactites and stalagmites** — option **(4)** is correct.
That makes Belum a **karst** cave — carved by groundwater dissolving limestone.
**Sandstone** and **Buddhist stupas** fit Undavalli and Bojjannakonda, which are rock-cut, not karst.
xa: Belum: **2nd-longest** natural cave system in India.
First discovered **1884** by **Robert Bruce Foote**; mapped by **H.D. Gebauer** (1982-84).
Declared a **Geo-Heritage Site by GSI** (Jun 2025).

13.s: Belum Caves were first discovered in 1884 by Robert Bruce Foote and mapped during 1982–84 by:
13.x: Robert Bruce Foote is associated with the first discovery of Belum Caves in 1884, while H. D. Gebauer mapped them during 1982–84.
13.tq: Separate the discoverer from the later mapper and use the date as a confirmation clue.
xs: Belum was mapped during **1982-84** by **H.D. Gebauer** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Robert Bruce Foote** only first discovered it in **1884**; **William King George** is linked (per some notes) to **Borra**'s discovery in **1807**.
xa: Belum is in **Nandyal** district (older notes: Kurnool).
Belum feature: **Patalaganga**.
Belum = **Geo-Heritage Site by GSI** (Jun 2025).

13.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with Belum Caves?
13.x: Patalaganga is associated with Belum Caves. The Gosthani flows through Borra Caves, Mesolithic paintings are noted at Borra, and the monolithic Buddha is associated with Bojjannakonda.
13.tq: Use distinctive cave-specific features to avoid swapping associated names.
xs: **Patalaganga** is matched with Belum Caves — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Gosthani** flows through **Borra**, which also has the **Mesolithic paintings**.
The **monolithic Buddha in Dhyana mudra** is at **Bojjannakonda**.
xa: Belum: **black limestone**, stalactites and stalagmites.
Belum is India's **2nd-longest** natural cave system.
⚠ **Belum** (Nandyal) and **Borra** (ASR) = karst; **Undavalli** and **Bojjannakonda** = rock-cut.

13.s: Undavalli Caves are best described as:
o: Natural limestone caves through which the Gosthani flows
Buddhist rock-cut caves with a monolithic Buddha in Dhyana mudra
Rock-cut cave temples associated with the Vishnukundins and a reclining Vishnu image
13.x: Undavalli consists of rock-cut cave temples associated with the Vishnukundins and contains a reclining Anantasayana Vishnu. It is not a karst cave.
13.tq: Match the cave with its religious, architectural and dynastic features.
xs: Undavalli has **rock-cut cave temples** of the **Vishnukundins**, with a **reclining Anantasayana Vishnu** — option **(4)**.
The **Gosthani** flows through **Borra**; **Patalaganga** is in **Belum**; the **Dhyana mudra Buddha** is at **Bojjannakonda**.
xa: Undavalli: **four-storey**, **4th-5th c. CE**, near **Vijayawada**, **Guntur** district.
Carved from a **sandstone** hill (some notes say granite); **not karst**.
⚠ **Undavalli** and **Bojjannakonda** = rock-cut, not karst.

13.s: Undavalli Caves are carved mainly from a:
13.x: Undavalli Caves are described as being carved from a sandstone hill. They are rock-cut caves rather than karst caves.
13.tq: Use the rock-type distinction to separate a rock-cut cave from a solutional cave.
xs: Undavalli Caves are carved from a **sandstone hill** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes say **granite**; either way they are **rock-cut**, not karst.
**Black limestone** is the rock of **Belum**.
xa: Undavalli: **Vishnukundins**, four-storey, **4th-5th c. CE**.
Reclining **Anantasayana Vishnu**.
Located near **Vijayawada**, **Guntur** district.

13.s: Bojjannakonda at Sankaram is associated with:
13.x: Bojjannakonda at Sankaram is a Buddhist rock-cut hilltop monastery complex with caves and stupas. It is not classified as a karst cave.
13.tq: Identify the site from its religious and architectural association.
xs: Bojjannakonda at **Sankaram** has **Buddhist rock-cut caves and stupas** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is a **hilltop monastery** with a monolithic Buddha in **Dhyana mudra** (**Mahayana-Vajrayana**); **not karst**.
**Black-limestone karst** = **Belum**; fossil limestone caves of Meghalaya = **Arwah**; **Vishnukundin** temples = **Undavalli**.
xa: Bojjannakonda is in **Anakapalli** (Visakhapatnam region).
⚠ **Belum** and **Borra** = karst; **Undavalli** and **Bojjannakonda** = rock-cut.
**APPSC-G1 2017** karst answer = **Belum**.

13.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
13.x: Bojjannakonda is located at Sankaram in Anakapalli, not Nandyal district. Arwah, Borra and Undavalli are correctly associated with Meghalaya, the Alluri Sitharama Raju area and the Guntur area respectively.
13.tq: Locate the swapped district by comparing the AP cave sites.
xs: **Bojjannakonda — Nandyal district** is wrong — option **(4)**: Bojjannakonda is at **Sankaram, Anakapalli**.
**Undavalli — Guntur**, **Arwah — Meghalaya** (Sohra), **Borra — Alluri Sitharama Raju**: all correct.
xa: **Nandyal** district has **Belum** caves and **Billa Surgam**.
**Arwah**: limestone caves with fossils (**APPSC 2018**).
Borra: **Ananthagiri hills**, Araku; the **Gosthani** flows through.

13.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
13.x: Belum Caves are located in Nandyal district. Borra Caves are in Alluri Sitharama Raju district, Billa Surgam is in Nandyal, and Gandikota is in YSR Kadapa.
13.tq: Start with the known landmark–district pair and eliminate the swapped locations.
xs: **Belum Caves — Nandyal** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Borra** is in **Alluri Sitharama Raju** district; **Billa Surgam** is in **Nandyal**, NOT Anantapuramu; **Gandikota** is in **YSR Kadapa**.
xa: Gandikota: **Penna gorge**, "**Grand Canyon of India**".
Billa Surgam: **Palaeolithic** cave site with animal skeletal remains (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
Belum: older notes place it in **Kurnool**.

13.s: The Borra Caves are associated with which combination of district and geological features?
o: ASR district; limestone formations with stalactites and stalagmites
Nandyal district; black limestone without mineral formations
Guntur district; a four-storey rock-cut monastery
Kurnool district; a Palaeolithic site with animal skeletal remains
13.x: Borra Caves are in the ASR district in the Ananthagiri hills near Araku. They are limestone caves containing stalactites and stalagmites.
13.tq: Start from the sure district–feature pair and reject combinations belonging to other caves.
xs: Borra Caves: **ASR district**; **limestone** formations with **stalactites and stalagmites** — option **(1)**.
They lie in the **Ananthagiri hills**, Araku.
Black limestone in **Nandyal** = **Belum**; four-storey rock-cut caves in **Guntur** = **Undavalli**; Palaeolithic site with animal remains = **Billa Surgam**.
xa: The **Gosthani** flows through Borra.
Discovered **1807** (William King George per some notes).
Borra has **Mesolithic paintings**.

13.s: Which river passes through the Borra Caves?
13.x: The Gosthani River passes through the Borra Caves. The caves are also associated with Mesolithic rock paintings.
13.tq: Link the cave with its specifically associated river rather than a major regional river.
xs: The **Gosthani** flows through the Borra Caves — option **(4)** is correct.
Borra: limestone karst caves in the **Ananthagiri hills**, Araku, **Alluri Sitharama Raju** district.
xa: Borra was discovered in **1807** (William King George per some notes).
Borra has **Mesolithic paintings**.
⚠ **Patalaganga** belongs to **Belum**, not Borra.

13.s: Belum Caves of Andhra Pradesh are notable as
o: The second-longest natural cave system in India
The longest natural cave system in the world
Rock-cut Buddhist caves of the Vishnukundin period
Sandstone caves through which the Gosthani flows
13.x: Belum (Nandyal) is India's second-longest natural cave system after Krem Liat Prah in Meghalaya. Mammoth Cave (USA) is the world's longest, Undavalli is the Vishnukundin rock-cut site, and the Gosthani flows through the limestone Borra Caves.
13.tq: Belum = 2nd-longest in India (after Krem Liat Prah); karst, black limestone.
xs: Belum is **the second-longest natural cave system in India** — option **(1)**.
The longest in India is **Krem Liat Prah** (Meghalaya); the world's longest is **Mammoth Cave** (USA).
Vishnukundin rock-cut caves = **Undavalli**; the Gosthani flows through **Borra**.
xa: Belum: **black limestone**, stalactites and stalagmites; **Nandyal** district.
First discovered **1884** by **Robert Bruce Foote**.
**Geo-Heritage Site by GSI** (Jun 2025).

13.s: Which statement correctly describes the cave paintings of Kethavaram?
o: They are in Chittoor district and mainly depict elephants.
They are in Visakhapatnam district and exclusively depict cattle.
They are in Kurnool district, where deer is the most painted animal.
They are in Anantapur district and mainly depict horses.
13.x: Kethavaram caves are in Kurnool district, and deer is the most frequently painted animal. A half-painted deer has also been found in Kurnool district.
13.tq: Pair the cave site with its dominant painted animal and district.
xs: Kethavaram caves are in **Kurnool district**, where **deer is the most painted animal** — option **(3)**.
A **half-painted deer** has also been found in Kurnool district.
xa: **Billa Surgam** (Nandyal, erstwhile Kurnool): **Palaeolithic** cave site (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
Kurnool caves and **Muchatla Chintamani Gavi** yielded **bone tools** (Upper Palaeolithic).
**Borra** caves have **Mesolithic paintings**.

13.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Muchchatla Chintamanu Gavi — Upper Palaeolithic bone tools
13.x: Billa Surgam is associated with Kurnool/Nandyal and not Anantapuramu. It is a Palaeolithic cave site with animal skeletal remains.
13.tq: Find the wrong district–site pair; the location is the decisive trap.
xs: **Billa Surgam — Anantapuramu district** is wrong — option **(3)**: Billa Surgam is in **Nandyal** (erstwhile **Kurnool**).
Billa Surgam is a **Palaeolithic** cave site with animal skeletal remains: correct (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
**Kethavaram** — rock paintings (deer most painted), and **Muchchatla Chintamanu Gavi** — Upper Palaeolithic **bone tools**: correct.
xa: Kethavaram caves are in **Kurnool**.
**Belum** is also in **Nandyal**.
**Gandikota** (YSR Kadapa) = Penna gorge.

13.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chandragiri — Raja Mahal and Vijayanagara fort
Lepakshi — Veerabhadra temple with a hanging pillar
Undavalli Caves — Fort on the Penna gorge
Gandikota — Fort on the Penna gorge
13.x: Undavalli Caves are rock-cut caves in Guntur district containing a reclining Vishnu image. The fort on the Penna gorge is Gandikota.
13.tq: Reject the swapped monument–feature pairing.
xs: **Undavalli Caves — Fort on the Penna gorge** is wrong — option **(3)**.
The fort on the **Penna gorge** is **Gandikota** (**YSR Kadapa**), the "**Grand Canyon of India**".
**Undavalli** = rock-cut cave temples near Vijayawada (**Guntur**), with a reclining **Anantasayana Vishnu**.
xa: Gandikota also has the **Gandikota reservoir**.
Undavalli: **Vishnukundins**, **4th-5th c. CE**, sandstone hill.
⚠ Undavalli is **not karst**.

13.s:
Which of the following are recognised agents involved in coastal erosion?
1. Waves
2. Tides and currents
3. Wind
4. Glacial ice as the principal coastal agent

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: Waves are the main agents, while tides, currents and wind also contribute. Glacial ice is not the principal agent of ordinary coastal erosion, so statement 4 is false.
13.tq: Separate the principal agents from an unrelated geomorphic agent.
xs: **1, 2 and 3 only** — **waves**, **tides and currents**, and **wind** — option **(2)**.
**Waves** are the **main agent**; tides, currents and wind also act.
Glacial ice is **not** a coastal-erosion agent in the notes; glaciers make **fjords** inland valleys that the sea later drowns.
xa: Processes: **hydraulic action, abrasion (corrasion), attrition**, solution.
Sequence: sea cliff + **wave-cut platform** → sea cave → **arch** → **stack** → stump.
AP: severe erosion at **Uppada** (Kakinada) and the **Krishna coast**.

13.s:
Which of the following are processes of coastal erosion?
1. Hydraulic action
2. Abrasion (corrasion)
3. Attrition
4. Saltation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: Hydraulic action, abrasion (corrasion) and attrition, along with solution, are the processes of coastal erosion. Saltation (bouncing of grains) is a mode of wind transport, not a coastal erosion process. Hence 1, 2 and 3 only.
13.tq: Saltation belongs to wind transport (deflation, saltation, surface creep).
xs: **1, 2 and 3 only** — option **(2)**: **hydraulic action, abrasion (corrasion), attrition** (plus **solution**).
**Saltation** (bouncing) is a mode of **wind transport**, with deflation and surface creep.
xa: Agents: **waves** (main), tides and currents, wind.
Erosional sequence ends: **arch → stack → stump**.
Hard defences: **seawalls, groynes, offshore breakwaters**.

13.s:
Arrange the following coastal erosional features in the correct sequence of development:
A. Stack
B. Sea cave
C. Wave-cut platform
D. Arch
E. Stump

Select the correct answer.
13.x: The usual sequence is cliff and wave-cut platform, sea cave, arch, stack and finally stump.
13.tq: Use the progressive stages of coastal erosion from broad cutting to isolated remnants.
xs: Correct sequence **C, B, D, A, E** — option **(1)**.
**Wave-cut platform** (with sea cliff) → **sea cave** → **arch** → **stack** → **stump**.
xa: Main agent: **waves**.
Processes: **hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition**, solution.
Cliff and **stack** = waves and currents (**APPSC-G2 2023**: Cliffs — waves and currents).

13.s: Which one of the following is NOT a hard-engineering measure for coastal protection?
13.x: Beach nourishment is a soft coastal defence measure. Seawalls, groynes and offshore breakwaters are hard-engineering structures.
13.tq: Find the option belonging to the opposite category.
xs: **Beach nourishment** is a **soft** defence, not hard engineering — option **(3)**.
Hard defences: **seawalls**, **groynes**, **offshore breakwaters**.
xa: Soft defences: beach nourishment, **dune stabilisation**, **mangroves**.
Groynes are built **across longshore drift** to trap sand.
Human causes of erosion: harbours, **beach sand mining**, offshore dredging, **dams**.

13.s:
Which of the following human activities can reduce the supply of sediment to beaches and thereby intensify coastal erosion?
1. Harbour construction
2. Beach sand mining
3. Offshore dredging
4. Construction of dams

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: Harbours, sand mining, offshore dredging and dams can all disturb or reduce the natural supply and movement of coastal sediment.
13.tq: Recognise the common effect of several human interventions on sediment balance.
xs: **All four** — harbours, beach sand mining, offshore dredging and dams — option **(4)**.
**Dams** cut **sediment supply**; harbours, mining and dredging disturb or remove coastal sediment.
xa: **East coast** erodes more: soft, low-lying alluvial sand and silt, no rocky cliffs.
Soft defences: **beach nourishment**, dune stabilisation, mangroves.
AP: severe erosion at **Uppada** (Kakinada).

13.s:
Consider the following statements about the east coast of India:
1. It is more vulnerable to erosion because it is soft and low-lying.
2. It consists largely of alluvial sand and silt.
3. Its flat and wide plains allow the sea to move inland.
4. Rocky cliffs are a dominant feature throughout the coast.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: The east coast is soft, low-lying and largely alluvial, and its flat wide plains allow inland movement of the sea. Rocky cliffs are not dominant throughout this coast.
13.tq: Identify the single reversed physical characteristic in a set describing coastal erosion.
xs: **Statements 1, 2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statements 1 and 2 — correct: the **east coast** is **soft, low-lying alluvial sand and silt**.
Statement 3 — correct: **flat wide plains** let the sea move inland.
Statement 4 — wrong: the east coast has **no rocky cliffs**.
xa: AP: erosion severe at **Uppada** (Kakinada) and the **Krishna coast** (Jul 2026).
Human causes: harbours, sand mining, dredging, **dams cutting sediment supply**.
East-coast lagoons: **Chilika**, **Pulicat**.

13.s:
Which of the following statements about Dalmatian and ria coasts is correct?
1. In a Dalmatian coast, mountain ranges run parallel to the coast.
2. Drowning of a Dalmatian coast produces long islands and channels parallel to the shore.
3. In a ria coast, mountain ranges generally lie at right angles to the shore.
4. Croatia on the Adriatic is associated with the Dalmatian coast.
13.x: All four statements are correct. Parallel mountain ranges characterise the Dalmatian coast, while ranges at right angles are associated with ria coasts.
13.tq: Compare coast types by orientation of relief and the resulting drowned features.
xs: **All four statements** are correct — option **(4)**.
Statements 1 and 2 — correct: in a **Dalmatian** coast the ranges run **parallel** to the coast; drowning leaves **long islands + channels** parallel to shore.
Statement 3 — correct: in a **ria** coast the ranges lie at **right angles** to the shore.
Statement 4 — correct: Dalmatian = **Adriatic (Croatia)**.
xa: **Ria** = drowned **river** valley — **NW Spain**.
**Fiord** = drowned **glacial** valley — **Norway**.
⚠ **Ria** = right angles; **Dalmatian** = parallel.

13.s: A sand or shingle deposit lying between the low- and high-tide marks is called a
13.x: A beach is the zone of sand or shingle between the low- and high-tide limits.
13.tq: Use the positional definition to identify the coastal depositional feature.
xs: Sand or shingle between **low and high tide** is a **beach** — option **(1)**.
A **tombolo** joins an island to the mainland; a **spit** is a sand ridge joined to land at one end; a **bar** runs across a bay mouth.
xa: **Longshore drift** moves sediment along the coast.
Bar closing a bay → **lagoon** (**Chilika**, **Pulicat**).
Soft defence: **beach nourishment**.

13.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Spit — ridge joined to land at one end
Bar — ridge joining an island to the mainland
Tombolo — ridge across a desert basin
Beach — ridge across the mouth of a bay
13.x: A spit is a depositional sand ridge attached to the land at one end. A bar may cross a bay mouth, while a tombolo joins an island to the mainland.
13.tq: Separate coastal depositional features by their points of attachment.
xs: **Spit — ridge joined to land at one end** is correct — option **(1)**.
A **bar** is a ridge across a bay mouth; a **tombolo** joins an island to the mainland; a **beach** lies between low and high tide.
xa: Bar closing a bay → **lagoon**.
Spit and bar are made by **waves and currents**.
**Groynes** trap sand moved by longshore drift.

13.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A lagoon is shallow coastal water cut off from the sea by a bar, reef or sandbar.
2. An estuary retains a free connection with the sea.
3. A lagoon and an estuary are identical features because both are fully enclosed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. An estuary remains connected to the sea, whereas a lagoon is partly or substantially cut off; statement 3 is false.
13.tq: Use the distinction between restricted and free marine connection.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 — correct: a **lagoon** is shallow coastal water **cut off by a bar, reef or sandbar**.
Statement 2 — correct: an **estuary** keeps a **free connection** to the sea.
Statement 3 — wrong: they differ — an estuary is **not** enclosed.
xa: Lagoons: **Chilika**, **Pulicat**.
Estuaries: west-flowing **Narmada** and **Tapi**.
Estuary is an **ecotone**.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about longshore drift:
1. Longshore drift moves sediment along the shoreline.
2. Groynes are built across longshore drift to trap sand.
3. Groynes are a soft coastal defence measure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: longshore drift moves sediment along the coast. Statement 2 is correct: groynes built across it trap sand. Statement 3 is wrong: groynes are hard defences (with seawalls and breakwaters); soft measures are beach nourishment, dune stabilisation and mangroves. Hence 1 and 2 only.
13.tq: Built structures (seawall, groyne, breakwater) = hard; natural fixes = soft.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 — correct: **longshore drift** moves sediment along the shore.
Statement 2 — correct: **groynes** built across it **trap sand**.
Statement 3 — wrong: groynes are **hard** defences, with **seawalls** and **offshore breakwaters**.
xa: Soft defences: **beach nourishment**, **dune stabilisation**, **mangroves**.
Human causes of erosion: harbours, **sand mining**, dredging, dams.
Spit = sand ridge joined to land at one end.

13.s: Which of the following is a depositional coastal landform?
13.x: A spit is formed by deposition. Wave-cut platforms, sea arches and sea caves are erosional landforms.
13.tq: Find the depositional feature among predominantly erosional coastal forms.
xs: The **spit** is depositional — option **(2)** is correct.
**Sea arch**, **wave-cut platform** and **sea cave** are **erosional** features.
xa: Other depositional forms: **beach**, **bar**, **tombolo**.
Erosional sequence: cliff + **wave-cut platform** → cave → arch → **stack** → stump.
Bar closing a bay → **lagoon**.

13.s: A coastal bar closing a bay generally forms a:
13.x: When a bar closes a bay, the enclosed water body becomes a lagoon. Chilika and Pulicat are examples of lagoons.
13.tq: Apply the bar-and-bay formation process to identify the resulting water body.
xs: A bar closing a bay forms a **lagoon** — option **(1)**.
Examples: **Chilika**, **Pulicat**.
A **stack** is an erosional sea feature; a **peneplain** and **gorge** are river landforms.
xa: ⚠ **Lagoon** = cut off by a bar/reef vs **estuary** = free connection to the sea.
**Pulicat** = **saltwater** lake; **Kolleru** = freshwater.
**Tombolo** = bar joining an island to the mainland.

13.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Coast type)
a. Fiord
b. Ria
c. Dalmatian
List-II (Example)
i. Adriatic coast of Croatia
ii. Norway
iii. North-western Spain
13.x: Norway has fiord coasts, north-western Spain has ria coasts, and the Adriatic coast of Croatia is a Dalmatian coast.
13.tq: Start with Norway–fiord, the strongest sure pair, and complete the geographical matches.
xs: Correct code: **a–ii, b–iii, c–i** — option **(1)**.
**Fiord — Norway** (drowned glacial valley); **ria — NW Spain** (drowned river valley).
**Dalmatian — Adriatic coast of Croatia** (ranges parallel to the coast).
xa: ⚠ **Ria** = ranges at right angles to the shore; **Dalmatian** = ranges **parallel**.
Fjords also in **Greenland** and **New Zealand**.
Karst is named after a region on the same **Adriatic** coast (Slovenia).

13.s: Which one of the following groups consists exclusively of landforms produced by running water?
o: Sand dune, yardang, mushroom rock and loess
Sea cliff, stack, spit and bar
13.x: Delta, V-valley, gorge and canyon are formed by running water. The other groups represent glacial, marine and aeolian landforms respectively.
13.tq: Classify the options by matching each landform with its geomorphic agent.
xs: **Delta, V-valley, gorge and canyon** are all made by **running water** — option **(1)**.
Sand dune, yardang, mushroom rock, loess = **wind**; cliff, stack, spit, bar = **waves and currents**; cirque, horn, U-valley, esker = **glacier**.
xa: Running water also makes **levees** and **peneplains**.
Groundwater (solution in limestone): **sinkhole, doline, stalactite, stalagmite**.
**APPSC-G2 2023**: Delta — running water; Cirque — glaciers; Cliffs — waves; Sand dunes — winds.

13.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
13.x: A doline is a solutional depression produced by groundwater action in limestone, not by a glacier. Levees, stacks and loess are respectively associated with rivers, marine action and wind.
13.tq: Find the landform whose geomorphic agent belongs to a different group.
xs: **Doline — Glacier** is wrong — option **(4)**: a doline is made by **groundwater** (solution in limestone).
**Loess — wind**, **stack — waves and currents**, **levee — running water**: all correct.
xa: Doline = **joined sinkholes**; clay can seal it into a **doline lake**.
Karst sequence: **sinkhole → doline → uvala → polje**.
Glacial landforms: cirque, horn, U-valley, hanging valley, moraine, till, **esker**.

13.s: Which one of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?
13.x: An esker is a glacial depositional feature. Yardang and mushroom rock are aeolian features, while a peneplain is associated with prolonged fluvial denudation.
13.tq: Use the wrong-agent trap in a geomorphic-landform pairing.
xs: **Esker — Waves and currents** is wrong — option **(1)**: an esker is a **glacier** landform.
Esker = long, winding ridge of **stratified** sediment marking a **sub-glacial tunnel**.
**Mushroom rock** and **yardang** — wind; **peneplain** — running water: correct.
xa: ⚠ **Moraine** = unsorted; **esker** = stratified.
Waves and currents make **cliff, stack, spit, bar**.
Peninsular plateau = **rejuvenated peneplain**.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about hanging glaciers:
1. They are stranded on steep slopes as the main glacier thins.
2. Their collapse can set off ice-rock avalanches, LLOFs and GLOFs.
3. They form when the main glacier thickens and advances.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: hanging glaciers are stranded on steep slopes as the main glacier thins. Statement 2 is correct: their collapse can trigger ice-rock avalanches, LLOFs and GLOFs. Statement 3 is wrong: they are left behind by thinning, not thickening. Hence 1 and 2 only.
13.tq: Thinning glacier leaves ice 'hanging' - collapse means floods.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 — correct: hanging glaciers are **stranded on steep slopes as the main glacier thins**.
Statement 2 — correct: their collapse sets off **ice-rock avalanches, LLOFs and GLOFs** (Nepal flash flood, 1 Sep 2026).
Statement 3 — wrong: they form when the main glacier **thins**, not thickens.
xa: CWC monitors **2,843** glacial lakes and water bodies (**2,485** glacial lakes) from **2025**, up from **902**.
Monitoring is under **NRSC's Glacial Lake Atlas**.
⚠ Hanging **glacier** vs hanging **valley** (tributary valley left high, stream enters as a waterfall).

13.s: Severe coastal erosion in Andhra Pradesh has been particularly reported at which of the following locations?
o: Uppada in Kakinada and the Krishna coast
13.x: Severe coastal erosion has been reported at Uppada in Kakinada and along the Krishna coast. The other options refer to caves, lakes or deltaic features.
13.tq: Use location-based elimination by distinguishing coastal erosion sites from inland landforms and water bodies.
xs: Severe coastal erosion is at **Uppada in Kakinada and the Krishna coast** — option **(3)** (Jul 2026).
Vamsadhara and Penna are **minor deltas**; Borra and Belum are **caves**; Kolleru and Pulicat are **lakes**.
xa: **East coast** erodes more: soft, low-lying **alluvial sand and silt**.
Human causes: harbours, beach sand mining, dredging, **dams**.
Soft defences: beach nourishment, dune stabilisation, **mangroves**.

13.s: Which institution declared Belum Caves a Geo-Heritage Site?
13.x: The Geological Survey of India declared Belum Caves a Geo-Heritage Site. The other institutions are associated with remote sensing, water monitoring or international heritage listing.
13.tq: Apply the authority trap by identifying which institution is responsible for geological heritage recognition.
xs: Belum Caves were declared a **Geo-Heritage Site** by the **Geological Survey of India** (GSI) — option **(4)** (Jun 2025).
**NRSC** runs the **Glacial Lake Atlas**; **CWC** monitors glacial lakes; **UNESCO**'s Tentative List took Erra Matti Dibbalu and Tirumala Silathoranam.
xa: Belum = **2nd-longest** natural cave system in India.
Belum: **black limestone**, **Nandyal** district.
**APPSC-G1 2017**: karst topography = **Belum**.

13.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Erra Matti Dibbalu in Visakhapatnam consists of late-Quaternary red dunes.
2. Tirumala Silathoranam is a quartzite arch more than 1.5 billion years old.
3. Both sites were inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites in September 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: Erra Matti Dibbalu are late-Quaternary red dunes in Visakhapatnam. Statement 2 is correct: Silathoranam is a quartzite arch over 1.5 billion years old. Statement 3 is wrong: in Sep 2025 they were added to UNESCO's Tentative List (among 7 natural sites), not inscribed as World Heritage Sites. Hence 1 and 2 only.
13.tq: Tentative List is not inscription - a classic trap.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 — correct: **Erra Matti Dibbalu** = **late-Quaternary red dunes**, Visakhapatnam.
Statement 2 — correct: **Tirumala Silathoranam** = **quartzite arch**, **1.5+ billion yr** old.
Statement 3 — wrong: in **Sep 2025** they joined UNESCO's **Tentative List** (among **7** natural sites), not the World Heritage list.
xa: Collector ordered **tourism upgrades** at Erra Matti Dibbalu (15 May 2026).
Belum = **Geo-Heritage Site by GSI** (Jun 2025).
Wind landforms include **sand dunes** and **loess**.

13.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the deltaic and lacustrine features of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Godavari-Krishna delta plains are called the rice granary of South India, while Kolleru and Pulicat are both freshwater lakes.
The Godavari-Krishna delta plains are called the rice granary of South India, while Kolleru is freshwater and Pulicat is saltwater.
The Krishna and Penna delta plains are called the rice granary of South India, while Kolleru is saltwater.
The Vamsadhara and Penna are the principal lakes of the coastal plain, while Pulicat is freshwater.
13.x: The Godavari-Krishna delta plains are known as the rice granary of South India. Kolleru is a freshwater lake and Pulicat is a saltwater lake.
13.tq: Check the descriptive title, river-delta association and freshwater–saltwater contrast together.
xs: **Godavari-Krishna delta plains** = "**rice granary of South India**"; **Kolleru** is **freshwater**, **Pulicat** is **saltwater** — option **(2)**.
Option 1 is wrong because **Pulicat is saltwater**; **Vamsadhara** and **Penna** are minor deltas, not lakes.
xa: Pulicat is a **lagoon** formed by a bar closing a bay.
Minor deltas: **Vamsadhara** and **Penna**.
Coastal erosion: **Uppada** (Kakinada), Krishna coast.

13.s: Which of the following pairs consists of the minor deltas mentioned in relation to the coastal plains of Andhra Pradesh?
13.x: Vamsadhara and Penna are identified as minor deltas. Godavari and Krishna form the major deltaic plains, whereas Kolleru and Pulicat are lakes.
13.tq: Start from the sure river–landform association and reject options containing lakes or places.
xs: The minor deltas are **Vamsadhara and Penna** — option **(1)**.
**Godavari and Krishna** form the major delta plains; **Kolleru and Pulicat** are lakes; **Uppada** is an erosion site, **Borra** a cave.
xa: Godavari-Krishna delta plains = "**rice granary of South India**".
Delta types: **arcuate** (Nile), **cuspate** (Tiber), **bird-foot** (Mississippi).
Kolleru = **freshwater**; Pulicat = **saltwater**.

13.s: As per the Glacial Lake Atlas of the National Remote Sensing Centre, the Central Water Commission now monitors how many glacial lakes and water bodies?
13.x: From 2025, the Central Water Commission monitors 2,843 glacial lakes and water bodies, including 2,485 glacial lakes; the earlier number was 902.
13.tq: Separate the total number from the number of glacial lakes included within that total.
xs: CWC now monitors **2,843** glacial lakes and water bodies — option **(3)** (from **2025**).
**2,485** of these are **glacial lakes**; **902** was the earlier number.
xa: Monitoring is under **NRSC's Glacial Lake Atlas**.
Hanging glaciers collapsing → **ice-rock avalanches, LLOFs and GLOFs**.
Example: **Nepal flash flood** (1 Sep 2026).

14.s: Which one of the following gases constitutes approximately 0.93 per cent by volume of the atmosphere?
14.x: Argon constitutes about 0.93 per cent by volume of the atmosphere. Carbon dioxide, neon and krypton occur in much smaller proportions.
14.tq: Use the exact numerical composition rather than confusing the trace gases with argon.
xs: **Argon** makes up about **0.93%** of the atmosphere by volume — option **(4)**.
xa: Order: **Nitrogen > Oxygen > Argon > CO2** (APPSC-G1 **2023**).
⚠ Third place = **Argon**, not CO2.

14.s: The approximate percentage by volume of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, as given in the standard composition table, is
14.x: Carbon dioxide constitutes about 0.04 per cent by volume in the standard atmospheric composition table. Its concentration is also expressed in parts per million.
14.tq: Distinguish percentage values by placing the decimal at the correct order of magnitude.
xs: **CO2** is about **0.04 per cent** by volume — option **(2)**.
Older notes give **0.036**.
CO2 is **transparent to incoming sunlight** but **absorbs outgoing terrestrial radiation** (greenhouse gas).
xa: CO2 rose **3.5 ppm** to **423.9 ppm** in **2024** (WMO Bulletin **2025**).
CO2 and water vapour reach only about **90 km**.
⚠ CO2 is **fourth**, behind **Argon (0.93%)**.

14.s: According to the WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin 2025, the atmospheric concentration of carbon dioxide in 2024 was approximately
14.x: Per the WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin 2025, CO2 rose by 3.5 ppm to 423.9 ppm in 2024, the largest rise since 1957 and about 152% of the pre-industrial level.
14.tq: Test the precise current-affairs figure against nearby numerical distractors.
xs: CO2 reached **423.9 ppm** in **2024** — option **(1)** (WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin **2025**).
It rose **3.5 ppm** — the **largest rise since 1957**.
That is **152%** of the pre-industrial level.
xa: By volume CO2 is about **0.04%** (older notes: **0.036**).
CO2 absorbs **outgoing terrestrial radiation** — a greenhouse gas.
**Water vapour** is the **most abundant greenhouse gas**.

14.s:
Consider the following statements about atmospheric water vapour:
1. It may constitute up to 4 per cent of the atmosphere in warm, wet tropical regions.
2. It is generally below 1 per cent in deserts and polar air.
3. Its amount increases with altitude.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
14.x: Water vapour may reach 4 per cent in warm, wet tropics and is below 1 per cent in deserts and polar air. Its amount decreases with altitude, so statement 3 is false.
14.tq: Find the reversed distribution statement; water vapour decreases rather than increases with altitude.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: water vapour reaches up to **4%** in **warm, wet tropics**.
Statement 2 correct: it is **under 1%** in **deserts and polar air**.
Statement 3 wrong: water vapour **decreases with height** (and from equator to poles).
xa: It is the **most abundant greenhouse gas** and decides **air stability**.
It absorbs insolation and keeps in Earth's heat (**blanket effect**).
CO2 and water vapour reach only about **90 km**.

14.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the role of water vapour in the atmosphere?
o: It absorbs insolation but does not affect terrestrial heat.
It absorbs terrestrial heat but has no role in atmospheric stability.
It is a permanent constituent whose concentration is uniform at all heights.
It acts as a blanket by absorbing insolation and terrestrial heat and also influences air stability.
14.x: Water vapour is variable, absorbs insolation and terrestrial heat, produces a blanket effect and influences atmospheric stability. It is not uniformly distributed.
14.tq: Choose the option that combines the several stated functions without adding an absolute claim.
xs: Water vapour acts as a **blanket**, absorbing **insolation** and **Earth's heat**, and decides **air stability** — option **(4)**.
It is a **variable** constituent: up to **4%** in tropics, **under 1%** in deserts — not uniform (option 3).
xa: It is the **most abundant greenhouse gas**.
It **decreases with height** and from **equator to poles**.
**Dust** acts as **hygroscopic nuclei** for condensation.

14.s: Which of the following is NOT a source of atmospheric dust particles mentioned in relation to atmospheric composition?
14.x: Sea salt, pollen and meteor dust are atmospheric dust sources. Water vapour is a gaseous variable constituent, not a dust particle.
14.tq: Identify the item that does not belong to the stated group of dust sources.
xs: **Water vapour** is a gas, not a dust source — option **(4)**.
Dust sources: **sea salt, soil, smoke, soot, ash, pollen, meteor dust**.
xa: Dust is concentrated in the **lower layers**.
Dust is more common in **subtropical and temperate** belts (dry winds).
Dust acts as **hygroscopic nuclei** for clouds.

14.s: Atmospheric dust particles are generally more concentrated in the lower layers and are relatively more abundant in
14.x: Dust is concentrated in the lower atmospheric layers and is more abundant in subtropical and temperate belts, where dry winds help raise and transport particles.
14.tq: Use the distribution comparison rather than the extreme option involving only one belt.
xs: Dust is more abundant in **subtropical and temperate** belts — option **(3)**.
**Dry winds** there lift and carry it; **equatorial and polar** belts have less (option 2).
Dust is concentrated in the **lower layers**, not the thermosphere.
xa: Dust sources: **sea salt, soil, smoke, soot, ash, pollen, meteor dust**.
It acts as **hygroscopic nuclei** for condensation.
Water vapour is **under 1%** in deserts and polar air.

14.s: Dust particles help in cloud formation because they
o: act as hygroscopic nuclei for condensation
14.x: Dust particles serve as hygroscopic nuclei around which water vapour can condense, assisting cloud formation.
14.tq: Link the atmospheric constituent with its specific process-based function.
xs: Dust particles **act as hygroscopic nuclei for condensation** — option **(2)**.
Water vapour condenses around them, forming **clouds**.
xa: Dust is concentrated in the **lower layers**.
More dust in **subtropical and temperate** belts.
Sources include **sea salt** and **meteor dust**.

14.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Carbon dioxide is transparent to incoming sunlight but absorbs outgoing terrestrial radiation.
2. Carbon dioxide and water vapour are found only up to about 90 km.
3. Oxygen becomes negligible by about 90 km.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
14.x: Statement 1 is correct: CO2 lets in sunlight but absorbs outgoing terrestrial radiation. Statement 2 is correct: CO2 and water vapour reach only about 90 km. Statement 3 is wrong: oxygen becomes negligible only by about 120 km. Hence 1 and 2 only.
14.tq: 90 km for CO2 and vapour; 120 km for oxygen.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **CO2** is transparent to **incoming sunlight** but absorbs **outgoing terrestrial radiation**.
Statement 2 correct: **CO2 and water vapour** reach only about **90 km**.
Statement 3 wrong: **oxygen** becomes negligible only by **120 km**.
xa: The **homosphere** extends to **~80-90 km**.
CO2 rose to **423.9 ppm** in **2024**.
Greenhouse effect: atmosphere **transparent to incoming** solar radiation, **opaque to outgoing** terrestrial radiation.

14.s: Which one of the following gives the correct descending order of the permanent gases of the atmosphere by volume?
14.x: Nitrogen (about 78.08%) > oxygen (20.95%) > argon (0.93%) > carbon dioxide (about 0.04%) (APPSC-G1 2023). Putting oxygen first, or CO2 above argon, or argon above oxygen are all wrong orders.
14.tq: N2 78 > O2 21 > Ar 0.93 > CO2 0.04 - argon beats CO2.
xs: **Nitrogen > Oxygen > Argon > Carbon dioxide** — option **(1)** (APPSC-G1 **2023**).
⚠ Option (3) puts CO2 above argon — the common trap.
xa: Nitrogen ~**78%** was asked in APPSC-GS **2025**.
Trace gases: **neon 0.002**, **krypton 0.001**, **helium 0.0005**.
**Xenon** and **hydrogen** occur only in traces.

14.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the homosphere and heterosphere:
1. The homosphere extends from the surface to approximately 80–90 km.
2. The gases of the homosphere are relatively evenly mixed.
3. The heterosphere lies above approximately 80–90 km and contains gases arranged according to molecular weight.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
14.x: All three statements are correct. The homosphere has a relatively uniform mixture, while the heterosphere has gases arranged in layers by molecular weight.
14.tq: Test the height, composition and contrast together before choosing the complete code.
xs: All three — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct — option **(4)**.
The **homosphere** runs from the surface to **~80-90 km**, with gases **evenly mixed**.
The **heterosphere** lies above **~80-90 km**, gases layered by **molecular weight**.
xa: Homosphere layers: **troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere**.
Heterosphere layers: **thermosphere and exosphere**.
Heterosphere gases upward: **N2 → O → He → H**.

14.s: Which one of the following sequences represents the principal gases of the heterosphere from lower to higher levels, according to molecular weight?
14.x: The heterosphere is described as having nitrogen, atomic oxygen, helium and hydrogen in upward order according to molecular weight.
14.tq: Arrange the gases by the stated upward molecular-weight sequence.
xs: Upward order: **nitrogen, atomic oxygen, helium, hydrogen** — option **(2)**.
In the **heterosphere** gases are layered by **molecular weight**, heaviest lowest.
Option (1) is the reverse order.
xa: The heterosphere lies above **~80-90 km**.
It holds the **thermosphere and exosphere**.
The **homosphere** below has a **uniform** mix of gases.

14.s: Which of the following atmospheric layers are included in the homosphere?
14.x: The homosphere comprises the troposphere, stratosphere and mesosphere. The thermosphere and exosphere belong to the heterosphere.
14.tq: Distinguish the two groups of sub-layers by their boundary near 80–90 km.
xs: The homosphere holds the **troposphere, stratosphere and mesosphere** — option **(4)**.
The **thermosphere and exosphere** belong to the **heterosphere**.
xa: Homosphere: surface to **~80-90 km**; gases evenly mixed.
Heterosphere gases are layered by **molecular weight**.
Composition gives this division; the five-layer division is by **temperature**.

14.s:
Consider the following statements about the troposphere:
1. Its average height is about 13 km.
2. It is about 8 km high over the poles and about 18 km over the equator.
3. Temperature in it rises with height.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
14.x: Statement 1 is correct: average height about 13 km. Statement 2 is correct: about 8 km at the poles and 18 km at the equator. Statement 3 is wrong: temperature falls with height (about 1 deg C per 165 m). Hence 1 and 2 only.
14.tq: Troposphere: thick at the hot equator, thin at the cold poles, cools upward.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: the troposphere averages **13 km**.
Statement 2 correct: about **8 km** at the poles and **18 km** at the equator.
Statement 3 wrong: temperature **falls** with height, about **1°C per 165 m**.
xa: The troposphere holds **all weather** — water vapour, dust, clouds.
Older notes give **0-10 km** for the troposphere.
It is thickest at the **equator** due to **convection currents**.

14.s: Which of the following is the correct description of the stratosphere?
o: It is the outermost layer merging directly into space
Temperature falls continuously and meteors burn up in it
Temperature rises with height and it contains the ozone layer
It contains all clouds and almost all water vapour
14.x: The stratosphere extends from the tropopause to about 50 km, has a temperature inversion and contains the ozone layer.
14.tq: Identify the layer from its defining feature rather than its position alone.
xs: In the **stratosphere** temperature **rises with height** and it holds the **ozone layer** — option **(3)**.
The rise is an **inversion**: **ozone absorbs UV**.
Meteors burn in the **mesosphere**; clouds and water vapour are in the **troposphere**.
xa: It extends from the tropopause to **~50 km**.
Calm, stable air suits **high-altitude balloons**; jet aircraft cruise near its base.
Ozone layer in the stratosphere: APPSC **2025**.

14.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
14.x: The exosphere is extremely thin and merges into outer space; dense clouds and rainfall are features of the troposphere.
14.tq: Find the mismatched feature by locating the phenomenon in its natural layer.
xs: **Exosphere — dense clouds and rainfall** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**.
The exosphere is **extremely thin** and **merges into outer space**; clouds and rain belong to the **troposphere**.
**Mesosphere** — meteors; **troposphere** — weather; **stratosphere** — balloons: all correct.
xa: Meteors burn in the **mesosphere** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
**Aurora** and **airglow** occur in the **thermosphere (ionosphere)**.

14.s: The coldest layer of the atmosphere is generally the:
14.x: The mesosphere is the coldest layer, with temperature falling to about −100°C near 80 km.
14.tq: Use the extreme-value clue to identify the correct atmospheric layer.
xs: The **mesosphere** is the coldest layer — option **(4)**.
Temperature falls to about **-100°C** at **80 km**.
xa: Meteors **burn up** in the mesosphere (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
Its top is the **mesopause** (~**80 km**).
Tropopause temperature: **-80 °C** over the equator, **-45 °C** over the poles.

14.s:
Consider the following statements about the thermosphere:
1. Temperature rises rapidly with height in it.
2. It contains the ionosphere, where auroras occur.
3. The International Space Station orbits at about 400 km within it.
4. It is the coldest layer of the atmosphere.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
14.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: temperature rises rapidly, it holds the ionosphere and auroras, and the ISS orbits at about 400 km. Statement 4 is wrong: the mesosphere is the coldest layer (about -100 deg C at 80 km). Hence 1, 2 and 3 only.
14.tq: Coldest = mesosphere; thermosphere heats up again.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: temperature **rises rapidly** in the **thermosphere**.
Statements 2 and 3 correct: it holds the **ionosphere** (auroras); the **ISS** orbits at **~400 km**.
Statement 4 wrong: the **mesosphere** is the coldest layer (**-100°C** at 80 km).
xa: The **ionosphere reflects radio waves**.
The thermosphere's rise comes from **absorption of high-energy radiation**.
It extends to **~600 km**.

14.s:
With reference to the exosphere, consider the following statements:
1. It is the outermost atmospheric layer.
2. It extends approximately from 600 km to 10,000 km.
3. It is extremely thin and merges into outer space.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
14.x: All three statements correctly describe the exosphere, the outermost and extremely rarefied layer extending roughly from 600 to 10,000 km.
14.tq: Check whether all defining characteristics of the outermost layer are included.
xs: All three — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct — option **(4)**.
The **exosphere** is the **outermost** layer, **~600-10,000 km**.
It is **extremely thin / rarefied** and **merges into outer space**.
xa: Below it is the **thermosphere**, where temperature **rises rapidly**.
Exosphere and thermosphere make up the **heterosphere**.
The **ISS** orbits at **~400 km**, in the thermosphere.

14.s: The primary basis for dividing the atmosphere into troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere is:
14.x: These layers are identified mainly on the basis of how temperature changes with height. Composition provides the basis for the homosphere and heterosphere division.
14.tq: Distinguish the basis of thermal layering from the basis of compositional layering.
xs: The five layers are based on **how temperature changes with height** — option **(3)**.
**Composition** gives the other division — **homosphere/heterosphere** (option 1).
xa: Trend: **falls → rises → falls → rises** (troposphere to thermosphere).
**99%** of the atmosphere's mass lies within **32 km**.
Reversal layers: **stratosphere and thermosphere**.

14.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the distribution of atmospheric mass?
o: All atmospheric mass is confined to the troposphere
Nearly 99% of atmospheric mass lies within 32 km of the surface
14.x: About 99% of the atmosphere’s mass is concentrated within 32 km of the Earth’s surface.
14.tq: Check the magnitude and altitude together rather than accepting an extreme alternative.
xs: About **99%** of atmospheric mass lies within **32 km** of the surface — option **(4)**.
So it is not confined to the troposphere alone (avg **13 km**).
xa: The troposphere is **8 km** at the poles, **18 km** at the equator.
The stratosphere extends to **~50 km**.
The exosphere (**~600-10,000 km**) is extremely thin.

14.s: Which of the following sequences correctly represents the temperature trend with increasing altitude from the troposphere upward?
14.x: Temperature falls in the troposphere, rises in the stratosphere, falls in the mesosphere and rises again in the thermosphere.
14.tq: Track the alternating temperature reversals layer by layer.
xs: Temperature **falls, rises, falls, rises** — option **(1)**.
**Falls** in the troposphere; **rises** in the stratosphere (ozone absorbs UV).
**Falls** in the mesosphere; **rises** in the thermosphere (high-energy radiation).
xa: Reversal (inversion) layers: **stratosphere and thermosphere**.
Coldest point: about **-100°C** at **80 km**.
Normal lapse rate: **1 °C per 165 m**.

14.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Temperature rises in the stratosphere because ozone absorbs ultraviolet radiation.
2. Temperature falls in the mesosphere.
3. Temperature rises in the thermosphere because high-energy radiation is absorbed there.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
14.x: All three statements are correct. The stratospheric and thermospheric temperature increases are inversion trends caused by absorption of radiation, while temperature falls through the mesosphere.
14.tq: Separate each layer-specific cause from the overall alternating temperature pattern.
xs: All three — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1 correct: temperature **rises** in the stratosphere as **ozone absorbs UV** (an inversion).
Statement 2 correct: it **falls** in the **mesosphere**.
Statement 3 correct: it **rises** in the **thermosphere** by absorbing **high-energy radiation**.
xa: Reversal layers: **stratosphere and thermosphere**.
The mesosphere is the coldest layer (**-100°C**).
Troposphere lapse rate: **6.5°C/km**.

14.s: Which pair of atmospheric layers represents the principal temperature-inversion or reversal layers?
14.x: The stratosphere and thermosphere are reversal layers in which temperature increases with height, unlike the normal decrease in the troposphere and mesosphere.
14.tq: Distinguish layers with a temperature rise from those with the normal temperature fall.
xs: The reversal layers are the **stratosphere and thermosphere** — option **(1)**.
In both, temperature **rises with height**.
In the **troposphere** and **mesosphere** it falls.
xa: Stratosphere: **ozone absorbs UV**.
Thermosphere: **absorption of high-energy radiation**.
The thermosphere holds the **ionosphere**.

14.s: The normal rate of decrease of temperature in the troposphere is approximately:
14.x: In the troposphere, temperature falls by approximately 1°C for every 165 metres, or about 6.5°C per kilometre.
14.tq: Separate the standard lapse-rate figures by checking their units.
xs: The normal lapse rate is **1°C per 165 m** — option **(2)**.
That equals **6.5 °C per km**; option (3) mixes the two figures.
xa: The troposphere is thickest at the **equator** — **convection currents** lift heat higher.
Troposphere: avg **13 km**.
The tropopause caps **weather and vertical mixing**.

14.s: The tropopause is situated at approximately what height over the equator and the poles, respectively?
14.x: The tropopause is about 18 km high over the equator and about 8 km high over the poles.
14.tq: Discriminate between the equatorial and polar values by checking their order.
xs: The tropopause is about **18 km** over the equator and **8 km** over the poles — option **(3)**.
Option (4) reverses them.
It is **higher in summer** than in winter.
xa: ⚠ The tropopause is **higher and colder** over the equator (**-80 °C**) than the poles (**-45 °C**).
Stratopause **~50 km**; mesopause **~80 km**.
It caps the **weather** of the troposphere.

14.s: Why is the tropopause higher over the equator than over the poles?
o: The equator has no vertical mixing in the troposphere.
The tropopause is fixed at the same height everywhere, but appears higher at the equator.
Strong equatorial heating produces convection that carries heat higher.
The poles receive stronger solar heating and greater convection.
14.x: Strong heating at the equator generates powerful convection currents that carry heat upward, making the tropopause higher there.
14.tq: Connect the height difference with its stated cause instead of relying on a location-only fact.
xs: **Strong equatorial heating** drives **convection currents** that lift heat higher — option **(3)**.
So the troposphere is **thickest at the equator** and thinnest at the poles.
xa: Tropopause: **~18 km** at the equator, **~8 km** at the poles.
It is higher in **summer** than in winter.
Tropopause temperature: **-80 °C** over the equator.

14.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
14.x: The mesopause is situated at approximately 80 km. The stratopause is around 50 km, while the tropopause varies from about 8 km to 18 km.
14.tq: Start from the sure height-layer pair and reject the swapped boundary values.
xs: **Mesopause — ~80 km** is correct — option **(3)**.
The **stratopause** is at **~50 km** — options (1) and (2) mix these up.
The **tropopause** is at **8-18 km**, not 50 or 120 km.
xa: The mesosphere falls to **-100°C** at **80 km**.
**Oxygen** is negligible by **120 km**.
Above **~80-90 km** begins the **heterosphere**.

14.s: Which of the following statements about the tropopause is correct?
o: Its temperature is approximately -80°C over the equator and -45°C over the poles.
It promotes unrestricted vertical mixing of weather throughout the stratosphere.
It is lower in summer than in winter at all locations.
It is the boundary between the stratosphere and mesosphere.
14.x: The temperature at the tropopause is about -80°C over the equator and -45°C over the poles. It separates the troposphere from the stratosphere and caps weather and vertical mixing in the troposphere.
14.tq: Use the precise temperature comparison and reject boundary or function reversals.
xs: Tropopause temperature: **-80°C** over the equator, **-45°C** over the poles — option **(1)**.
It **caps** weather and vertical mixing — option (2) wrong.
It is **higher in summer** — option (3) wrong; it separates **troposphere and stratosphere** — option (4) wrong.
xa: ⚠ Tropopause is **higher and colder** over the equator.
Height: **~8 km** poles, **~18 km** equator.
**Mesopause** (~**80 km**) tops the mesosphere.

14.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the ionosphere is correct?
o: It prevents auroras by absorbing all charged particles.
It consists exclusively of neutral gases and contains no ions.
It reflects radio waves back to Earth, enabling long-distance communication.
It extends only up to 150 km and is inactive at night.
14.x: The ionosphere contains charged particles that reflect radio waves back to Earth, making long-distance communication possible. It also contributes to auroras and airglow.
14.tq: Identify the functional statement and reject absolute claims about the ionosphere.
xs: The ionosphere **reflects radio waves** back to Earth, enabling **long-distance communication** — option **(3)**.
It is made by **UV and X-rays** stripping electrons — so it is full of **ions** (option 2 wrong).
Its charged particles produce **auroras and airglow** (option 1 wrong).
xa: Extent: about **60 km to over 1,000 km**.
It **expands by day, shrinks at night**.
**Solar flares** and **geomagnetic storms** disrupt **GNSS** signals.

14.s: The ionosphere generally
o: expands during the day and contracts at night
remains unchanged between day and night
contracts during the day and expands at night
14.x: Solar radiation causes the ionosphere to expand during the day, while it contracts at night.
14.tq: Directly distinguish the day-night reversal in the behaviour of the ionosphere.
xs: The ionosphere **expands by day** and **shrinks at night** — option **(1)**.
It forms when solar **UV and X-rays** strip electrons from atoms.
