1: the main belt is the **Gudur-Nellore mica belt**. 2: **muscovite** white, **phlogopite** amber, **biotite** black.
3: mica was declared a **minor mineral in 2015**.
4 is wrong: AP is **first** (**70.2%** production); **Rajasthan** is second.
xa: AP also has the largest mica reserves (**40.5%**).
Nellore has bulk black-spotted **"electrical mica"**.
Jharkhand mica areas: **Koderma, Hazaribagh**; some notes still call Jharkhand the largest producer.
Minor minerals are regulated by **states**.

53.s: The Jaipur–Udaipur mica belt is associated with which State?
53.x: Rajasthan has the Jaipur–Udaipur mica belt and ranks second in the stated comparison. Jharkhand includes the Koderma and Hazaribagh mica areas.
53.tq: Belt–State matching.
xs: The **Jaipur-Udaipur** mica belt is in **Rajasthan** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Rajasthan ranks **2nd** in mica after AP.
**Jharkhand**'s mica areas are **Koderma and Hazaribagh**; AP's belt is **Gudur-Nellore**.
xa: AP leads mica: reserves **40.5%**, production **70.2%**.
Some notes still call **Jharkhand** the largest producer.
Mica was declared a **minor mineral in 2015**.

53.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh is famous for mica blocks used in the electronics industry?
53.x: Nellore, with the Gudur mica belt, is famous for mica blocks used in electronics (APPSC 2025 key). Visakhapatnam is linked with bauxite and manganese, Anantapur with gold and iron ore, and Kurnool with limestone and gold.
53.tq: Mica = Gudur-Nellore; AP 40.5% reserves, 70.2% production.
xs: **Nellore** (Gudur belt) is famous for **mica blocks used in electronics** (APPSC 2025 key) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Visakhapatnam** is linked with bauxite and manganese, **Anantapur** with gold and iron ore, **Kurnool** with limestone and gold.
xa: Nellore has bulk black-spotted **"electrical mica"**.
The **Nellore mica schist belt** lies in **Dharwar** rocks.
**Vermiculite** occurs in **Nellore** and Chittoor.
APPSC 2023 match pair: **Mica — Nellore**.

53.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Swarnagiri Gold Mine?
o: It is located in Gudur and produces mica as its principal mineral.
It is located in Ramagiri and operated by a public-sector company.
It is operated by APMDC under a five-year lease.
It is operated by GeoMysore Services under a 30-year lease.
53.x: The Swarnagiri mine is operated by GeoMysore Services under a 30-year lease and is located in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district.
53.tq: Who-operates-what trap.
xs: Swarnagiri is run by **GeoMysore Services** on a **30-year lease** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is in **Tuggali mandal, Kurnool** — not Gudur (mica) or Ramagiri — and it is a **private** gold mine, not APMDC's.
xa: Renamed from **Jonnagiri** by **G.O. Ms. No. 181**; area **597.820 ha**; **open-pit**.
Output ~**1,000 kg gold a year**; bars branded **"Made in Jonnagiri"**.
It is **India's first private-sector gold mine after Independence** (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
⚠ India's **oldest** gold field is **Kolar**, Karnataka.

53.s: Commercial production from the Swarnagiri Gold Mine began in approximately:
53.x: Commercial production began in late June 2026. The mine is projected to produce about 1,000 kg of gold annually.
53.tq: Year-based factual recall with close distractors.
xs: Commercial production at Swarnagiri began in **late June 2026** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Some notes say **July 2026**; the 2024 and 2025 dates are too early.
xa: Expected output: ~**1,000 kg gold a year**, branded **"Made in Jonnagiri"**.
Operator **GeoMysore Services**, **30-year lease**, open-pit, **597.820 ha**.
Location: **Tuggali mandal, Kurnool**.
Six **Javakula** blocks (Anantapur) are under G2-level exploration after two failed auctions.

53.s: The first private gold mine after Independence in Andhra Pradesh is associated with:
53.x: Jonnagiri, also referred to as Swarnagiri, in Kurnool is identified as the first private gold mine after Independence.
53.tq: Distinguish the gold-mining location from Andhra Pradesh’s better-known barytes, uranium and granite areas.
xs: The first private gold mine after Independence is **Jonnagiri / Swarnagiri** in **Kurnool** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Araku** is bauxite, **Tummalapalle** is uranium and **Chimakurthy** is black granite.
xa: It is India's **first and largest private gold mine**.
Renamed by **G.O. Ms. No. 181**; in **Tuggali mandal**.
Operator **GeoMysore Services**, **30-year lease**.
⚠ India's oldest gold field = **Kolar**, Karnataka.

53.s: India's first private-sector gold mine (2026) is in which State?
53.x: India's first private-sector gold mine is at Jonnagiri (Kurnool), Andhra Pradesh. Karnataka's Kolar is the oldest gold field.
53.tq: Distinguish the first private-sector mine from the oldest and best-known producing State.
xs: India's first private-sector gold mine is at **Jonnagiri (Swarnagiri), Kurnool** in **Andhra Pradesh** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Karnataka**'s **Kolar** is India's **oldest** gold field — a different FIRST.
xa: The mine opened in **Jun-Jul 2026**; ~**1,000 kg** gold a year.
Other AP gold: **Ramagiri** (Anantapur), Tuggali (Kurnool), Chittoor.
Next gold auctions: **Boksampalli, Javakula, Chigurugunta, Ramagiri**.

53.s: Which one of the following correctly describes uranium resources in Andhra Pradesh?
o: They are concentrated at Mangampeta and the ore is high-grade.
They are concentrated at Tummalapalle and the ore is low-grade.
They are concentrated at Chimakurthy and the ore is coal-associated.
They are concentrated at Ramagiri and the ore is exclusively placer-type.
53.x: Tummalapalle is the principal uranium locality mentioned for Andhra Pradesh, and its uranium ore is described as low-grade.
53.tq: Combine the locality and ore-quality clues to identify the complete description.
xs: AP's uranium is at **Tummalapalle** and its ore is **low-grade** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Mangampeta** is barytes, **Chimakurthy** is black granite and **Ramagiri** is gold.
xa: Tummalapalle is in **YSR Kadapa**, within the **Cuddapah** basin.
Indian uranium ore in general is **low-grade**.
Other uranium mines: **Jaduguda, Narwapahar** (Jharkhand).
⚠ Kadapa holds both **barytes (Mangampeta)** and **uranium (Tummalapalle)**.

53.s: Tummalapalle uranium mine is located in:
o: Kurnool district, in the Kurnool Group
Srikakulam district, in the coastal sands
Nellore district, in the Dharwar belt
YSR Kadapa district, in the Cuddapah basin
53.x: Tummalapalle is located in YSR Kadapa district within the Cuddapah basin. The Indian uranium ore there is low-grade.
53.tq: Mine–district–geological basin identification.
xs: **Tummalapalle** is in **YSR Kadapa district, in the Cuddapah basin** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Kurnool Group** has no metallic minerals; Srikakulam is **beach sands**; Nellore's Dharwar belt is **mica**.
xa: Its uranium ore is **low-grade**.
The Cuddapah formation is **Proterozoic** (~**1.6** bn yrs) and also holds **barytes**.
Jharkhand uranium mines: **Jaduguda, Narwapahar**.
Meghalaya Assembly opposed **uranium mining** (Aug **2026**).

53.s: Which of the following pairs of uranium mines is located in Jharkhand?
53.x: Jaduguda and Narwapahar are uranium mines in Jharkhand. Tummalapalle is in YSR Kadapa district of Andhra Pradesh.
53.tq: Use the sure mine–State pair.
xs: **Jaduguda and Narwapahar** are uranium mines in **Jharkhand** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Tummalapalle** (uranium) and **Ramagiri** (gold) are in AP; **Jonnagiri** is gold, **Mangampeta** barytes.
**Gudur** is mica and **Bhavanapadu** is beach sand minerals.
xa: AP's uranium mine is **Tummalapalle**, YSR Kadapa, Cuddapah basin.
Indian uranium ore is **low-grade**.
Jharkhand's mica areas: **Koderma, Hazaribagh**.

53.s: Thorium used in India’s nuclear programme is obtained mainly from:
53.x: Thorium comes from monazite, which occurs with ilmenite, rutile and zircon in coastal beach sands (e.g. Srikakulam coast), so option B is right. Gondwana rocks give coal, Dharwar quartz gives gold, and Cuddapah limestone/dolomite are not thorium sources. Thorium is meant to fuel Stage III of India's nuclear programme.
53.tq: Source–use application.
xs: Thorium comes from **monazite** in the **beach sands** with **ilmenite** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Gondwana** seams give coal, **Dharwar** quartz gives gold, and **Cuddapah** limestone/dolomite is not a thorium source.
xa: Srikakulam coast beach sands: **ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet**, sillimanite, **monazite**.
AP holds ~**327 Mt** of India's **1,078 Mt** of heavy mineral beach sand (about **30.4%**).
**Bhavanapadu** (Srikakulam) is a beach-sand deposit.
Beach sands stretch from **Srikakulam to Nellore**.

53.s:
Consider the following statements about critical minerals in Andhra Pradesh:
1. NGRI reported rare earth elements in syenite rocks of Srikakulam district in 2023.
2. The Chief Minister ordered statewide mineral mapping for critical minerals, with value addition through APMDC.
3. Titanium, lithium and gallium are the focus minerals of this mapping.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
53.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the REEs were found in syenite rocks of Anantapur district, not Srikakulam (Srikakulam is known for beach sands). Statement 2 is correct: statewide mapping for critical minerals with value addition via APMDC (2026). Statement 3 is correct: focus minerals are titanium, lithium and gallium. So 2 and 3 only; options containing statement 1 are wrong.
53.tq: REE in syenite = Anantapur; beach sands = Srikakulam coast. Don't mix them.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
1 is wrong: NGRI found **REEs in syenite rocks of Anantapur** district (**2023**), not Srikakulam.
2 is correct: the CM ordered statewide **mineral mapping** for critical minerals with value addition via **APMDC** (**2026**).
3 is correct: focus minerals are **titanium, lithium and gallium**.
xa: **Srikakulam** is known for beach sands (ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet, monazite).
AP's slogan shift: **"from mineral wealth to manufacturing"**.
Policy also backs beneficiation of **low-grade iron ore** and **CDW-grade barytes**.

53.s: Which one of the following sets contains only granite varieties or granite localities associated with Andhra Pradesh?
o: Galaxy/black granite–Chimakurthy; Srikakulam Blue; Pista Green–Kadapa; Chilli Red–Anantapur
Galaxy/black granite–Ramagiri; Srikakulam Blue–Kondapalli; Pista Green–Guntur; Chilli Red–Nellore
Galaxy/black granite–Mangampeta; Srikakulam Blue–Tuggali; Pista Green–Krishna; Chilli Red–Kurnool
Galaxy/black granite–Tummalapalle; Srikakulam Blue–Gudur; Pista Green–Vizianagaram; Chilli Red–Bapatla
53.x: Chimakurthy is known for Galaxy or black granite, while Srikakulam Blue, Pista Green of Kadapa and Chilli Red of Anantapur are other noted granite varieties or localities.
53.tq: Match each distinctive granite name with its stated locality.
xs: Option **(1)** is correct: **Galaxy/black granite — Chimakurthy**, **Srikakulam Blue**, **Pista Green — Kadapa**, **Chilli Red — Anantapur**.
The other sets use mineral places: **Ramagiri** and **Tuggali** (gold), **Mangampeta** (barytes), **Tummalapalle** (uranium), **Gudur** (mica), **Kondapalli** (chromite).
xa: Chimakurthy is in **Prakasam** (Ongole belt).
**Kashmir White / River White** — Visakhapatnam; **Chocolate Brown** — Kurnool.
**Slate** — Prakasam; **Vermiculite** — Nellore, Chittoor.

53.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Black Galaxy or black granite — Chimakurthy, Prakasam
2. Srikakulam Blue — Srikakulam
3. Kashmir White or River White — Visakhapatnam
4. Slate — Nellore

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
53.x: Black Galaxy is found in the Chimakurthy–Prakasam or Ongole belt, Srikakulam Blue in Srikakulam and Kashmir White or River White in Visakhapatnam. Slate is associated with Prakasam, not Nellore.
53.tq: Find the one wrong district association before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Black Galaxy — Chimakurthy, Prakasam** (Ongole belt); **Srikakulam Blue — Srikakulam**; **Kashmir White / River White — Visakhapatnam**.
Pair 4 is wrong: **Slate** comes from **Prakasam**, not Nellore.
xa: Nellore is linked with **vermiculite** (with Chittoor) and **mica**.
**Pista Green** — YSR Kadapa; **Chilli Red** — Anantapur; **Chocolate Brown** — Kurnool.
**Steatite** (soapstone) comes from the Cuddapah system, Kadapa.

53.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Stone or mineral)

a. Chilli Red
b. Chocolate Brown
c. Vermiculite
d. Steatite

List-II (District or geological system)

i. Cuddapah system, Kadapa
ii. Anantapur
 iii. Nellore and Chittoor
iv. Kurnool

Codes:
53.x: Chilli Red is associated with Anantapur, Chocolate Brown with Kurnool, Vermiculite with Nellore and Chittoor, and Steatite with the Cuddapah system of Kadapa.
53.tq: Use the distinctive mineral–district pair first and then complete the remaining matches.
xs: The correct match is **a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Chilli Red — Anantapur**; **Chocolate Brown — Kurnool**.
**Vermiculite — Nellore and Chittoor**; **Steatite** (soapstone) **— Cuddapah system, Kadapa**.
xa: **Pista Green** — YSR Kadapa; **Srikakulam Blue** — Srikakulam.
**Sandstone** — Kurnool and Kadapa basins.
Black Galaxy granite — **Chimakurthy, Prakasam**.

53.s: With reference to the regulation of minerals in India, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Minor minerals such as building stone, gravel, clay and sand are regulated by the States, while major minerals listed in the First Schedule of the MMDR Act, 1957 are under the Centre.
All minerals, major and minor, are regulated exclusively by the States.
Major minerals are regulated by the States under the Mines Act, 1952, while minor minerals are under the Centre.
Minor minerals are listed in the First Schedule of the MMDR Act, 1957 and regulated by the Centre.
53.x: Minor minerals (building stone, gravel, clay, sand) are regulated by the States; major minerals in the First Schedule of the MMDR Act, 1957 come under the Centre. The other options reverse or merge this division, and the Mines Act, 1952 is not the basis named.
53.tq: MMDR Act 1957: First Schedule majors = Centre; minors = States.
xs: **Minor minerals** (building stone, gravel, clay, sand) are regulated by the **States**; **major minerals** in the **First Schedule of the MMDR Act, 1957** are under the **Centre** — option **(1)**.
Options 2, 3 and 4 merge or reverse this division between States and Centre.
xa: **Mica** was declared a **minor mineral in 2015**.
Granites like **Black Galaxy** (Chimakurthy) are among AP's dimension stones.
AP is a leading producer of **barytes, limestone, mica, granite**.

53.s:
Which of the following areas are covered by the Krishna-Godavari basin in the context of Andhra Pradesh?
1. Kakinada offshore
2. Amalapuram/Konaseema
3. Krishna offshore
4. Barmer-Sanchore
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
53.x: Kakinada offshore, Amalapuram/Konaseema and Krishna offshore are associated with the KG basin. Barmer-Sanchore belongs to Rajasthan, not the KG basin.
53.tq: Use the wrong-location trap to exclude a petroleum basin from another State.
xs: **Kakinada offshore, Amalapuram/Konaseema and Krishna offshore** are in the **KG basin** — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Barmer-Sanchore** is not part of the KG basin.
xa: The **KG basin** is AP's gas basin (APPSC 2025 key).
**KG-D6** deepwater block: **Reliance Industries** with **BP**.
**Ravva** (shallow offshore): **Cairn-ONGC** JV; onshore KG fields: **ONGC**.
**Tatipaka**: ONGC mini-refinery, Konaseema.

53.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. KG-D6 — Reliance Industries with BP
2. Ravva — Cairn-ONGC joint venture
3. Deendayal block — GSPC, later taken over by ONGC
4. Tatipaka — ONGC mini-refinery
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
53.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. KG-D6 is operated by Reliance Industries with BP, Ravva is associated with the Cairn-ONGC joint venture, the Deendayal block was associated with GSPC and later ONGC, and Tatipaka has an ONGC mini-refinery.
53.tq: Check operator, field type and facility together because the entities are easily confused.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**KG-D6** — Reliance with **BP**; **Ravva** — **Cairn-ONGC** JV.
**Deendayal** block — **GSPC**, later **ONGC**; **Tatipaka** — **ONGC mini-refinery**, Konaseema.
xa: Onshore KG fields are run by **ONGC**.
AP's main refinery: HPCL's **Visakhapatnam** refinery.
KG basin covers **Kakinada offshore, Amalapuram/Konaseema, Krishna offshore**.

53.s: Which one of the following is the principal refinery of Andhra Pradesh mentioned in relation to the State's petroleum infrastructure?
53.x: HPCL's Visakhapatnam refinery is Andhra Pradesh's main refinery. Tatipaka is an ONGC mini-refinery in Konaseema.
53.tq: Separate a principal refinery from a mini-refinery and oilfield operators.
xs: AP's main refinery is HPCL's **Visakhapatnam refinery** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Tatipaka** is only an **ONGC mini-refinery** (Konaseema); **Ravva** is an oil field (Cairn-ONGC); GSPC held the **Deendayal** block.
xa: The **KG basin** is AP's gas basin (APPSC 2025 key).
Reliance plans **underground coal-gasification** near Recherla and Chintalapudi, **Eluru district**.
**KG-D6**: Reliance Industries with BP.

53.s: The national natural-gas energy-mix target mentioned for 2030 is an increase from approximately 6.7% to:
53.x: Natural gas is targeted to rise from approximately 6.7% to 15% of the energy mix by 2030.
53.tq: Retain both the baseline and target percentage and select the stated target figure.
xs: Natural gas in the energy mix is to rise from **~6.7% to 15%** by **2030** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The 10%, 12% and 20% figures are not the stated target.
xa: India's gas basins: **Mumbai Offshore, KG, Assam, Cambay**.
**One Nation One Gas Grid**; pipeline target over **32,000 km**.
**JHBDPL** = Pradhan Mantri **Urja Ganga** pipeline.

53.s:
Which of the following are identified as major natural-gas basins in India?
1. Mumbai Offshore
2. Krishna-Godavari
3. Assam
4. Cambay
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
53.x: Mumbai Offshore, Krishna-Godavari, Assam and Cambay are all identified as major natural-gas basins in India.
53.tq: Treat a complete named list as a set and test whether any entry has been wrongly inserted.
xs: **Mumbai Offshore, Krishna-Godavari, Assam and Cambay** are all listed gas basins — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
The **KG basin** is AP's gas basin (APPSC 2025 key).
xa: KG covers **Kakinada offshore, Amalapuram/Konaseema, Krishna offshore**.
Gas target: **~6.7% → 15%** of the energy mix by **2030**.
**JHBDPL** (Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga) is part of **One Nation One Gas Grid**.

53.s: The pipeline initiative associated with the Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga project is:
53.x: JHBDPL is associated with the Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga gas-pipeline project. KG-D6 and Ravva are petroleum fields or blocks, not the pipeline initiative.
53.tq: Distinguish the pipeline acronym from field and block names.
xs: **JHBDPL** is the **Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga** pipeline — so option **(4)** is correct.
**KG-D6** and **Ravva** are oil and gas blocks/fields, not pipelines.
xa: It is part of the **One Nation One Gas Grid**.
National pipeline target: over **32,000 km**.
Gas share target: **~6.7% → 15%** by **2030**.

53.s: A proposed underground coal-gasification project near Recherla and Chintalapudi is associated with which district?
53.x: The proposed project near Recherla and Chintalapudi is in Eluru district. It is intended to produce gas, hydrogen, ammonia and urea.
53.tq: Link the project locations to the district rather than to the nearby mineral-producing districts.
xs: The coal-gasification project near **Recherla and Chintalapudi** is in **Eluru** district — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is Reliance's **underground coal-gasification** plan for gas, **hydrogen, ammonia and urea**.
xa: Investment: over **Rs 2 lakh crore** (Aug **2026**).
AP's coal lies in **Gondwana** rocks of the **Godavari valley**; APPSC 2023 key: **Coal — West Godavari**.
**YSR Kadapa** is linked with barytes and uranium, **Anantapur** with gold and iron ore.

53.s:
Consider the following statements about the drainage basins of Andhra Pradesh:

1. The Godavari, Krishna and Pennar are major river basins of the State.
2. Vamsadhara and Nagavali are important basins in northern Andhra Pradesh.
3. The State has no major river basin apart from the Krishna and Godavari.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
53.x: Godavari, Krishna and Pennar are the major basins, while Vamsadhara and Nagavali occur in the north. Statement 3 is false because it excludes the Pennar and northern basins.
53.tq: Reject the absolute exclusion in statement 3 and retain the listed basin groups.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
1: **Godavari, Krishna and Pennar** are AP's major basins. 2: **Vamsadhara and Nagavali** lie in the north.
3 is wrong: it leaves out the **Pennar** and the northern basins.
xa: **Tanks** are the traditional source in **Rayalaseema** and the north coast.
AP's coastline is **974 km** (2024-25), 2nd after **Gujarat**.
Forest cover: **30,084.96 sq km = 23.59%** of the state.

53.s: In which parts of Andhra Pradesh are tanks traditionally an important source of water?
o: Rayalaseema and the Krishna-Godavari deltas only
Only in the coastal deltaic districts
Only in the Visakhapatnam Agency area
53.x: Tanks are the traditional source of water in Rayalaseema and the north coast of Andhra Pradesh.
53.tq: Test the regional comparison directly rather than confusing traditional tanks with river basins.
xs: **Tanks** are the traditional water source in **Rayalaseema and the north coast** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The deltas, coastal districts or Agency areas alone are not the stated tank regions.
xa: Major basins: **Godavari, Krishna, Pennar**; **Vamsadhara, Nagavali** in the north.
Red sanders is endemic to the **Seshachalam**-Palakonda-Lankamalla hills of Rayalaseema.
Gold-bearing quartz occurs in **Rayalaseema** (Anantapur, Chittoor, Kurnool).

53.s: The planned port-based mineral beneficiation plants in Andhra Pradesh are associated primarily with which resource setting?
o: The coastal region and its port network
The inland tank systems of Rayalaseema
The deltaic forests of the Godavari basin alone
53.x: Andhra Pradesh plans port-based mineral beneficiation plants, linking mineral processing with the State’s coastal and port infrastructure.
53.tq: Identify the location implied by the port-based industrial activity.
xs: Port-based mineral beneficiation plants are tied to the **coastal region and its port network** — so option **(2)** is correct.
AP's marine resources include a **974 km** coastline, 2nd after **Gujarat**.
xa: AP plans **port-based mineral processing** along the coast and **manganese clusters** in Vizianagaram.
Policy backs beneficiation of **low-grade iron ore** and **CDW-grade barytes**.
Beach sand minerals run along the **Srikakulam** coast.

53.s: With a coastline of about 974 km (2024-25), Andhra Pradesh ranks where among Indian States in coastline length?
o: Third, after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu
53.x: Andhra Pradesh's coastline of 974 km (2024-25) is the second longest in India, after Gujarat. It is not the first, and Tamil Nadu does not rank above it.
53.tq: AP coast 974 km = 2nd after Gujarat.
xs: AP's **974 km** coastline (2024-25) is **second, after Gujarat** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is not first, and **Tamil Nadu** is not ranked above it.
xa: AP plans **port-based mineral beneficiation plants**.
Coastal sands run from **Srikakulam to Nellore**.
The **KG basin** covers Kakinada offshore, Konaseema and Krishna offshore.
Forest cover: **23.59%** of the state.

53.s: The forest cover of Andhra Pradesh is approximately:
o: 30,084.96 sq km, constituting 23.59% of the State
40,084.96 sq km, constituting 23.95% of the State
20,084.96 sq km, constituting 13.59% of the State
30,804.96 sq km, constituting 32.59% of the State
53.x: Andhra Pradesh has 30,084.96 sq km of forest cover, which accounts for 23.59% of the State’s area.
53.tq: Compare both the area and percentage carefully; the distractors alter one digit or reverse the figures.
xs: AP's forest cover is **30,084.96 sq km**, i.e. **23.59%** of the State — so option **(1)** is correct.
The other options change the area or the percentage.
xa: **6.13 crore** seedlings were planted in **2025-26**.
**Red sanders** (Pterocarpus santalinus) is endemic to the **Seshachalam**-Palakonda-Lankamalla hills.
**GCC** (Girijan Cooperative Corporation), Visakhapatnam, buys minor forest produce from tribals.
AP's coastline is **974 km** (2024-25), 2nd after **Gujarat**.

53.s: Red sanders, scientifically known as Pterocarpus santalinus, is endemic to which group of hills?
53.x: Red sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) is endemic to the Seshachalam, Palakonda and Lankamalla hills of Rayalaseema.
53.tq: Use the exact species–habitat association and avoid substituting other hill groups of Andhra Pradesh.
xs: **Red sanders** (Pterocarpus santalinus) is endemic to the **Seshachalam–Palakonda–Lankamalla hills** — so option **(4)** is correct.
These hills lie in **Rayalaseema**.
xa: AP's forest cover: **30,084.96 sq km = 23.59%** of the State.
**6.13 crore** seedlings were planted in **2025-26**.
**Tanks** are the traditional water source in Rayalaseema and the north coast.

53.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the role of the Girijan Cooperative Corporation (GCC) of Andhra Pradesh?
o: It manages only bamboo plantations owned by the State.
It purchases major minerals from mining companies at export prices.
It purchases minor forest produce from tribals at fair prices.
It regulates fishing harbours along the coast.
53.x: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation, headquartered at Visakhapatnam, buys minor forest produce from tribals at fair prices.
53.tq: Identify the institutional function rather than confusing GCC with a mining, fisheries or plantation agency.
xs: The **Girijan Cooperative Corporation** buys **minor forest produce from tribals at fair prices** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is based at **Visakhapatnam**; it does not buy minerals or regulate fishing harbours.
xa: Produce bought: **tamarind, honey, gum karaya, adda leaves**.
**Bauxite mining** in the Visakhapatnam Agency (Araku) raises **PVTG/tribal rights**, FCA and FRA issues.
Forest cover: **23.59%** of the State.

53.s:
Match the deposit with its mineral:
A. Mangampet  B. Tummalapalle  C. Gudur  D. Bhavanapadu
1. Mica  2. Beach sand minerals  3. Barytes  4. Uranium
53.x: Mangampet (YSR Kadapa) = barytes; Tummalapalle (YSR Kadapa) = uranium; Gudur (Nellore) = mica; Bhavanapadu (Srikakulam) = beach sand minerals. The other codes swap mica and beach sands or barytes and uranium.
53.tq: Two Kadapa deposits: Mangampet barytes, Tummalapalle uranium.
xs: The correct match is **A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2** — option **(1)**.
**Mangampet — Barytes** (YSR Kadapa); **Tummalapalle — Uranium** (YSR Kadapa).
**Gudur — Mica** (Nellore); **Bhavanapadu — Beach sand minerals** (Srikakulam).
xa: ⚠ Kadapa holds both **barytes (Mangampeta)** and **uranium (Tummalapalle)**.
**Jonnagiri (Swarnagiri)** — gold, Kurnool (Tuggali mandal).
**Araku-Chintapalle** — bauxite, Alluri Sitharama Raju.
Beach sands: **ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet**, sillimanite; **monazite** → thorium.

53.s:
Arrange the following mineral deposits of Andhra Pradesh from the district associated with barytes to the district associated with uranium and then to the district associated with gold:
A. Jonnagiri
B. Mangampeta
C. Tummalapalle
53.x: Mangampeta is the barytes deposit in YSR Kadapa, Tummalapalle is the uranium mine in YSR Kadapa, and Jonnagiri is the gold mine in Kurnool. Thus the sequence is B, C, A.
53.tq: Order the listed sites by the mineral specified in the stem.
xs: The order is **B, C, A** — option **(1)**.
**Mangampeta** = barytes (YSR Kadapa); **Tummalapalle** = uranium (YSR Kadapa); **Jonnagiri** = gold (Kurnool).
xa: AP produces nearly **a quarter of world barytes**.
Tummalapalle lies in the **Cuddapah basin**; its ore is **low-grade**.
Jonnagiri, renamed **Swarnagiri**, is India's first private-sector gold mine after Independence.
Other gold: **Ramagiri** (Anantapur), Chittoor.

53.s: The Gudur belt of Nellore is particularly associated with which mineral?
53.x: The Gudur belt in Nellore is an important mica-bearing area and supplies mica blocks used in electronics.
53.tq: Test the specific belt–mineral association rather than the district alone.
xs: The **Gudur** belt of **Nellore** is AP's **mica** belt — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Barytes** is Mangampeta, **gold** Ramagiri/Jonnagiri, **chromite** Kondapalli hills.
xa: Nellore mica blocks are used in **electronics** (APPSC 2025 key).
AP has the largest mica reserves (**40.5%**) and production (**70.2%**).
Mica ores: **muscovite** (white), **phlogopite** (amber), **biotite** (black).
Mica became a **minor mineral in 2015**.

53.s: The Araku-Chintapalle bauxite deposits fall in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
53.x: The Araku-Chintapalle bauxite deposits are in Alluri Sitharama Raju district, which was carved out of the old Visakhapatnam district.
53.tq: Araku = ASR = bauxite hills.
xs: **Araku-Chintapalle** bauxite is in **Alluri Sitharama Raju** district (old Visakhapatnam) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**YSR Kadapa** is barytes and uranium; **Srikakulam** is beach sands.
xa: Bauxite also: **East Godavari** (APPSC 2023 key), Paderu, Anantagiri, Anakapalli.
Bauxite is hosted by **Eastern Ghats khondalites**.
AP bauxite (older data): ~**615 Mt** (~**17.7%**).
Bauxite mining in Araku raises **Eastern Ghats ecology** and **PVTG** rights issues.

53.s: Which of the following pairs of proposed or emerging mineral-related initiatives in Andhra Pradesh is correctly matched?
o: Manganese processing clusters — Vizianagaram; port-based mineral processing — coastal region
Manganese processing clusters — Nellore; port-based mineral processing — Rayalaseema tanks
Manganese processing clusters — Kurnool; port-based mineral processing — Himalayan region
Manganese processing clusters — Srikakulam; port-based mineral processing — inland coalfields only
53.x: Planned manganese processing clusters are associated with Vizianagaram, while port-based mineral processing is planned along the Andhra Pradesh coast.
53.tq: Match each initiative with its stated regional setting and reject shifted locations.
xs: **Manganese processing clusters — Vizianagaram** and **port-based mineral processing — coastal region** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Nellore (mica), Kurnool (limestone, gold) and inland or Himalayan areas are not the stated places.
xa: Manganese districts: **Vizianagaram**, Srikakulam.
**Visakhapatnam** was the world's **No. 1 manganese** producer until **1929**.
AP's coastline: **974 km**, 2nd after **Gujarat**.
AP's shift: **"from mineral wealth to manufacturing"**.

53.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the recent mining-related developments mentioned for Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya?
o: Andhra Pradesh opened the Swarnagiri gold mine, while the Meghalaya Assembly opposed uranium mining.
Meghalaya opened the Swarnagiri gold mine, while Andhra Pradesh opposed all uranium mining.
Both States opened private uranium mines after Independence.
Both States prohibited all forms of mineral processing.
53.x: Swarnagiri gold mine was opened in Andhra Pradesh during June–July 2026, while the Meghalaya Assembly opposed uranium mining.
53.tq: Separate the State, mineral and action in each half of the comparison.
xs: **AP** opened the **Swarnagiri gold mine** (Jun-Jul **2026**), while the **Meghalaya Assembly opposed uranium mining** (Aug **2026**) — option **(1)**.
Swarnagiri is in AP's **Kurnool**, not Meghalaya.
xa: Swarnagiri is India's **first private-sector gold mine after Independence**.
Operator **GeoMysore Services**; ~**1,000 kg** gold a year.
AP's uranium: **Tummalapalle** (low-grade ore).

53.s:
Consider the following statements regarding bauxite mining in the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh:

1. It has implications for Eastern Ghats ecology.
2. It can affect the rights of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups.
3. The debate involves the Forest Conservation Act and the Forest Rights Act.
4. It is entirely free from social and environmental controversy.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
53.x: Bauxite mining in the Eastern Ghats raises ecological concerns and issues relating to PVTG rights under the Forest Conservation Act and Forest Rights Act. Statement 4 is false because the activity is controversial.
53.tq: Reject the absolute phrase ‘entirely free’ and retain the ecological, tribal-rights and legal dimensions.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Bauxite mining in the **Visakhapatnam Agency (Araku)** is debated over **Eastern Ghats ecology**, **PVTG/tribal rights**, the **FCA** and the **FRA**.
Statement 4 is wrong: the mining is a matter of **criticism and debate**.
xa: Bauxite is hosted by **Eastern Ghats khondalites**.
Bauxite places: Araku, **Paderu**, Chintapalli, Anantagiri; **East Godavari** (APPSC 2023 key).
**GCC**, Visakhapatnam, buys minor forest produce from tribals at fair prices.

54.s: Trewartha's classification of Indian climates differs from Koeppen's classification mainly because it:
o: Rejects temperature and rainfall as climatic controls
Classifies India exclusively into polar and desert regions
Modifies Koeppen's logic and presents a simpler regional classification for India
54.x: Trewartha modified Koeppen's temperature-rainfall approach and made it simpler for application to India.
54.tq: Test the relationship between two similar classification systems.
xs: **Trewartha** modified **Koeppen's** temperature-rainfall logic into a **simpler classification for India** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It keeps temperature and rainfall as controls, so options 1 and 3 are wrong; it has five regions, not just polar and desert ones.
xa: Trewartha regions: **Am** (rainforest), **Aw** (savanna), **BS/BW** (steppe, desert), **Caw** (humid subtropical), **H** (highland).
⚠ Trewartha **Caw** = Koeppen **Cwg**; Trewartha **H** = Koeppen **Dfc/E**.
**Thornthwaite** used a moisture-based scheme instead.

54.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched under Trewartha's classification?
o: Am — tropical rainforest of the west coast and North-East
Caw — tropical savanna of the Peninsula
54.x: Under Trewartha, Am denotes tropical rainforest in the west coast and North-East. Aw covers most of the Peninsula, BS/BW the steppe and desert areas, Caw the Ganga plain and H the Himalaya.
54.tq: Reject options formed by swapping neighbouring regional categories.
xs: **Am — tropical rainforest of the west coast and North-East** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Caw** is the humid subtropical **Ganga plain**; the Peninsula savanna is **Aw**.
**H** is the **Himalayan highland**; **BS/BW** is the steppe and desert of **Rajasthan** and rain-shadow Deccan.
xa: ⚠ Trewartha **Caw** = Koeppen **Cwg**; **H** = Koeppen **Dfc/E**.
AP's Koppen type is **Aw** — tropical wet and dry (savannah).
Thornthwaite's wettest belt is the same **Western Ghats-west coast and North-East**.

54.s: The humid subtropical climate with dry winter in the Ganga plain under Trewartha corresponds broadly to which Koeppen type?
54.x: Trewartha's Caw corresponds broadly to Koeppen's Cwg for the Ganga plain, both indicating a humid subtropical or monsoonal climate with dry winter.
54.tq: Link equivalent labels across two classification systems.
xs: Trewartha's **Caw** (humid subtropical with dry winter, Ganga plain) equals Koeppen's **Cwg** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Aw** is tropical savanna (Peninsula); **Dfc** is part of the Himalayan highland (Trewartha **H**).
xa: ⚠ Trewartha **H** = Koeppen **Dfc/E**.
**BS/BW** = steppe and desert: Rajasthan, rain-shadow Deccan.
**Am** = tropical rainforest: west coast, NE.

54.s: Thornthwaite classified climates mainly using which combination?
54.x: Thornthwaite used precipitation effectiveness expressed through moisture conditions and thermal efficiency represented by potential evapotranspiration.
54.tq: Identify the classification system from its distinctive criteria.
xs: **Thornthwaite** used **precipitation effectiveness (moisture index)** and **thermal efficiency (potential evapotranspiration)** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Vegetation, pressure belts and ocean currents are not his criteria.
xa: Moisture types: **perhumid/wet (A)** → humid (B) → sub-humid (C) → semi-arid (D) → **arid (E)**.
Wettest: **Western Ghats-west coast and the North-East**; arid: **western Rajasthan (Thar)** + Kutch.
**Trewartha**, by contrast, modified **Koeppen's** temperature-rainfall logic.

54.s:
Arrange the following Thornthwaite moisture types from the wettest to the driest:
A. Semi-arid
B. Perhumid or wet
C. Arid
D. Humid
54.x: The sequence is perhumid or wet, humid, semi-arid and arid. These correspond respectively to A, B, D and E in the moisture classification described.
54.tq: Arrange a moisture gradient from maximum effectiveness to minimum effectiveness.
xs: Wettest to driest is **B, D, A, C** — **perhumid → humid → semi-arid → arid** — option **(1)**.
Thornthwaite's letters run **A** (perhumid) → **B** (humid) → C (sub-humid) → **D** (semi-arid) → **E** (arid).
xa: Semi-arid in India: the **rain-shadow interior Deccan**.
Arid: **western Rajasthan (Thar)** + Kutch.
Basis: **moisture index** and **potential evapotranspiration**.

54.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in relation to Thornthwaite moisture regions in India?
o: Western Ghats and west coast — perhumid belt
Western Rajasthan and Kutch — arid end
54.x: The rain-shadow interior of the Deccan is semi-arid, not humid. The Western Ghats-west coast and North-East are wettest, while western Rajasthan and Kutch represent the arid end.
54.tq: Find the reversed moisture comparison in the location-based options.
xs: **Rain-shadow interior Deccan — humid belt** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**; the interior Deccan is **semi-arid**.
Correct pairs: **Western Ghats-west coast** and **North-East** = perhumid (wettest); **western Rajasthan and Kutch** = arid.
xa: Thornthwaite's scale: **perhumid (A)** → humid (B) → sub-humid (C) → semi-arid (D) → **arid (E)**.
In Trewartha's scheme the rain-shadow Deccan falls under **BS/BW** (steppe).
AP's **Rayalaseema** is a **rain-shadow** region.

54.s: Under the Köppen classification, the broad climate type of Andhra Pradesh is
o: Aw — tropical wet and dry climate
54.x: Andhra Pradesh is classified as Aw, the tropical wet and dry or savannah climate.
54.tq: Discriminate between closely related Köppen codes.
xs: Under Köppen, AP is **Aw — tropical wet and dry** (savannah) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Am** is the tropical rainforest of the west coast and NE; AP is not desert or Mediterranean.
xa: AP's climate is also described as **Tropical Monsoon** (APPSC-GS 2018: **Tropical**).
Latitude: **12°41'N to 19°07'N**.
Influences: **Bay of Bengal, Eastern Ghats**, SW + NE monsoons.

54.s: Which one of the following regional descriptions is correctly matched?
o: Humid Coastal — Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and Kakinada
Deltaic — Anantapur, Kurnool and YSR Kadapa
Semi-arid Rayalaseema — Araku, Lambasingi and Horsley Hills
Hill or micro-climate — Krishna, Konaseema and Godavari districts
54.x: The humid coastal region includes Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and Kakinada. The other options interchange the deltaic, Rayalaseema and hill regions.
54.tq: Start from a sure region-district pair and identify swapped regional groupings.
xs: **Humid coastal — Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and Kakinada** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Deltaic** = Konaseema, East/West Godavari, Krishna; **semi-arid Rayalaseema** = Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai, Kurnool, Nandyal, YSR Kadapa.
**Hill/micro-climate** = **Araku, Lambasingi, Horsley Hills**.
xa: Humid coast: **high humidity, heavy rain**.
Rayalaseema: low rain, **droughts**, extreme heat.
Coldest place: **Lambasingi (ASR)**.

54.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the climate of Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: It has a Mediterranean climate and extends from 8°04'N to 12°41'N.
It has a tropical monsoon climate and extends approximately from 12°41'N to 19°07'N.
It has a tundra climate and extends from 12°41'S to 19°07'S.
It has a polar climate and extends from 19°07'N to 28°41'N.
54.x: Andhra Pradesh has a tropical monsoon climate and lies approximately between 12°41'N and 19°07'N.
54.tq: Combine the correct climatic description with the stated latitude range.
xs: AP has a **tropical monsoon climate** and lies from **12°41'N to 19°07'N** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is not Mediterranean, tundra or polar, and it lies in the northern hemisphere.
xa: Köppen type: **Tropical Wet and Dry (Aw)**.
Influences: **Bay of Bengal, Eastern Ghats**, SW + NE monsoons.
State average rainfall: **~966 mm**.

54.s:
Match the following regions of Andhra Pradesh with their characteristic features:

List-I
 a. Humid coastal region
 b. Deltaic region
 c. Semi-arid Rayalaseema
 d. Hill or micro-climate region

List-II
 i. Cool conditions and high local rainfall
 ii. Low rainfall, droughts and extreme heat
 iii. High humidity and heavy rainfall
 iv. Fertile land influenced by the south-west monsoon and rivers
54.x: The humid coast has high humidity and heavy rain; the deltaic region is fertile and river-fed; Rayalaseema is semi-arid; and the hills have cool micro-climates with local rain.
54.tq: Start with the distinctive Rayalaseema and hill-region pairs, then complete the code.
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**Humid coastal** = high humidity, heavy rain; **deltaic** = fertile, SW monsoon and river-fed.
**Semi-arid Rayalaseema** = low rain, droughts, extreme heat; **hill/micro-climate** = cool, high local rain.
xa: Hill stations: **Araku, Lambasingi, Horsley Hills**.
Deltaic districts: **Konaseema, East/West Godavari, Krishna**.
Rayalaseema peaks in **Oct-Nov** (NE monsoon).

54.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the rainfall gradient of Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Rainfall decreases from Rayalaseema towards the Sileru valley.
Rainfall is highest in the Sileru and Sabari valleys and decreases towards Rayalaseema.
Rainfall is highest in the Hagari valley and increases towards Rayalaseema.
All regions of the State receive nearly equal rainfall.
54.x: Rainfall is highest in the Sileru and Sabari valleys and decreases towards the drier Rayalaseema region.
54.tq: Use the direction of the gradient to reject the reversed statements.
xs: Rainfall is **highest in the Sileru and Sabari valleys** and **decreases towards Rayalaseema** — option **(2)**.
The **Hagari valley** is the driest (**<51 cm**), so rain does not rise towards Rayalaseema.
xa: Sileru-Sabari: **140-152 cm**; highest district **Visakhapatnam**.
Lowest district: **Anantapur**.
State average: **~966 mm**.
Coast peaks in **July**; Rayalaseema in **Oct-Nov**.

54.s: Which district has the highest rainfall in Andhra Pradesh, according to the stated district comparison?
54.x: Visakhapatnam is identified as the district with the highest rainfall in Andhra Pradesh.
54.tq: Distinguish the highest-rainfall district from the highest-rainfall valley.
xs: **Visakhapatnam** is the highest-rainfall district — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Anantapur** is the lowest-rainfall district; **Palnadu** has the hottest place, **Rentachintala**.
xa: Wettest area: **Sileru and Sabari valleys** (**140-152 cm**).
Driest area: **Hagari valley** (**<51 cm**).
⚠ Wettest **Sileru-Sabari / Visakhapatnam** vs driest **Hagari / Anantapur**.

54.s: The Hagari valley is associated with which of the following rainfall characteristics?
54.x: The Hagari valley receives less than 51 cm of rainfall and represents the lowest-rainfall zone.
54.tq: Match the named region with its reported rainfall range.
xs: The **Hagari valley** gets **rainfall below 51 cm** — the driest area — so option **(4)** is correct.
**140-152 cm** belongs to the wettest **Sileru and Sabari valleys**.
xa: Lowest-rainfall district: **Anantapur**.
**Scarce Rainfall Zone**: Kurnool, Anantapuramu.
Rayalaseema is a **rain-shadow** area peaking in **Oct-Nov**.

54.s: Why does Rayalaseema receive its peak rainfall during October-November rather than during the main south-west monsoon period?
o: It is directly exposed to the Arabian Sea branch of the monsoon.
It lies in the rain-shadow and benefits relatively more from the north-east monsoon.
It receives winter rainfall from western disturbances.
Its rainfall is controlled exclusively by local convection in April.
54.x: Rayalaseema lies in the rain-shadow of the south-west monsoon and receives its peak rainfall in October-November from the north-east monsoon.
54.tq: Connect the rain-shadow condition with the season of maximum rainfall.
xs: Rayalaseema is a **rain-shadow** region and gets its peak in **Oct-Nov** from the **NE monsoon** — option **(2)**.
The coast, by contrast, peaks in **July**.
xa: Rayalaseema: **low rain, droughts, extreme heat**.
Rainfall is highest in the **north coast** and falls towards Rayalaseema.
The **Scarce Rainfall Zone** needs **Handri-Neeva**-type lift irrigation.

54.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the climatic extreme in Andhra Pradesh?
54.x: The Sileru-Sabari valleys are identified as the wettest area. Rentachintala is the hottest, Lambasingi the coldest, and the Hagari valley the driest.
54.tq: Avoid swapping the named climatic extremes and locate the distinctive wettest area.
xs: **Wettest area — Sileru-Sabari valleys** is correct — option **(3)**.
**Rentachintala (Palnadu)** is the **hottest** and **Lambasingi (ASR)** the **coldest**, so options 1 and 2 are swapped.
The driest area is the **Hagari valley**, not Konaseema (a deltaic district).
xa: Sileru-Sabari rainfall: **140-152 cm**; Hagari **<51 cm**.
Highest district **Visakhapatnam**; lowest **Anantapur**.

54.s: Which of the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh's agro-climatic zones is correct?
o: The State has ten agro-climatic zones, all based on altitude.
The Scarce Rainfall Zone includes only coastal delta districts.
The State has three agro-climatic zones and no scarce rainfall zone.
The State has six agro-climatic zones, including the Scarce Rainfall Zone.
54.x: The current figure given is six agro-climatic zones, including the Scarce Rainfall Zone. Kurnool and Anantapuramu are included in that zone.
54.tq: Prefer the current stated count while checking the named special zone.
xs: AP has **six agro-climatic zones**, including the **Scarce Rainfall Zone** — option **(4)** (2024-25).
Older notes say **seven**; not ten or three.
xa: Scarce Rainfall Zone: **Kurnool, Anantapuramu** — not coastal deltas.
It needs **Handri-Neeva**-type lift irrigation.
Lowest-rainfall district: **Anantapur**.

54.s: The average annual rainfall of Andhra Pradesh is approximately:
54.x: The State average is about 966 mm. About 500 mm is nearer the driest Hagari valley (<51 cm), about 1,500 mm is the wettest Sileru-Sabari valleys (140-152 cm), and 2,000 mm is not reached anywhere in the State as given.
54.tq: AP avg ~966 mm; Sileru-Sabari wettest, Hagari driest.
xs: AP's state average rainfall is **~966 mm** — option **(2)**.
Rainfall ranges from **140-152 cm** (Sileru-Sabari) down to **<51 cm** (Hagari).
xa: Highest in the **north coast**, decreasing towards Rayalaseema.
Highest district **Visakhapatnam**; lowest **Anantapur**.
IMD forecast a **below-normal 2026 monsoon** for most of AP (**El Nino**).

54.s: Which one of the following statements about India's temperature trend is correct?
o: 2024 was India's warmest year since 1901, with 446 heatwave days.
2024 had no significant heatwave episode according to IMD.
2025 recorded India's highest heatwave total since 1901 at 446 days.
2024 was India's coldest year since 1901, with 446 heatwave days.
54.x: 2024 was India's warmest year since 1901 and recorded 446 heatwave days, the highest number since 2000.
54.tq: Separate the year of the record from the year of the comparison period.
xs: **2024 was India's warmest year since 1901**, with **446 heatwave days** — option **(1)**.
446 days was the **highest since 2000**, and it belongs to **2024**, not 2025.
xa: WMO: 2025 ~**1.43°C** above pre-industrial.

54.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The World Meteorological Organization placed 2025 at about 1.43°C above the pre-industrial level.
2. The years 2015-2025 constituted the eleven warmest years.
3. Himalayan heavy rainfall has increased by about 50% since the 1950s.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
54.x: All three statements are correct: 2025 was about 1.43°C above pre-industrial levels, 2015-2025 were the eleven warmest years, and Himalayan heavy rainfall rose by about 50% since the 1950s.
54.tq: Verify each independently reported climate indicator before choosing the combined code.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
WMO put **2025** at ~**1.43°C** above pre-industrial; **2015-2025** were the **11 warmest years**.
Himalayan heavy rainfall is up **~50% since the 1950s**.
xa: **2024** was India's warmest year since **1901**.
**446 heatwave days** in 2024.

54.s: The below-normal 2026 monsoon forecast for most of Andhra Pradesh was attributed to which phenomenon?
54.x: The forecast of a below-normal 2026 monsoon for most of Andhra Pradesh cited El Nino as a contributing factor.
54.tq: Match the forecast direction with the named climate phenomenon.
xs: IMD's **below-normal 2026 monsoon** forecast for most of AP cited **El Nino** — option **(3)**.
Western disturbances, La Nina and the Indian Ocean Dipole are not the cause the notes give.
xa: AP's rainfall peak: coast in **July**; Rayalaseema in **Oct-Nov**.
Projections: AP + Tamil Nadu may get **excess SW-monsoon rain**.
APSDMA has a **Heatwave Action Plan 2026**.

54.s: Coastal erosion at Uppada and along the Krishna coast is associated primarily with:
o: Glacial outburst floods and snow avalanches
River capture in the Eastern Ghats
Rising sea levels and cyclonic waves
54.x: The erosion at Uppada near Kakinada and along the Krishna coast is linked to rising seas and cyclonic waves.
54.tq: Identify the linked causes in a coastal-impact scenario.
xs: Erosion at **Uppada (Kakinada)** and the Krishna coast comes from **rising seas and cyclonic waves** — option **(4)**.
Glacial floods, volcanoes and river capture play no part.
xa: The **Godavari delta** is **sinking**; land subsidence exceeds regional sea-level rise.
AP coastline now **1,053.07 km** (3rd longest), **28** districts.
AP's coast is **cyclone-prone**.

54.s: Which statement best describes the present condition of the Godavari delta?
o: It is sinking, and land subsidence exceeds the regional sea-level rise.
It is rising faster than the regional sea level because of sediment accumulation.
It is unaffected by sea-level change because it lies inland.
It is being uplifted by tectonic activity.
54.x: The Godavari delta is sinking, and the rate of land subsidence exceeds the regional rise in sea level.
54.tq: Distinguish land subsidence from the separate process of sea-level rise.
xs: The **Godavari delta is sinking**: **land subsidence exceeds regional sea-level rise** — option **(1)**.
So it is neither rising, uplifted nor unaffected by sea-level change.
xa: **Uppada (Kakinada)** and the Krishna coast face erosion from rising seas and cyclonic waves.
~**40 coastal districts** may warm **>1°C by 2040**.
Deltaic districts: **Konaseema, East/West Godavari, Krishna**.

54.s: Which of the following correctly represents the change in heatstroke cases and deaths in Andhra Pradesh between 2023 and 2025?
o: Cases rose from 833 to 3, while deaths fell from 5,154 to 0.
Cases rose from 833 to 5,154, while deaths fell from 3 to 0.
Cases fell from 5,154 to 833, while deaths rose from 0 to 3.
Both cases and deaths increased during the period.
54.x: Heatstroke cases increased from 833 in 2023 to 5,154 in 2025, while reported deaths declined from 3 to zero.
54.tq: Keep the two parallel trends separate instead of assuming both move in the same direction.
xs: Heatstroke cases rose **833 (2023) → 5,154 (2025)**, while deaths fell **3 → 0** — option **(2)**.
The other options swap or misplace these figures.
xa: APSDMA **Heatwave Action Plan 2026**.
**2024** was India's warmest year since **1901**, with **446** heatwave days.
Hottest place in AP: **Rentachintala (Palnadu)**.

54.s: Which of the following projections regarding climate change impacts is correct?
o: Only inland districts may warm by more than 1°C by 2040.
Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu may receive no south-west monsoon rain, and no coastal district may warm by 2040.
Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu may receive excess south-west monsoon rain, and about 40 coastal districts may warm by more than 1°C by 2040.
The projection indicates a decline of more than 1°C in all coastal districts by 2040.
54.x: The projection indicates possible excess south-west monsoon rainfall in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu and warming above 1°C in around 40 coastal districts by 2040.
54.tq: Select the option retaining both the rainfall projection and the quantified warming estimate.
xs: AP and Tamil Nadu may get **excess SW-monsoon rain**, and ~**40 coastal districts** may warm **>1°C by 2040** — option **(3)**.
The projection is warming of coastal districts, not cooling or inland-only warming.
xa: IMD forecast a **below-normal 2026 monsoon** for most of AP (**El Nino**).
Coastal erosion at **Uppada** and the Krishna coast.
Himalayan heavy rainfall up **~50%** since the **1950s**.

54.s: Which of the following correctly states the latest figures given for Andhra Pradesh's coastline and coastal districts?
54.x: The latest figures stated are a coastline of 1,053.07 km, the third longest, and 28 coastal districts. Earlier figures were 974 km and 26 districts.
54.tq: Separate the latest figures from the earlier figures presented as a trap.
xs: The latest figures: **1,053.07 km** coastline (**3rd longest**) and **28 districts** (2025-26) — option **(4)**.
**974 km** and **26 districts** are the earlier (2024-25) figures.
xa: **Uppada (Kakinada)** faces coastal erosion.
The **Godavari delta** is sinking.
~**40** coastal districts may warm **>1°C by 2040**.

54.s: The National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) was launched on:
54.x: The NAPCC was launched on 30 June 2008.

The SAPCCs came later: **Odisha** prepared the first in **2010**.
xa: It has **8 missions**: Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, Strategic Knowledge.
**Odisha** was the first state with a **SAPCC (2010)**.

54.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change?
o: Solar; Enhanced Energy Efficiency; Sustainable Habitat; Water; Himalayan Ecosystem; Green India; Sustainable Agriculture; Strategic Knowledge
Solar; Nuclear Energy; Sustainable Habitat; Water; Himalayan Ecosystem; Green India; Industrial Agriculture; Strategic Knowledge
Solar; Enhanced Energy Efficiency; Rural Housing; Water; Himalayan Ecosystem; Blue India; Sustainable Agriculture; Strategic Knowledge
Solar; Enhanced Energy Efficiency; Sustainable Habitat; River Linking; Western Ghats Ecosystem; Green India; Sustainable Agriculture; Digital Knowledge
54.x: The eight NAPCC missions are Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture and Strategic Knowledge.
54.tq: Match the complete official list and eliminate options containing substituted mission names.
xs: The 8 missions are **Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, Strategic Knowledge** — option **(1)**.
Nuclear Energy, Rural Housing, Blue India, River Linking and Western Ghats are not NAPCC missions.
xa: NAPCC launch: **30 June 2008**.
SAPCCs shifted from mitigation (**2010-15**) to **district-level, risk-based adaptation** (2020 onwards).
First SAPCC: **Odisha (2010)**.

54.s:
Consider the following statements regarding climate adaptation expenditure and State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCCs):
1. Adaptation spending was estimated at 5.6% of GDP in FY 2022.
2. SAPCCs initially focused on mitigation plans during 2010–15.
3. From 2020 onwards, SAPCCs shifted towards district-level, risk-based adaptation plans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
54.x: All three statements are correct. Adaptation spending was 5.6% of GDP in FY 2022, while SAPCCs moved from mitigation plans during 2010–15 to district-level, risk-based adaptation planning from 2020 onwards.
54.tq: Read the time sequence carefully and retain all statements supported by the stated figures and periods.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Adaptation spending: **5.6% of GDP (FY22)**.
SAPCCs moved from **mitigation plans (2010-15)** to **district-level, risk-based adaptation plans (2020 onwards)**.
xa: First SAPCC: **Odisha (2010)**.
NAPCC launched **30 June 2008** with **8 missions**.
AP SAPCC 2025-30: **8 energy-sector adaptation measures**.

54.s: Which State was the first to prepare a State Action Plan on Climate Change (SAPCC)?
54.x: Odisha was the first State to have a SAPCC, prepared in 2010.
54.tq: Apply the first-in-sequence recall method to a state-level climate initiative.
xs: **Odisha** was the first state with a **SAPCC**, in **2010** — option **(1)**.
It is the **FIRST/LAST** fact of this topic; AP's own plan is the **AP SAPCC 2025-30**.
xa: SAPCCs: mitigation (**2010-15**) → district-level adaptation (**2020** onwards).

NAPCC launch: **30 June 2008**.

54.s:

xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.

Statement 4 is wrong: the target is **1 lakh** EV charging stations, not 10 lakh.

AP's hill micro-climates: **Araku, Lambasingi, Horsley Hills**.

54.s: Which statement best explains the importance of climate classification for Andhra Pradesh agriculture?

Cropping patterns are determined exclusively by soil texture, irrespective of rainfall.

AP has **six** agro-climatic zones (2024-25).
Driest: **Hagari valley** (**<51 cm**); lowest district **Anantapur**.

54.s: Which one of the following correctly characterises the broad climatic contrast within Andhra Pradesh?
o: Mediterranean climate, rain-shadow conditions in the coast, and a cyclone-free interior
Desert climate throughout the State, with no significant coastal influence
Tundra climate, humid conditions throughout Rayalaseema, and a cyclone-prone plateau
Aw climate, rain-shadow conditions in Rayalaseema, and a cyclone-prone coast
54.x: The stated AP climatic contrast includes Aw climate, the rain-shadow character of Rayalaseema and the cyclone-prone coast.
54.tq: Combine three regional descriptors without replacing one with its opposite.
xs: AP's contrast: **Aw climate**, **rain-shadow Rayalaseema** and a **cyclone-prone coast** — option **(4)**.
AP is not Mediterranean, desert or tundra.

Rayalaseema peaks in **Oct-Nov** (NE monsoon); coast peaks in **July**.
Coastal erosion: **Uppada** and Krishna coast.

54.s: The AP SAPCC for 2025–30 prescribed how many energy-sector adaptation measures through the AP State Climate Change Cell?
54.x: The AP State Climate Change Cell prescribed eight energy-sector adaptation measures under the AP SAPCC 2025–30.
54.tq: Distinguish the exact count from nearby even-number distractors.
xs: The AP SAPCC 2025-30 prescribed **8** energy-sector adaptation measures — option **(2)**.
They were prescribed by the **AP State Climate Change Cell**.
xa: Measures: renewables to **40%**, **120 GW** RE, two green hydrogen hubs (**60 MW**), **1 lakh EV charging stations**.
⚠ NAPCC also has **8 missions**.
First SAPCC: **Odisha (2010)**.

54.s: Which one of the following correctly pairs the first and the latest-year climate facts mentioned for India and State climate planning?
o: Odisha—first SAPCC in 2010; 2024—India’s warmest year since 1901
Andhra Pradesh—first SAPCC in 2010; 2024—India’s coldest year since 1901

Gujarat—first SAPCC in 2010; 2024—India’s wettest year since 1901

AP and Gujarat were not first; 2024 was the warmest, not coldest or wettest.

IMD anomaly: 2024 **+0.65°C**.
NAPCC launched **30 June 2008**.

La Nina, the Indian Ocean Dipole and the MJO are not the cause named.

Longer-term projection: AP + Tamil Nadu may get **excess SW-monsoon rain**.

55.s: Approximately what proportion of humanity lives on about one-tenth of the world's land area?
55.x: About 90 percent of humanity lives on approximately 10 percent of the world's land area.

xs: About **90 percent** of humanity lives on about **10%** of the land — option **(1)**.
So population is highly uneven: a small share of land carries almost everyone.
xa: Largest dense clusters: **East Asia** (eastern China, Japan) and **South Asia** (Ganga plains, Bangladesh delta).
Most people live in the **Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes and tropics of Asia**.
Hot and cold deserts (**Sahara, Arctic**) repel population.
India holds **17.7%** of world population on **2.4%** of area.

55.s:
Which of the following are identified as the two major dense population clusters of the world?
1. East Asia
2. South Asia
3. Central Sahara
4. Arctic Siberia
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
55.x: East Asia, including eastern China and Japan, and South Asia, including the Ganga plains and Bangladesh delta, are the two major dense population clusters.
55.tq: Eliminate sparsely populated regions first, then identify the two dense clusters.
xs: The two largest dense clusters are **East Asia** and **South Asia** — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Sahara** and **Arctic** are sparse: hot and cold deserts repel people.
xa: East Asia = **eastern China, Japan**; South Asia = **Ganga plains, Bangladesh delta**.
The **Ganges-Brahmaputra delta** is among the most densely populated areas on Earth.
**Asia** is the densest continent; **Africa** has the highest growth.

55.s: The Ganges-Brahmaputra delta is significant in world population geography because it is:
o: A region populated mainly because of mining
One of the most densely populated areas on Earth
A major sparsely populated desert region
55.x: The Ganges-Brahmaputra delta is among the most densely populated areas on Earth.
55.tq: Identify the density characteristic associated with the named physical region.
xs: The **Ganges-Brahmaputra delta** is **one of the most densely populated areas on Earth** — option **(3)**.
It belongs to the **South Asia** dense cluster (Ganga plains, Bangladesh delta), not a desert or mining region.

River valleys are densest — e.g. the **Nile valley**.
About **90%** of humanity lives on about **10%** of land.

55.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Factor)
(a) Water
(b) Landform
(c) Climate
(d) Soil

List-II (Effect)
(i) Moderate conditions attract population
(ii) River valleys support dense settlement

55.x: Water is associated with river valleys, landform with plains, climate with moderate conditions, and soil with fertile alluvium.
55.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a wrong environmental relationship.
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
**Water** → river valleys densest; **Landform** → plains favoured over mountains.
**Climate** → moderate climates attract; **Soil** → fertile alluvium supports dense farming.

**Industry**: jobs concentrate people — **Kobe-Osaka**.

55.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Katanga-Zambia copper belt — mining attracts workers
Kobe-Osaka — sparse population caused by absence of industry
Pilgrim towns — population repelled by religious activity
Arctic — moderate climate supporting dense farming
55.x: Mining in the Katanga-Zambia copper belt attracts workers. Kobe-Osaka illustrates industrial-urban concentration, while religious centres attract population.

**Kobe-Osaka** is dense because **industry** concentrates jobs; **pilgrim towns** attract people.
The **Arctic** is a cold desert that repels population.
xa: Social-cultural factor: religious centres attract; **unrest repels**.
⚠ **North-eastern USA** is dense but does **not depend directly on agriculture** (MPPSC 2021 key).
Moderate climates attract population.

55.s: The north-eastern United States is densely populated primarily because of its:
55.x: The north-eastern United States is a densely populated industrial-urban region and does not depend directly on agriculture in the manner of the Nile valley, Java or eastern China.
55.tq: Distinguish industrial-urban concentration from agriculturally based population concentration.
xs: The **north-eastern USA** is dense because of **industrial and urban development** — option **(3)**.
It does **not depend directly on agriculture** (MPPSC 2021 key), unlike the **Nile valley, Java, eastern China**.
xa: Industry and urbanisation: jobs concentrate people — **Kobe-Osaka**.
Fertile alluvium supports dense farming in **Java** and **eastern China**.
Mining draws workers — **Katanga-Zambia** copper belt.

55.s: Most of the world's population is concentrated in the:
o: Southern Hemisphere's high latitudes and polar regions
Equatorial regions of South America alone
Northern Hemisphere's mid-latitudes and the tropics of Asia
55.x: Population is concentrated mainly in the Northern Hemisphere's mid-latitudes and in the tropical regions of Asia.
55.tq: Combine the latitudinal and regional clues rather than selecting only one of them.
xs: Most people live in the **Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes and tropics of Asia** — option **(4)**.
Polar, Arctic-Antarctic and high southern latitudes are sparse; cold deserts repel people.
xa: About **90%** of humanity is on about **10%** of land.
Dense clusters: **East Asia** and **South Asia**.
**Asia** is the densest continent.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about the ten most populous countries of the world:
1. Together they hold about 60% of the world's population.
2. Six of them are located in Africa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
55.x: Statement 1 is correct: the top ten hold about 60% of humanity. Statement 2 is wrong: six of the ten are in Asia, not Africa (Africa is the fastest-growing continent, not the home of most top-ten countries). Hence '1 only'; '2 only' and 'Both' accept the wrong statement and 'Neither' rejects the correct one.
55.tq: Top 10 = 60%, 6 in Asia; do not confuse with Africa's fastest growth.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
1: the **top 10** countries hold **60%** of world population.
2 is wrong: **6** of the top 10 are in **Asia**, not Africa.
xa: ⚠ **Africa** has the **highest growth**; **Asia** is the **densest** continent.
**India** is the most populous country (since **April 2023**).
**Brazil** is the most populous South American country.

55.s: India overtook China as the world's most populous country in:
55.x: India overtook China in April 2023, when India's population was approximately 1.4258 billion.
55.tq: Use the middle date carefully; nearby years are the principal distractors.
xs: India overtook China in **April 2023** (~**1.4258** bn) — option **(1)**.
**China** had peaked at **1.426** bn in **2022**.
xa: India reached **1.46 billion** in **2025** (UNFPA SOWP 2025).
India = **17.7%** of world population on **2.4%** of area.
The world reached **8 billion** on **15 Nov 2022**.

55.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a continent with the stated demographic characteristic?
o: Brazil — most populous country in South America
South America — highest population growth rate
55.x: Brazil is the most populous country in South America. Africa has the highest population growth rate, while Asia is the densest continent.
55.tq: Match each continent or country with its specific demographic distinction.
xs: **Brazil** is the **most populous country in South America** — option **(3)** (UPPSC 2023 key).
**Africa** has the **highest growth**, and **Asia** is the **densest** continent — options 1 and 2 swap them.
xa: ⚠ The key swaps **Africa (growth)** and **Asia (density)** as traps.
**6** of the top 10 most populous countries are in **Asia**.
The top 10 hold **60%** of world population.

55.s: According to the UNFPA State of World Population 2025, India's population in 2025 was approximately:
55.x: SOWP 2025 put India at about 1.46 billion. India had about 1.4258 billion when it overtook China in April 2023, so 1.30 and 1.38 billion are too low, and 1.60 billion is too high.
55.tq: India 1.46 bn (SOWP 2025); overtook China Apr 2023.
xs: SOWP 2025 (UNFPA) puts India at **1.46 billion** in 2025 — option **(3)**.
India had ~**1.4258** bn when it overtook China in **April 2023**.
xa: The same report, **"The Real Fertility Crisis"**, put the world at **8.2 billion**.
China peaked at **1.426** bn (**2022**).
India's fertility has fallen to **replacement** without famine.

55.s:
Arrange the following population milestones in chronological order:
A. World population reached 3 billion
B. World population reached 5 billion
C. World population reached 2 billion
D. World population reached 7 billion
55.x: The milestones occurred in 1927, 1960, 1987 and 2011 respectively: 2 billion, 3 billion, 5 billion and 7 billion.
55.tq: Fix the earliest milestone first, then compare the intervening dates.
xs: The order is **C, A, B, D** — option **(1)**.
xa: **1 billion** came around **1804**, after over a million years.
**8 billion** — **15 Nov 2022** (UPSC).
The world was **2.5 billion in 1950**.

55.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a population milestone with its approximate year?
55.x: The world reached approximately 1 billion people around 1804. The 2, 4 and 6 billion milestones occurred in 1927, 1974 and 1999 respectively.
55.tq: Match the milestone number with its year and reject shifted entries from the same sequence.
xs: **1 billion — 1804** is correct — option **(1)**.
**2 billion** came in **1927**, **4 billion** in **1974**, **6 billion** in **1999**.
**1960** is the 3 billion year, **1987** the 5 billion year, **2011** the 7 billion year.
xa: The 1 billion mark took **over a million years**; 2 billion took ~**123 yrs** more.
8 billion: **15 Nov 2022**.
World was **2.5 billion** in **1950**.

55.s: The approximate intervals required for the world population to increase from 2 billion to 3 billion and from 7 billion to 8 billion were, respectively:
55.x: The population rose from 2 billion in 1927 to 3 billion in 1960, taking about 33 years, and from 7 billion in 2011 to 8 billion in 2022, taking about 11 years.
