2. It focuses on infrastructure in Minority Concentration Areas.
3. From 2022-23, it was revised to cover all districts, including 112 Aspirational Districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: PMJVK is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, supports infrastructure in Minority Concentration Areas and, after revision from 2022-23, covers all districts including 112 Aspirational Districts.
67.tq: Check the scheme’s funding pattern, target area and later geographical expansion independently.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
**PMJVK** is **centrally sponsored**; builds **infrastructure in Minority Concentration Areas**.
Revised from **2022-23** to cover **all districts**, incl. **112 Aspirational Districts**.
xa: Formerly **MsDP**.
**2024-25**: **₹646.91 crore** of projects approved.
**Jiyo Parsi** targets Parsi population decline.

67.s: Jiyo Parsi is intended to address:
o: The educational backwardness of Urdu-speaking students
The decline of the Parsi population
The infrastructure gap in Minority Concentration Areas
67.x: Jiyo Parsi targets the decline of the Parsi population.
67.tq: Match a distinctive scheme name with its narrowly defined target group.
xs: **Jiyo Parsi** targets the **decline of the Parsi population** — option **(3)** is correct.
Urdu coaching is run by the **AP Urdu Academy**; Haj aid by the **Haj Committee**; MCA infrastructure by **PMJVK**.
xa: **PMJVK** (formerly **MsDP**) funds infrastructure in **Minority Concentration Areas**.
**Central Waqf Council** = statutory, **1964**.
Latest notified minority: **Jains (2014)**.

67.s: The Central Waqf Council is a statutory body established in:
67.x: The Central Waqf Council is a statutory body dating from 1964.
67.tq: Use direct institutional year recall while separating the Council from later Waqf legislation.
xs: The **Central Waqf Council** is statutory, set up in **1964** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is a central body, separate from the state-level **AP State Waqf Board**.
xa: **Waqf (Amendment) Act 2025 / UMEED**: notified **5 April 2025**, in force **8 April 2025**.
The Act applies the **Limitation Act** and audits waqfs earning over **₹1 lakh**.
AP Waqf Board surveyed un-notified waqf properties: **7,005** of **10,522**.

67.s: The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, commonly associated with UMEED, was notified and brought into force on:
o: Notified on 5 April 2025 and enforced on 8 April 2025
Notified on 8 April 2025 and enforced on 5 May 2025
Notified on 1 April 2025 and enforced on 5 April 2025
Notified on 5 May 2025 and enforced on 8 May 2025
67.x: The Act was notified on 5 April 2025 and came into force on 8 April 2025.
67.tq: Preserve the order of closely spaced notification and commencement dates.
xs: The **Waqf (Amendment) Act 2025** was notified on **5 April 2025** and in force from **8 April 2025** — option **(1)** is correct.
Other options shift the dates.
xa: The **Limitation Act** now applies to waqfs.
Property data must go on the **UMEED portal** within **6** months.
Audit for waqfs earning over **₹1 lakh**.

67.s: Which one of the following is NOT a provision or associated feature mentioned in relation to the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 and UMEED?
o: Mandatory audit of every waqf irrespective of its income
Uploading property data on the UMEED portal within six months
Audit of waqfs earning over ₹1 lakh
67.x: The stated audit requirement applies to waqfs earning over ₹1 lakh; a mandatory audit of every waqf irrespective of income is not specified.
67.tq: Find the option that extends a qualified provision into an absolute one.
xs: **Mandatory audit of every waqf irrespective of income** is not a provision — option **(2)** is correct.
The audit applies only to waqfs **earning over ₹1 lakh**.
The **Limitation Act** applies, and property data go on the **UMEED portal** within **6** months — both are provisions.
xa: Notified **5 April 2025**; in force **8 April 2025**.
**Central Waqf Council** dates from **1964**.
AP Waqf Board pays **₹10,000/month** to Imams.

67.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Andhra Pradesh body/scheme)
a. AP State Minorities Finance Corporation
b. AP State Christian Minorities Finance Corporation
c. AP State Waqf Board
d. AP State Haj Committee

List-II (2024-25 fact)
i. 1,652 pilgrims approved for Haj 2025
 ii. Post-matric RTF of ₹36.34 crore to 50,767 beneficiaries
 iii. ₹10,000 per month to Imams and ₹5,000 to Mouzzans
 iv. ₹150.92 crore allocation and Jerusalem pilgrimage assistance

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
67.x: The Minorities Finance Corporation corresponds to post-matric RTF, the Christian Corporation to ₹150.92 crore and pilgrimage assistance, the Waqf Board to payments to Imams and Mouzzans, and the Haj Committee to 1,652 pilgrims.
67.tq: Start from the distinctive Haj-pilgrim and Waqf honorarium pairs, then complete the matching.
xs: **Minorities FC-RTF, Christian FC-₹150.92 cr, Waqf Board-Imam honorarium, Haj Committee-1,652 pilgrims** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Minorities FC**: post-matric RTF **₹36.34 cr** to **50,767**; **Christian FC**: **₹150.92 cr** + Jerusalem aid.
**Waqf Board**: **₹10,000/month** to Imams, **₹5,000** to Mouzzans; **Haj Committee**: **1,652** pilgrims for Haj **2025**.
xa: Minorities FC also pays **NTR Bharosa** **₹1,362.81 cr** to **3,26,617** minority pensioners.
Christian FC: **₹5,000** honorarium to pastors of **8,427** churches.

67.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with an AP minority welfare measure?
o: Urdu Academy — Free computer training in 36 centres and CEDM coaching of ₹5 crore
Haj Committee — Free computer training in 36 centres and CEDM coaching of ₹5 crore
Waqf Board — Christian Bhavan at Adavithakkellapadu
Christian Finance Corporation — Survey of 10,522 un-notified waqf properties
67.x: The AP State Urdu Academy provides free computer training in 36 centres and CEDM coaching involving ₹5 crore.
67.tq: Use the institutional-function match and reject cross-swapped departmental responsibilities.
xs: **Urdu Academy** — free computer training in **36** centres and **CEDM** coaching (**₹5 cr**) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Christian Bhavan** at Adavithakkellapadu belongs to the **Christian Finance Corporation**; the waqf survey of **10,522** properties to the **Waqf Board**.
xa: Waqf survey done for **7,005** of **10,522** un-notified properties.
**Haj Committee**: **1,652** pilgrims for Haj **2025**.
**Urdu** declared **second official language** (**17 Mar 2026**).

67.s: The allocation for minorities in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 was raised from:
67.x: The AP minority allocation was raised from ₹5,434 crore to ₹6,090 crore in the 2026-27 Budget.
67.tq: Test the direction and exact values of a budget increase.
xs: AP's minority allocation rose from **₹5,434 crore → ₹6,090 crore** in Budget **2026-27** — option **(4)** is correct.
The other options misstate the starting or final figure.
xa: **₹180 crore** a year to **Imams** and **Mouzams**.
**Urdu** declared **second official language** (**17 Mar 2026**).
First two years: minorities got **₹4,856 crore** of welfare (over **17 lakh** beneficiaries).

67.s: Which of the following statements regarding recent Andhra Pradesh minority-related measures is correct?
o: ₹1,800 crore a year was allocated to Imams and Mouzams, and Urdu ceased to have official status.
₹180 crore a year was allocated only to pastors, and Telugu was declared the second official language.
₹18 crore a year was allocated to Imams and Mouzams, and Urdu was declared the third official language.
₹180 crore a year was allocated to Imams and Mouzams, and Urdu was declared the second official language.
67.x: The annual allocation for Imams and Mouzams was stated as ₹180 crore, and Urdu was declared the second official language of Andhra Pradesh.
67.tq: Combine the correct amount with the correct language-status fact and reject altered scale or status.
xs: **₹180 crore** a year goes to **Imams and Mouzams**, and **Urdu** was declared the **second official language** — option **(4)** is correct.
The other options change the amount, the beneficiaries or the language's status.
xa: Urdu became second official language on **17 Mar 2026**.
Minority allocation **₹5,434 crore → ₹6,090 crore**.
AP Waqf Board: **₹10,000/month** to Imams, **₹5,000** to Mouzzans.

67.s: Which one of the following accurately describes the status of the Uniform Civil Code in the context stated?
o: Uttarakhand’s UCC has been in force since January 2025; Bills passed by Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh await Presidential assent.
UCC has been in force in all NDA-ruled States since January 2025; no State Bills await assent.
Only Assam’s Bill awaits Presidential assent, while Uttarakhand’s UCC has not yet commenced.
Uttarakhand, Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh all implemented their UCC laws in 2024.
67.x: Uttarakhand’s UCC came into force in January 2025, while the Bills of Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh were awaiting Presidential assent.
67.tq: Separate an enacted and operative law from Bills that have only been passed and await assent.
xs: **Uttarakhand**'s UCC is in force since **January 2025**; **Assam, Gujarat, MP** Bills await **Presidential assent** — option **(1)** is correct.
So UCC is not in force in all NDA states, and the three states have not implemented it.
xa: Union Home Minister: UCC in all **21** NDA-ruled States by **2029**.
NCM Chairperson: **Harjit Singh Grewal** (**Jul 2026**).
Census **2027** asks the religion and birthplace of both parents.

67.s: Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act has been criticised primarily because it:
o: Gives the Centre unbridled power to notify minorities, despite the state-level identification approach associated with T.M.A. Pai.
Transfers all minority identification powers exclusively to State Commissions.
Requires every minority community to be identified only through a census conducted by the Supreme Court.
Prevents the Centre from notifying any minority community.
67.x: The criticism is that Section 2(c) gives the Centre unbridled power to notify minorities, whereas T.M.A. Pai is associated with state-level identification.
67.tq: Match the legal criticism with the correct authority and constitutional interpretation.
xs: **Section 2(c)** gives the Centre "**unbridled power**" to notify minorities, against the **T.M.A. Pai** **state-level** identification test — option **(1)** is correct.
It does not hand powers to State Commissions or bar the Centre from notifying.
xa: Latest notified minority: **Jains (2014)**.
Religious minorities are only about **5%** of higher-judiciary appointees.
"**Demography**" narrative vs **fertility** data is another debate.

67.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relevant minority institutions and facts in Andhra Pradesh?
o: AP has only a Waqf Board; Christians number 6.28 lakh and Urdu is the third official language.
AP has a State Minorities Commission, but Urdu is not an official language and Christians number 8.62 lakh.
AP has only a Central Minorities Commission and no separate Christian Finance Corporation or Waqf Board.
AP has a State Minorities Commission, separate Minorities and Christian Minorities Finance Corporations, and a Waqf Board; Christians number 6.82 lakh and Urdu is the second official language.
67.x: Andhra Pradesh has the stated State Minorities Commission, separate Minorities and Christian Minorities Finance Corporations and a Waqf Board; its Christian population is 6.82 lakh and Urdu is the second official language.
67.tq: Check the complete institutional and numerical combination rather than one isolated fact.
xs: AP has a **State Minorities Commission**, separate **Minorities** and **Christian Minorities Finance Corporations**, a **Waqf Board**; Christians **6.82 lakh**; **Urdu** second official language — option **(4)** is correct.
**6.28** and **8.62 lakh** are distorted figures; Urdu is the **second**, not third, official language.
xa: Christians ≈ **1.4%** of AP.
Urdu declared second official language on **17 Mar 2026**.
AP also has a **Haj Committee** and an **Urdu Academy**.

67.s: In April 2026, the Andhra Pradesh minority cell fast-tracked DBT of post-matric scholarships. The income ceiling associated with the scheme is:
67.x: The income ceiling for the post-matric scholarship is ₹2.5 lakh, and the AP minority cell fast-tracked its DBT in April 2026.
67.tq: Apply the scheme’s income criterion to a current administrative action.
xs: The post-matric scholarship income ceiling is **₹2.5 lakh** — option **(3)** is correct.
The AP minority cell fast-tracked its **DBT** in **April 2026**.
xa: Central post-matric scholarship: parental income below **₹2.5 lakh**; **30%** for girls.
AP Minorities FC: post-matric RTF **₹36.34 cr** to **50,767**.
Paid through **NSP 2.0**.

67.s: Which of the following statements regarding religious enumeration in India is correct?
o: The 2011 Census recorded the Hindu share above 80% and introduced only a ‘No Religion’ category.
The 2011 Census was the first census in which the Hindu share fell below 80%, and it also included a ‘No Religion’ option for the first time.
The 2001 Census was the first in which the Hindu share fell below 80%, but it did not include a ‘No Religion’ option.
The 2021 Census was the first census in which the Hindu share fell below 80%.
67.x: The year 2011 marked both the first census in which the Hindu share fell below 80% and the first inclusion of a ‘No Religion’ option.
67.tq: Combine two first-occurrence facts tied to the same census year.
xs: Census **2011** was the first with the **Hindu share below 80%** and the first **"No Religion"** option — option **(2)** is correct.
Hindu share fell **80.5% to 79.8%** from **2001** to **2011** — so 2001 was still above 80%.
xa: Muslim share **13.4% to 14.2%**.
Religion data released **27 August 2015**.
Census **2027**: six religions + "other religion".

67.s: The Census 2027 enumeration schedule includes which of the following?
o: Only the six notified religions, without any parental information
The six religions plus ‘other religion’, along with the religion and birthplace of both parents
Only ‘No Religion’ and ‘Other Religion’, along with the birthplace of grandparents
The six religions plus caste, but no question on birthplace
67.x: The Census 2027 schedule lists the six religions and ‘other religion’, and asks the religion and birthplace of both parents.
67.tq: Watch for omissions and substitutions in a list-based enumeration question.
xs: Census **2027** lists **six religions + "other religion"** and asks the **religion and birthplace of both parents** — option **(2)** is correct.
It asks about **parents**, not grandparents, and keeps the **six religions**.
xa: Census **2011** first offered a **"No Religion"** option.
Six major religions: **Hindu, Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain**.
**ORP** = **Other Religions and Persuasions** (**0.7%** in **2011**).

67.s: Which one of the following pairs correctly represents the two debates mentioned in relation to religious minorities?
o: The ‘demography’ narrative versus literacy data; and the over-representation of religious minorities in higher-judiciary appointments.
The ‘demography’ narrative versus fertility data; and the low representation of religious minorities in higher-judiciary appointments.
The ‘migration’ narrative versus rainfall data; and the absence of minorities from all courts.
The ‘demography’ narrative versus urbanisation data; and the representation of minorities exclusively in local courts.
67.x: The debates include the demography narrative in relation to fertility data and the fact that religious minorities constitute only about 5% of higher-judiciary appointees.
67.tq: Match each debate with its correct comparison and avoid reversing the representation claim.
xs: The debates: "**demography**" narrative vs **fertility data**, and **low** minority share of **higher-judiciary** appointees — option **(2)** is correct.
Religious minorities are only about **5%** of higher-judiciary appointees — under-, not over-represented.
xa: The fertility debate is dated **8 Jun 2026**.
Muslim share **10% (1951)** to **14% (2011)** tied to economic status and female education.
**Section 2(c)** vs **T.M.A. Pai** is a third debate.

67.s: Which notified minority community is the latest among the following, with notification in 2014?
67.x: Jains were notified as a minority community in 2014 and are the latest notified minority among the communities mentioned.
67.tq: Use chronology and distinguish the latest notified community from older notified groups.
xs: **Jains** were the latest notified minority, in **2014** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Christians**, **Parsis** and **Buddhists** were notified earlier.
xa: Jains: **0.4%** of India; lowest growth **5.4%**.
Jains have the **highest literacy** (about **95%**).
Most Jains live in **Maharashtra**.

67.s: Who was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities for a full three-year term in July 2026?
67.x: Harjit Singh Grewal was appointed NCM Chairperson for a full three-year term in July 2026. T.M.A. Pai is the Supreme Court case on State-level identification of minorities, Virginius Xaxa chaired the 2013 committee on tribal status, and K.S. Singh led AnSI's People of India project.
67.tq: NCM Chairperson (Jul 2026): Harjit Singh Grewal.
xs: **Harjit Singh Grewal** became NCM Chairperson for a full **3**-year term in **Jul 2026** — option **(2)** is correct.
**T.M.A. Pai** is a judgment on minority identification; **Xaxa** and **K.S. Singh** are tribal/anthropology figures.
xa: **Section 2(c)** of the NCM Act gives the Centre power to notify minorities.
Latest notified minority: **Jains (2014)**.
AP has its own **State Minorities Commission**.

68.s: Which language family accounted for approximately 73 per cent of India's speakers according to the older figures used in APPSC material?
68.x: The Indo-European or Indo-Aryan family accounted for approximately 73 per cent of speakers in the older figures. The 2011 Census estimate was about 78.05 per cent.
68.tq: Use the distinctive numerical share to separate the major language families.
xs: **Indo-European (Indo-Aryan)** had about **73%** of speakers in the older figures — option **(2)** is correct.
Older shares: Dravidian about **20%**, Austric about **1.38%**, Sino-Tibetan about **0.85%**.
xa: Census **2011**: Indo-Aryan **78.05**, Dravidian **19.64**, Austro-Asiatic **1.11**, Tibeto-Burman **1.01**.
Indo-Aryan is the **largest by area and speakers** (north, west, east India).
Minor group: **Semito-Hamitic (Afro-Asiatic)** — Arabic.

68.s: The Dardic branch, including Kashmiri, belongs to which language family?
68.x: Kashmiri belongs to the Dardic branch of the Indo-Aryan family. Dardic is not a Sino-Tibetan branch.
68.tq: Discriminate between the closely confused Dardic and Sino-Tibetan classifications.
xs: **Dardic** (incl. **Kashmiri**) is **Indo-Aryan** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ "**Dardi is Sino-Tibetan**" was the false statement in the APPSC-G1 **2024** PYQ.
xa: Dardic is spoken in **J&K**.
Other Indo-Aryan: Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Odia, Assamese, **Sindhi, Kachchhi**.
Sino-Tibetan includes **Manipuri, Bodo, Bhotia, Garo**.

68.s:
With reference to the Dravidian language family, consider the following statements:
1. Telugu is classified as a South-Central Dravidian language.
2. Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam are associated with the southern branch.
3. Kui, Gondi and Kurukh are identified with Central or North Dravidian areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: All three statements are correct. Telugu is South-Central Dravidian, while Kui, Gondi and Kurukh represent Central or North Dravidian languages or pockets.
68.tq: Check each branch-language association before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
**Telugu** = **South-Central Dravidian**; **Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam** = South branch.
**Kui/Kuvi, Gondi, Kurukh** = Central/North Dravidian tribal languages.
xa: ⚠ An older table puts AP under "**Central Dravidian**".
Dravidian share: about **20%** (older), **19.6%** in **2011**.
North Dravidian areas: **Bihar, Odisha, WB**.

68.s: The Austro-Asiatic language family in India is represented by which of the following branches?
68.x: The Austro-Asiatic family includes the Munda branch, with languages such as Santhali and Mundari, and the Mon-Khmer branch, including Khasi.
68.tq: Recall the two-branch structure of the Austro-Asiatic family.
xs: Austro-Asiatic has the **Munda** and **Mon-Khmer** branches — option **(4)** is correct.
**Tibeto-Burman** is Sino-Tibetan; **Dardic** is Indo-Aryan; the others are Dravidian branches.
xa: Munda: **Santhali, Mundari, Ho, Savara**; Mon-Khmer: **Khasi, Nicobarese**.
Areas: **Jharkhand-Odisha-WB** tribal belt, **Meghalaya**, **Nicobar Islands**.
Share about **1.1-1.4%**.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
68.x: Kui is a Dravidian language associated with the Kandhas of Odisha. Santhali, Khasi and Garo are correctly matched with their respective branches or families.
68.tq: Find the wrongly assigned language family among otherwise familiar tribal-language pairs.
xs: **Kui — Austro-Asiatic** is wrong; **Kui** is **Dravidian** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Garo** = Sino-Tibetan; **Santhali** = Munda; **Khasi** = Mon-Khmer — all correct.
xa: Kui is spoken by the **Kandhas** of Odisha (Dongria Kondh).
⚠ **Khasi** = Austro-Asiatic (Mon-Khmer); **Garo** = Sino-Tibetan (Bodo group).
⚠ **Kui** and **Koya** = Dravidian; **Savara** and **Ho** = Munda.

68.s: The Sino-Tibetan or Tibeto-Burman languages of India are concentrated mainly in which region?
o: The north-eastern States, Sikkim and Himalayan areas
The Deccan plateau and Tamil Nadu
The Konkan coast and western Rajasthan
68.x: Sino-Tibetan languages are concentrated in the north-eastern States, Sikkim and Himalayan areas, and are also represented in Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh.
68.tq: Use regional distribution to distinguish Sino-Tibetan languages from the other families.
xs: Sino-Tibetan languages are concentrated in the **NE States, Sikkim** and **Himalaya** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Jharkhand-Odisha** belt is Austric; the **Deccan** and Tamil Nadu are Dravidian.
xa: Also in **Ladakh** and **Himachal Pradesh**.
Members: **Manipuri, Bodo, Bhotia, Garo**.
Share about **0.85-1%**.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ho — Dravidian language of Tamil Nadu
68.x: Halbi is an Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh. Kui is Dravidian, while Ho and Mundari are Austro-Asiatic Munda languages.
68.tq: Start with the sure regional association and eliminate the swapped family-location pairs.
xs: **Halbi — Indo-Aryan language of Bastar** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Kui** is Dravidian (Odisha); **Ho** and **Mundari** are Austro-Asiatic (Munda) of **Jharkhand and Odisha**.
xa: **Gor Boli** is also Indo-Aryan.
**Koya** (Godavari agency) is Dravidian.
**Savara (Sora)** is Munda — Srikakulam-Vizianagaram hills.

68.s: The presence of Khasi, an Austro-Asiatic language of the Mon-Khmer branch, is considered evidence that the Meghalaya plateau was once part of:
68.x: Khasi is treated as evidence that the Meghalaya plateau was once part of peninsular India. Its Mon-Khmer affiliation links it with the Austro-Asiatic linguistic zone.
68.tq: Apply a linguistic-distribution clue to infer the historical geographical relationship.
xs: **Khasi** (Mon-Khmer) suggests the Meghalaya plateau was once part of **Peninsular India** — option **(2)** is correct.
Khasi is Austro-Asiatic, like the peninsular Munda languages.
xa: ⚠ **Garo** is **Sino-Tibetan** (Bodo group), despite also being in Meghalaya.
Meghalaya declared **Khasi and Garo** official languages alongside English.
**Nicobarese** is also Mon-Khmer.

68.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Santhali — Austro-Asiatic
2. Savara — Austro-Asiatic
3. Garo — Sino-Tibetan
4. Gor Boli — Indo-Aryan
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
68.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Santhali and Savara are Austro-Asiatic, Garo is Sino-Tibetan and Gor Boli is Indo-Aryan.
68.tq: Verify each tribal-language affiliation individually before choosing the complete combination.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
**Santhali** and **Savara** = Austro-Asiatic; **Garo** = Sino-Tibetan; **Gor Boli** = Indo-Aryan.
xa: **Gor Boli (Lambadi)**: spoken by **Banjaras**; **no native script**.
Santhali script: **Ol Chiki**.
**Gadaba** has Munda (**Gutob**) and Dravidian (**Ollari**) varieties.

68.s:
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the older figures from the 2011 Census-based estimates for India's language families?
1. The older estimate for Indo-Aryan was about 73 per cent, whereas the 2011 estimate was about 78.05 per cent.
2. The older estimate for Dravidian was about 20 per cent, whereas the 2011 estimate was about 19.64 per cent.
3. The older estimate for Tibeto-Burman was about 20 per cent.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
68.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the older Tibeto-Burman estimate was about 0.85 per cent, not 20 per cent.
68.tq: Compare corresponding figures and detect the misplaced decimal-scale percentage.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
3: Wrong — the older Tibeto-Burman figure was about **0.85%**, not 20.
xa: Census **2011**: Austro-Asiatic **1.11**, Tibeto-Burman **1.01**.
Older Austric figure: **1.38%**.
Indo-Aryan is the **largest** family.

68.s: Which one of the following statements about Santhali is correct?
o: It is written in Roman script and was included through the 73rd Amendment of 1992.
It is written in Ol Chiki, created by Raghunath Murmu in 1925, and entered the Eighth Schedule through the 92nd Amendment of 2003.
It is written in Ol Chiki, created in 1950, and is not a Scheduled Language.
It is written in Devanagari and entered the Eighth Schedule through the 42nd Amendment of 1976.
68.x: Santhali is written in Ol Chiki, created by Raghunath Murmu in 1925. It was included in the Eighth Schedule through the 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.
68.tq: Combine script, creator and amendment-year facts to reject near-miss options.
xs: **Santhali** is written in **Ol Chiki** (created by **Raghunath Murmu**, **1925**) and entered via the **92nd Amendment, 2003** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is a **scheduled** language and its script is not Roman or Devanagari.
xa: The **92nd Amendment** also added **Bodo, Dogri, Maithili**.
Santhali is **Austroasiatic** (Munda).
The President released a **digital Constitution** in Santhali (**2026**).

68.s: According to an APPSC (2007) question, most of the tribal languages of central and eastern India belong to which language family?
68.x: Most tribal languages of central and eastern India (Jharkhand-Odisha-West Bengal belt: Santhali, Mundari, Ho) are Austric. Dravidian covers only some central tribal pockets (Gondi, Kui, Kurukh); Sino-Tibetan is the language family of the North-East and Himalaya; Indo-Aryan is the family of the north, west and east plains.
68.tq: Central-eastern tribal belt = Austric (Munda).
xs: Most tribal languages of central and eastern India are **Austric (Austro-Asiatic)** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC **2007**).
Austric is spoken by the tribes of **Jharkhand**.
xa: Munda languages: **Santhali, Mundari, Ho, Savara**.
⚠ Some central tribal tongues — **Kui, Gondi, Kurukh** — are Dravidian.
Share about **1.1-1.4%**.

68.s: According to the 1961 Census, how many mother tongues were listed?
68.x: The 1961 Census listed 1,652 mother tongues.
68.tq: Direct numerical recall of a census figure.
xs: Census **1961** listed **1,652 mother tongues** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-G1 **2024**, true statement).
xa: Census **2011**: about **19,500** raw → **1,369** mother tongues → **121** languages.
**Grierson** (**1903-1928**): **179** languages, **544** dialects.
**Ethnologue**: **455** living languages.

68.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Census 2011 language data:
1. About 19,500 raw mother tongues were rationalised into 1,369 mother tongues.
2. The 1,369 mother tongues were grouped into 121 languages.
3. The 121 languages comprised 22 scheduled and 99 non-scheduled languages.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: All three statements are correct. Census 2011 language returns were rationalised into 1,369 mother tongues and grouped into 121 languages, consisting of 22 scheduled and 99 non-scheduled languages.
68.tq: Combine the raw count, rationalised count and scheduled/non-scheduled classification.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
About **19,500** raw mother tongues → **1,369** mother tongues → **121 languages** (**22** scheduled + **99** non-scheduled).
xa: ⚠ "**123** major languages" for **2011** is wrong.
A Census "language" needs **10,000+** speakers.
About **56** languages are counted as subsets of **Hindi**.

68.s: For purposes of Census language classification, a language generally requires at least how many speakers?
68.x: The Census counts a language when it has 10,000 or more speakers.
68.tq: Test the exact threshold rather than the broader language count.
xs: A Census language needs **10,000+ speakers** — option **(3)** is correct.
About **56** languages are counted as **subsets of Hindi**.
xa: Critics say the **10,000-speaker cutoff** helps Hindi "erase" **Maithili, Braj, Awadhi**.
**SPPEL** covers languages with **fewer than 10,000** speakers.
**121** Census languages in **2011**.

68.s: Grierson's Linguistic Survey of India, conducted during 1903–1928, recorded:
68.x: Grierson's Linguistic Survey of India recorded 179 languages and 544 dialects between 1903 and 1928.
68.tq: Keep the language count and dialect count in their correct order.
xs: **Grierson**'s **Linguistic Survey of India** (**1903-1928**) recorded **179 languages, 544 dialects** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) swaps them; **121** and **1,369** are Census **2011** figures.
xa: **G.N. Devy**'s People's Linguistic Survey: **780+** languages.
Census **1961**: **1,652** mother tongues.
**Ethnologue**: **455**.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
68.x: Ethnologue lists 455 living languages in India. The People's Linguistic Survey documents more than 780 languages, while 1,652 mother tongues belong to the 1961 Census.
68.tq: Match each survey or source with its distinctive count.
xs: **Ethnologue — 455 living languages** is correct — option **(1)**.
**121** = Census **2011**; **1,652** = Census **1961**; **780+** = **People's Linguistic Survey** (G.N. Devy).
xa: **Grierson**: **179** languages, **544** dialects.
**Mother Tongue Survey of India**: about **19,500**, incl. **103** foreign.
Another PLSI count: **1,600+** (UPSC).

68.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Census language count from the constitutional language count?
o: Only the 99 non-scheduled languages are constitutionally recognised.
All 121 Census languages are included in the Eighth Schedule.
The Eighth Schedule contains all 1,369 rationalised mother tongues.
The 121-language Census count includes 22 scheduled and 99 non-scheduled languages.
68.x: The Census grouped mother tongues into 121 languages, of which 22 are in the Eighth Schedule and 99 are non-scheduled. The 121-language Census count should not be equated with the constitutional list.
68.tq: Separate the Census classification from constitutional recognition.
xs: The **121** Census languages = **22 scheduled + 99 non-scheduled** — option **(4)** is correct.
Only the **22** in the **Eighth Schedule** are constitutionally recognised — not all 121, nor the 99.
xa: ⚠ Calling the **121** "constitutionally recognised" (**21 Feb 2026**) is wrong.
**1,369** is the rationalised mother-tongue count.
**99 languages** remain outside the Schedule (**Jul 2025**).

68.s: Which group consists of the scheduled languages with the smallest number of speakers as per Census 2011?
68.x: Sanskrit, Bodo and Manipuri are the smallest scheduled languages. Hindi, Bengali and Marathi are the three largest; Telugu, Tamil and Kannada are large Dravidian languages; Kashmiri is not among the smallest, and Punjabi and Odia have many speakers.
68.tq: Smallest scheduled: Sanskrit, Bodo, Manipuri (not Kashmiri).
xs: The smallest scheduled languages are **Sanskrit, Bodo, Manipuri** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Telugu, Tamil** are the top languages.
xa: ⚠ Some notes list **Kashmiri** among the smallest — it is not.
**Bodo** joined via the **92nd** Amendment; **Manipuri** via the **71st**.
**Sanskrit** was in the original **14**.

68.s:
Arrange the following Indian languages in descending order of their share of speakers according to the 2011 Census:
A. Telugu
B. Hindi
C. Tamil
D. Bengali
68.x: The correct order is Hindi (43.6 per cent), Bengali (8.0 per cent), Telugu (6.7 per cent) and Tamil (5.7 per cent).
68.tq: Order the items by their numerical shares, beginning with the largest value.
xs: Descending: **Hindi > Bengali > Telugu > Tamil** (B, D, A, C) — option **(1)** is correct.
Shares: Hindi **43.6%**, Bengali **8.0%**, Telugu **6.7%**, Tamil **5.7%**.
xa: **Marathi** (**6.9%**) is third.
Telugu slipped **3rd (2001) → 4th (2011)**.
Hindi = most spoken first language.

68.s: Which change in the ranking of Indian languages occurred between the 2001 and 2011 Census figures?
o: Bengali moved from second to fifth, while Tamil became second.
Hindi moved from first to third, while Marathi became first.
Tamil moved from fifth to third, while Telugu became fifth.
Telugu moved from third to fourth, while Marathi overtook it for third place.
68.x: Telugu had occupied third place in 2001, but Marathi overtook it in 2011; Telugu consequently stood fourth.
68.tq: Test the direction of change in a close ranking rather than merely recalling the final order.
xs: **Telugu** slipped **3rd → 4th**, overtaken by **Marathi** — option **(4)** is correct.
Hindi stayed **1st** (**43.6%**) and Bengali **2nd** (**8.0%**).
xa: Marathi **6.9%**; Telugu **6.7%**.
Telugu is **classical** since **2008**.
**Telugu Language Day** = **29 August**.

68.s: Which of the following correctly states the world ranking of the three Indian languages mentioned among the world's most spoken languages?
68.x: Among the stated world rankings, Hindi is second, Bengali is seventh and Punjabi is tenth.
68.tq: Retain the separate world ranks and avoid substituting the Indian domestic ranking.
xs: World ranking: **Hindi 2nd, Bengali 7th, Punjabi 10th** — option **(3)** is correct.
After Hindi, **Bengali** is the Indian language most spoken worldwide (APPSC **2012**).
xa: In India Bengali is **2nd** (**8.0%**).
About **12%** of Indians speak lesser-recognised local languages.
Hindi = lingua franca of **north and central India**.

68.s: Which language is described as the most spoken first language and as the lingua franca of northern and central India?
68.x: Hindi is the most spoken first language and functions as the lingua franca of northern and central India.
68.tq: Distinguish the status of a first language and lingua franca from a language's global rank.
xs: **Hindi** is the most spoken first language and the **lingua franca** of north and central India — option **(1)** is correct.
Its share is **43.6%** (Census **2011**).
xa: **Art. 343**: Union official language = **Hindi in Devanagari**.
**Art. 351**: Union's duty to develop Hindi.
World rank: **2nd**.

68.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Each State may choose its own official language or languages.
2. Hindi and English are the official languages of the Union.
3. A State is constitutionally required to adopt Hindi as its only official language.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: States may choose their own official language or languages, while Hindi and English are the Union’s official languages. A State is not required to adopt Hindi as its only official language.
68.tq: Identify the extreme word ‘only’ in the false statement about State language choice.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
1: Each State **chooses its own** official language(s) — correct (**Art. 345**).
2: **Hindi + English** are Union official languages — correct (UPSC).
3: Wrong — no State must adopt Hindi alone.
xa: AP: **Telugu and Urdu** (**2019** PYQ).
Meghalaya: **English** + **Khasi and Garo**.
**Official Languages Act, 1963** kept English after **1965**.

68.s: The Munshi-Ayyangar formula was adopted on:
68.x: The Munshi-Ayyangar formula was adopted on 14 September 1949, a date now observed as Hindi Diwas.
68.tq: Distinguish the constitutional language date from Independence and Republic Day dates.
xs: The **Munshi-Ayyangar formula** was adopted on **14 September 1949** — option **(3)** is correct.
That date is now **Hindi Diwas**.
xa: Hindi in Devanagari = Union's official language with a **15-year** transition.
**14** languages recognised in the Eighth Schedule.
Provinces were free to choose a regional language or **English**.

68.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Munshi-Ayyangar formula?
o: Fourteen languages were recognised in the Eighth Schedule
All provinces were prohibited from using English for official purposes
Hindi in Devanagari was designated as the Union’s official language
68.x: The formula allowed provinces to choose a regional language or English. It did not prohibit all use of English; Hindi was to become the Union’s official language after a 15-year transition.
68.tq: Find the absolute prohibition that contradicts the provision allowing regional language or English.
xs: Prohibiting English in provinces was **not** a feature — option **(2)** is correct.
Provinces were **free to choose a regional language or English**.
**14** languages, a **15-year transition** and **Hindi in Devanagari** were features.
xa: Adopted **14 September 1949** (Hindi Diwas).
**Official Languages Act, 1963** kept English after **1965**.
**Art. 343** = Union official language.

68.s: The Official Languages Act, 1963 is significant because it:
o: Required every State to adopt the three-language formula
Continued the use of English alongside Hindi after 1965
Removed Hindi from the Union’s official-language framework
Made Sanskrit the sole official language of the Union
68.x: The Official Languages Act, 1963 continued English in use alongside Hindi after 1965.
68.tq: Identify the legal effect of the Act rather than confusing it with the original constitutional transition plan.
xs: The **Official Languages Act, 1963** kept **English** in use **after 1965**, alongside **Hindi** — option **(2)** is correct.
The three-language formula came from the **NPE 1968**, not this Act.
xa: **Munshi-Ayyangar** formula gave a **15-year** transition.
Union: **Hindi + English**.
**Art. 344**: Official Language Commission.

68.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Article)
A. Article 343
B. Article 344
C. Article 345
D. Article 351
List-II (Provision)
1. State Legislature adopts the official language(s) of the State
2. Official language of the Union: Hindi in Devanagari
3. Union's duty to develop Hindi
4. President's Official Language Commission and Parliamentary Committee
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
68.x: Art. 343 = Hindi in Devanagari as Union's official language (A-2); Art. 344 = President's Official Language Commission and Parliamentary Committee (B-4); Art. 345 = State Legislature adopts State official language(s) (C-1); Art. 351 = Union's duty to develop Hindi (D-3). Option 2 swaps 343 and 344, option 3 swaps 345 and 351, option 4 swaps 343 and 345.
68.tq: 343 Union, 344 Commission, 345 State, 351 directive to develop Hindi.
xs: **343-Hindi in Devanagari, 344-OL Commission, 345-State language, 351-develop Hindi** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Art. 345** lets the **State Legislature** adopt the State's official language(s); **Art. 351** draws on Sanskrit and Eighth Schedule languages.
xa: **Art. 346**: language between States and State-Union.
**Art. 350B**: **Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities**.
Eighth Schedule is linked to **Arts. 344(1) and 351**.

68.s: Language used for communication between one State and another State, or between a State and the Union, is dealt with under:
68.x: Article 346 concerns the language for communication between States and between a State and the Union.
68.tq: Use the functional subject of the Article—communication between governments—to identify the provision.
xs: Inter-State and State-Union language is **Article 346** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Art. 345** = State official language; **Art. 348** = language of SC, HCs and Acts (English).
xa: **Art. 349**: special procedure for language laws.
**Art. 350**: representations in any language.
**Art. 350A**: mother-tongue instruction at primary stage.

68.s:
Consider the following pairs:

Article — Subject
1. Article 348 — Language of the Supreme Court, High Courts and Acts
2. Article 349 — Special procedure for language laws
3. Article 350 — Representations for redress in any language
4. Article 350A — Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
68.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Articles 348 to 350A cover judicial and legislative language, special procedure, representations and primary-stage mother-tongue instruction respectively.
68.tq: Verify each neighbouring Article separately because the provisions form a closely spaced constitutional sequence.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
**348** = SC, HCs, Acts (English); **349** = special procedure; **350** = representations in any language; **350A** = mother-tongue instruction.
xa: **350B** = Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (**1957**, HQ **Allahabad**).
**351** = Union's duty to develop Hindi.
**344** = Official Language Commission.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 350A — Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
Article 350B — Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
Article 351 — Union’s duty to develop Hindi
Article 343 — Official language of the Union
68.x: Article 350B provides for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities. Article 350A concerns facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage.
68.tq: Use the neighbouring-Article trap by distinguishing 350A from 350B.
xs: **Article 350A — Special Officer** is wrong — option **(1)** is correct.
The Special Officer is under **Art. 350B**; **350A** = **mother-tongue instruction at primary stage**.
**351** (develop Hindi) and **343** (Union language) are correct.
xa: Special Officer office set up **1957**, HQ **Allahabad**.
**Art. 345**: State official language.
**Art. 394A**: authoritative translation of the Constitution.

68.s: The office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities was set up in 1957 and has its headquarters at:
68.x: The office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities was set up in 1957, with its headquarters at Allahabad.
68.tq: Test the office-location association and reject nearby administrative centres.
xs: The **Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities** (**Art. 350B**) has HQ at **Allahabad** — option **(4)** is correct.
Office set up in **1957**.
xa: **Art. 350A**: **mother-tongue instruction** at primary stage.
**Art. 350**: representations in any language.
**Art. 351**: Union's duty to develop Hindi.

68.s: Which one of the following is the correct present list of languages added by the 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003?
68.x: The 92nd Amendment Act, 2003 added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule.
68.tq: Discriminate between the language groups added by the 71st and 92nd Amendments.
xs: The **92nd Amendment** (**2003**) added **Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali** = **71st** (**1992**); **Sindhi** = **21st** (**1967**); **Urdu** was original.
xa: ⚠ **21 – 71 – 92** = **Sindhi – Konkani/Manipuri/Nepali – Bodo/Dogri/Maithili/Santhali**.
Total now **22** (from **14**).
Last addition: **92nd Amendment** (**2003**).

68.s: The 96th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011 changed the name of which language in the Eighth Schedule?
68.x: The 96th Amendment changed the constitutional name of the language from Oriya to Odia. It did not add a new language to the Eighth Schedule.
68.tq: Distinguish a change in nomenclature from the addition of a language.
xs: The **96th Amendment** (**2011**) changed "**Oriya**" to "**Odia**" — option **(3)** is correct.
It renamed a language already in the Schedule; it did not add one.
xa: Odia became **classical** in **2014**.
Odia was in the original **14** (**1950**).
Eighth Schedule: **14** originally, **22** now.

68.s:
Consider the following statements about inclusion in the Eighth Schedule:
1. There are no fixed criteria for inclusion of a language.
2. The Ashok Pahwa Committee was constituted in 1996.
3. The Sitakant Mohapatra Committee was constituted in 2003.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: All three statements are correct. No fixed constitutional criteria exist for inclusion, and the Ashok Pahwa and Sitakant Mohapatra Committees are associated with the years 1996 and 2003 respectively.
68.tq: Check both the general rule and the committee-year pairings.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
There are **no fixed criteria** despite the **Ashok Pahwa** (**1996**) and **Sitakant Mohapatra** (**2003**) committees.
xa: Pending demands: **Bhojpuri, Kokborok, Khasi and Garo, Gor Boli**.
**99 languages** remain outside (**Jul 2025**).
Benefits: Sahitya Akademi recognition, **Art. 394A** translation, UPSC option.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs of languages is correctly matched with its status in the Eighth Schedule?
o: Kokborok and Bhojpuri — not included in the Eighth Schedule
Bhojpuri and Gor Boli — included in the original list of 14
Gor Boli and Kokborok — included by the 92nd Amendment
Bhojpuri and Santhali — both excluded from the Eighth Schedule
68.x: Kokborok and Bhojpuri are not included in the Eighth Schedule. Gor Boli, also known as Lambadi, is likewise not included.
68.tq: Separate constitutionally included languages from pending or excluded demands.
xs: **Kokborok and Bhojpuri** are **not** in the Eighth Schedule — option **(1)** is correct.
**Gor Boli** is also pending; **Santhali** **was** added (**92nd**).
xa: PYQ: **Bhojpuri is NOT** in the Schedule, but **Nepali, Dogri, Bodo** are (UPPSC **2025**).
**English** has never been in the Schedule.
**Khasi and Garo** are also pending.

68.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Amendment)
A. 21st Amendment, 1967
B. 71st Amendment, 1992
C. 92nd Amendment, 2003
D. Original Schedule, 1950

List-II (Language addition or status)
1. Four languages added
2. Fourteen languages initially included
3. Sindhi added
4. Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali added

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
68.x: The 21st Amendment added Sindhi; the 71st added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; the 92nd added four languages; and the original Schedule contained 14 languages.
68.tq: Start with the sure amendment-language pair and complete the code.
xs: **21st-Sindhi, 71st-Konkani/Manipuri/Nepali, 92nd-four languages, 1950-fourteen** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **92nd** added **Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali**.
xa: **Sindhi** = **15th** scheduled language; first addition (**1967**).

68.s: Which of the following languages was included in the original Eighth Schedule in 1950?
68.x: Telugu was among the 14 languages included in the original Eighth Schedule in 1950. Sindhi, Konkani and Santhali were added later.
68.tq: Distinguish original scheduled languages from later additions.
xs: **Telugu** was in the **original** list of **14** (**1950**) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Sindhi** came by the **21st** (**1967**), **Konkani** the **71st** (**1992**), **Santhali** the **92nd** (**2003**).
xa: Original list also: Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tamil, **Urdu**.
Telugu: **classical since 2008**.
Telugu is **South-Central Dravidian**.

68.s: The Eighth Schedule is constitutionally linked with which of the following Articles?
68.x: The Eighth Schedule is linked to Article 344(1), concerning the Commission and Committee on official language, and Article 351, concerning promotion of Hindi.
68.tq: Use the constitutional-provision trap by separating linked Articles from other language provisions.
xs: The Eighth Schedule is linked with **Articles 344(1) and 351** — option **(1)** is correct.
**344** = Official Language Commission; **351** = Union's duty to develop Hindi drawing on **Eighth Schedule languages**.
xa: **Art. 394A**: authoritative translation — a benefit of inclusion.
**Art. 343**: Union language; **Art. 345**: State language.
Eighth Schedule: **14** originally, **22** now.

68.s: Which one of the following statements about English and the Eighth Schedule is correct?
o: English was included in the original Schedule but removed in 1992.
English has never been included in the Eighth Schedule.
English was added by the 92nd Amendment along with Santhali.
English is one of the 22 scheduled languages by convention.
68.x: English has never been included in the Eighth Schedule.
68.tq: Test the distinction between official use of English and its constitutional Schedule status.
xs: **English has never been** in the Eighth Schedule — option **(2)** is correct.
It is an official language of the Union with Hindi, but not a scheduled language.
xa: "**NOT** in the Eighth Schedule" PYQs: **Bhojpuri**, **English**.
**Official Languages Act, 1963** kept English after **1965**.
Meghalaya and **Nagaland** use **English** officially.

68.s: The 22 languages in the Eighth Schedule cover approximately what percentage of the population's mother tongues?
68.x: The 22 scheduled languages cover the mother tongues of approximately 96.71 percent of the population.
68.tq: Distinguish the current coverage figure from the earlier 91 percent figure.
xs: The **22** scheduled languages cover **96.71 percent** (**96.71%**) of mother tongues — option **(3)** is correct.
Earlier, **18** languages covered **91%** (before **2003**).
xa: **99 languages** remain outside (**Jul 2025**).
Hindi alone = **43.6%**.
Census **2011**: **121** languages.

68.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Khasi and Garo — not included in the Eighth Schedule
Kokborok — included in the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment
Gor Boli — spoken by Banjaras in several Indian States
68.x: Kokborok is not included in the Eighth Schedule and is among the languages for which inclusion has been demanded. The 92nd Amendment added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali.
68.tq: Find the wrongly matched inclusion claim among pending-demand languages.
xs: **Kokborok — included by the 92nd Amendment** is wrong — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kokborok** is a **pending** demand; the 92nd added **Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali**.
**Khasi and Garo** (not included), **Bhojpuri** (pending), **Gor Boli** (Banjaras) are correct.
xa: First-time Constitution editions in **Kokborok** and **Kashmiri** (**2026**).
**Tripura**'s CPI(M) opposed a **Devanagari** push for NE tribal languages.
Gor Boli demand concerns AP's **Banjara/Sugali** community.

68.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Gor Boli or Lambadi?
o: It is an Austroasiatic language written in Ol Chiki.
It is a Tibeto-Burman language confined to the North-East.
It is a Dravidian language with a widely standardised script of its own.
It is an Indo-Aryan language spoken by Banjaras and has no script of its own.
68.x: Gor Boli or Lambadi is Indo-Aryan, is spoken by Banjaras across several States, and has no script of its own.
68.tq: Separate language family, community, geographical spread and script.
xs: **Gor Boli (Lambadi)** is **Indo-Aryan**, spoken by **Banjaras**, with **no script of its own** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is written in **Telugu, Devanagari, Kannada**; **Ol Chiki** belongs to Santhali.
xa: Banjaras live in **AP, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Rajasthan**.
Demand for Eighth Schedule inclusion continues (**23 Jul 2026**).
**Halbi** is also Indo-Aryan.

68.s: Which of the following statements regarding recent constitutional editions is correct?
o: The first digital edition was released only in Bhojpuri and Gor Boli.
Only English and Hindi digital editions were released under Article 394A.
The President released a digital edition in Santhali, with first-time editions also in Kokborok and Kashmiri.
Digital editions of the Constitution were released in Santhali, Kokborok and Kashmiri for the first time in all three cases.
68.x: The President released digital editions of the Constitution in Santhali; first-time editions were also produced in Kokborok and Kashmiri.
68.tq: Distinguish the principal language from the languages receiving first-time editions.
xs: The President released a **digital Santhali** edition and **first-time** editions in **Kokborok** and **Kashmiri** — option **(3)** is correct.
Only Kokborok and Kashmiri were first-time; Santhali was a digital edition — so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Constitution also released in **Sindhi** (Devanagari + Persian scripts).
**Art. 394A**: authoritative translation of the Constitution.
Santhali script: **Ol Chiki**.

68.s: A language community seeks authoritative translation of the Constitution under Article 394A, interpretation in Parliament and central development funds. These are principally associated with:
o: Recognition as a non-scheduled Census language
Classification as a dialect under Hindi
Recognition by the People's Linguistic Survey alone
68.x: Interpretation in Parliament, authoritative constitutional translation under Article 394A and central development funds are stated benefits associated with Eighth Schedule inclusion.
68.tq: Apply the listed benefits to identify the relevant constitutional status.
xs: **Art. 394A** translation, Parliament interpretation and central funds come with **inclusion in the Eighth Schedule** — option **(3)** is correct.
Non-scheduled Census languages and PLSI listing give no such benefits.
xa: Other benefits: **Sahitya Akademi** recognition, option in the **UPSC** Indian-language paper.
**No fixed criteria** for inclusion.
**22** scheduled languages now.

68.s:
Arrange the following languages in chronological order of their recognition as classical languages of India:
A. Kannada
B. Sanskrit
C. Odia
D. Tamil
68.x: Tamil was recognised in 2004, Sanskrit in 2005, Kannada in 2008 and Odia in 2014.
68.tq: Fix the earliest and latest entries first, then place the intervening years.
xs: The correct order is **Tamil – Sanskrit – Kannada – Odia** (D, B, A, C) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Tamil** was the **first** classical language (**2004**), followed by **Sanskrit** (**2005**).
**Kannada** was recognised in **2008** (with Telugu) and **Odia** in **2014**.
xa: **Telugu** was recognised in **2008** together with Kannada; **Malayalam** in **2013**.
India now has **11** classical languages; **Pali and Prakrit** are the only ones **outside** the Eighth Schedule.
⚠ Trap: "Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Odia were all recognised in 2008" is **wrong**.
Classical status is granted by the **Government of India**.

68.s: Which one of the following is NOT among the criteria traditionally associated with the recognition of a classical language?
o: A rich ancient literary tradition regarded as heritage
High antiquity of early texts, generally 1,500 to 2,000 years old
A tradition that must be written exclusively in prose
68.x: The criteria relate to antiquity, a rich ancient literary tradition and originality; exclusive composition in prose is not a criterion.
68.tq: Find the option that reverses or distorts the exact wording of a formal criterion.
xs: A tradition **written exclusively in prose** is **not** a criterion — so option **(4)** is correct.

xa: The 2024 revision also added **epigraphic evidence** and dropped the **"original, not borrowed"** rule.

Statement 2: the **Kalamalla inscription (575 CE)** of the **Renati Cholas** is the first fully Telugu inscription — correct.

xa: Telugu is called the **"Italian of the East"**.
The **Coastal (Krishna-Godavari)** dialect is the base of **standard Telugu**.
Telugu has been **classical since 2008**.

68.s: Telugu is popularly known as the:
68.x: Telugu is popularly called the ‘Italian of the East’.

xs: Telugu is called the **"Italian of the East"** — so option **(1)** is correct.

xa: Earliest Telugu word: **"Nagabu"** (**Amaravati** inscription).

Telugu is the **4th** most spoken language (Census 2011), behind Hindi, Bengali and Marathi.

68.s: Deccani Urdu developed during the rule of the Qutb Shahis in a context where:
o: Telugu was the official language and Persian was spoken by the people
Urdu was the official language and Sanskrit was spoken by the people
Persian was the official language and Telugu was spoken by the people

xa: Today **Urdu** is AP's **second official language**, statewide since the **2022** amendment Act.
**AP State Urdu Academy** gives free computer training in **36 centres**.

68.s: Andhra Pradesh's Telugu Mahotsavam is intended to be held:
o: only when a new classical-language decision is taken
68.x: Andhra Pradesh has made Telugu Mahotsavam an annual event.

xs: Telugu Mahotsavam is held **annually** — AP made it an **annual event** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was announced at the **Undavalli Caves**, along with **Telugu Language Awards** on **29 Aug**.
xa: **29 August** is **Telugu Language Day**, Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy's birth anniversary.
**CESCT** (Classical Telugu centre) is now at **Nellore**.
Telugu has been a **classical language since 2008**.

68.s: Which language–tribe–family combination is correctly matched?
68.x: Sora is the language of the Savara and belongs to the Munda branch of the Austroasiatic family. Koya and Kuvi are Dravidian, while Lambadi is Indo-Aryan.
68.tq: Use a three-column match and eliminate by language-family reversal.
xs: **Sora – Savara – Munda (Austro-Asiatic)** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Koya** is **Dravidian**, not Indo-Aryan.
**Kui/Kuvi** (Kondh) is **Dravidian**, not Munda.
**Lambadi (Gor Boli)** is **Indo-Aryan**, not Dravidian.
xa: ⚠ **Kui** and **Koya** = Dravidian; **Savara** and **Ho** = Munda; **Halbi** and **Gor Boli** = Indo-Aryan.
**Savara** lives in the **Srikakulam-Vizianagaram hills**; it has rich folk literature.
**Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy** designed a script for Savara.

68.s:
Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy’s contribution to the Savara language included:
1. Designing a script for Savara.
2. Preparing Savara-Telugu dictionaries.
3. Preparing a Savara manual.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: Gidugu designed a script for Savara and prepared both Savara-Telugu dictionaries and a Savara manual.
68.tq: Combine several related contributions and verify each item before choosing the code.
xs: All three are correct — so option **(4)** "1, 2 and 3" is correct.
Gidugu **designed a script for Savara**.
He prepared **Savara-Telugu dictionaries** and a **Savara manual** — the **AP precedent**.
xa: He is the father of the **Vyavaharika/colloquial Telugu** movement.
**Savara (Sora)** is **Austro-Asiatic, Munda**, in the **Srikakulam-Vizianagaram hills**.
His birth anniversary **29 August** = **Telugu Language Day**.

68.s: Which Telugu dialect region is regarded as the base of standard Telugu?
o: Coastal Andhra, particularly the Krishna-Godavari region
68.x: The Coastal dialect region, especially the Krishna-Godavari area, is regarded as the base of standard Telugu.
68.tq: Match the dialect region with its linguistic significance.
xs: The **Coastal (Krishna-Godavari)** region is the base of **standard Telugu** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Rayalaseema**, **Kalinga/Uttarandhra** and **Telangana** are the other dialect regions.

Telugu = **"Italian of the East"**.

68.s: Which one of the following is the correct set of major Telugu dialect regions mentioned for Andhra Pradesh?
68.x: The major regions are Coastal, Rayalaseema, Kalinga/Uttarandhra and Telangana.
68.tq: Select the complete geographical classification while rejecting an inserted unrelated region.
xs: The regions are **Coastal, Rayalaseema, Kalinga/Uttarandhra and Telangana** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Konkan**, **Bundelkhand** and **Malwa** are not Telugu dialect regions.
xa: The **Coastal (Krishna-Godavari)** dialect is the **base of standard Telugu**.
**Kalinga/Uttarandhra** = **Srikakulam-Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam**.
Telugu is **South-Central Dravidian**.

68.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Tribal language of AP)
A. Koya
B. Savara (Sora)
C. Kui/Kuvi
D. Gadaba
List-II (Area)
1. AP-Odisha border hills
2. Godavari agency
3. Visakhapatnam-Vizianagaram agency
4. Srikakulam-Vizianagaram hills
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
68.x: Koya = Godavari agency (A-2); Savara = Srikakulam-Vizianagaram hills (B-4); Kui/Kuvi = AP-Odisha border hills (C-1); Gadaba = Visakhapatnam-Vizianagaram agency (D-3). Option 2 swaps Koya and Savara, option 3 swaps Kui and Gadaba, option 4 is wrong throughout.
68.tq: Koya-Godavari, Savara-Srikakulam, Kui-Odisha border, Gadaba-Visakhapatnam.
xs: **A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Koya** – **Godavari agency**; **Savara (Sora)** – **Srikakulam-Vizianagaram hills**.
**Kui/Kuvi** – **AP-Odisha border hills**; **Gadaba** – **Visakhapatnam-Vizianagaram agency**.
xa: ⚠ **Koya** and **Kui** = **Dravidian**; **Savara** = **Munda**.
**Gadaba** has **Munda (Gutob)** and **Dravidian (Ollari)** varieties.
Kui/Kuvi is spoken by the **Kandhas of Odisha** (Dongria Kondh).

68.s: Which statement regarding Gadaba is correct?
o: It is an Austro-Asiatic language confined to the Krishna delta.
It is a Dravidian language spoken only in the Godavari agency.
It has Munda Gutob and Dravidian Ollari varieties and is found in the Visakhapatnam-Vizianagaram agency.
It is exclusively an Indo-Aryan language of the Banjaras.
68.x: Gadaba includes Munda Gutob and Dravidian Ollari varieties and is associated with the Visakhapatnam-Vizianagaram agency.
68.tq: Avoid the exclusive-word trap and distinguish a language with multiple varieties from single-family languages.
xs: **Gadaba** has **Munda (Gutob)** and **Dravidian (Ollari)** varieties and is found in the **Visakhapatnam-Vizianagaram agency** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is not only Austro-Asiatic or only Dravidian; the **Godavari agency** language is **Koya**.
The **Indo-Aryan** language of the **Banjaras** is **Gor Boli (Lambadi)**.
xa: **Savara (Sora)** – Munda, Srikakulam-Vizianagaram hills.
**Kui/Kuvi** – Dravidian, AP-Odisha border hills.
AP agency languages: **Savara, Koya, Kui, Gadaba**.

68.s: Which of the following correctly represents the official-language arrangement mentioned for Andhra Pradesh?
o: Telugu as the major official language and Urdu as the second official language
Telugu as the only official language, with no provision for Urdu
Urdu as the major official language and Telugu as the second official language
Hindi as the major official language and Telugu as the second official language

xs: AP has **Telugu** as major official language and **Urdu** as **second official language** — so option **(1)** is correct.

Under the **Qutb Shahis**, **Persian** was official and **Telugu** was spoken by the people.

68.s: Which of the following correctly describes the recent debate concerning tribal languages of the North-East?
o: The Centre is encouraging the Devanagari script for tribal languages that do not have scripts, and Tripura's CPI(M) opposed the move.
The Centre is making Persian script compulsory for all North-Eastern tribal languages, and no political opposition was reported.
The Centre has withdrawn all script-related measures for North-Eastern tribal languages after opposition from Andhra Pradesh.
The Centre is replacing Devanagari with Ol Chiki for all North-Eastern tribal languages, and Tripura's CPI(M) supported the move.
68.x: The Centre has been pushing Devanagari for North-Eastern tribal languages without scripts, while Tripura's CPI(M) opposed the proposal.

xs: The Centre is pushing **Devanagari** for NE tribal languages **without scripts**, and **Tripura's CPI(M)** opposed it — so option **(1)** is correct.

The Constitution was released in **Sindhi** (Devanagari + Persian scripts) and digital **Santhali (Ol Chiki)**, **Kokborok**, **Kashmiri** editions.
**Kokborok** is still a **pending** Eighth Schedule demand.

o: Koya community of the North-Eastern region
Banjara or Sugali community of Andhra Pradesh

**Gor Boli (Lambadi)** is **Indo-Aryan**, spoken by **Banjaras** with **no native script**.
xa: It is written in **Telugu, Devanagari, Kannada** scripts.
The **Tribal Affairs Ministry** told Parliament the demand continues (**23 Jul 2026**).
Other pending demands: **Bhojpuri**, **Kokborok**, **Khasi and Garo**.

68.s: Which of the following issues is associated with the continuing dispute over language policy in India?
o: The replacement of Tamil by Sindhi as the first classical language
The abolition of all regional languages from education
The removal of Urdu as Andhra Pradesh's second official language

xs: The **three-language formula** is the continuing dispute (**Jun 2026**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Tamil** (**2004**) is still the **first classical language**; Sindhi was the **first addition** to the Eighth Schedule (**1967**).
**Urdu** remains AP's **second official language**.
xa: The formula comes from **NPE 1968**, after the **Kothari Commission**.
Other debates: **Hindi absorption** of Maithili, Braj, Awadhi; Census **10,000**-speaker cut-off.
Opposition to the **Devanagari push** for NE tribal languages.

68.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the tribal languages associated with the agency areas of Andhra Pradesh?
68.x: Savara, Koya and Kui are associated with the agency areas of Andhra Pradesh. Kokborok is mentioned in connection with a digital constitutional edition, not the listed agency-area languages of Andhra Pradesh.

xs: **Kokborok** is not an AP agency language — so option **(1)** is correct.
AP's agency languages are **Savara, Koya, Kui, Gadaba**.
Kokborok figures in the **first-time Constitution editions** (2026) and is a **pending** Eighth Schedule demand.
xa: **Koya** – Dravidian, **Godavari agency**; **Savara** – Munda, **Srikakulam-Vizianagaram hills**.
**Kui/Kuvi** – Dravidian, **AP-Odisha border hills**.
**Gadaba** – Munda (**Gutob**) and Dravidian (**Ollari**) varieties, **Visakhapatnam-Vizianagaram agency**.
**Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy** documented **Savara (Sora)** and designed its script.

68.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Telugu Language Act
B. Addition of Sindhi to the Eighth Schedule
C. Recognition of Tamil as the first classical language
D. Recognition of Telugu as a classical language

Select the correct sequence.
68.x: The correct sequence is 1966 Telugu Language Act, 1967 addition of Sindhi, 2004 recognition of Tamil as the first classical language, and 2008 recognition of Telugu as classical.

xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Telugu Language Act** – **1966**; **Sindhi** added to the Eighth Schedule – **1967** (21st Amendment).
**Tamil** first classical language – **2004**; **Telugu** classical – **2008**.

**Sanskrit** became classical in **2005**; **Kannada** alongside Telugu in **2008**.
**71st Amendment (1992)** added **Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali**.

68.s: Which law made Telugu the official language of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Andhra Pradesh Official Language Act, 1966
The Andhra Pradesh Official Language Act, 1956
68.x: The Andhra Pradesh Official Language Act, 1966 made Telugu the official language of the State.
68.tq: Match the language policy with its exact Act and year.
xs: The **Andhra Pradesh Official Language Act, 1966** made Telugu the official language — so option **(1)** is correct.
The notes link Telugu to the **1966 Act**; **2008** is the year Telugu became **classical**, not of any Act.
xa: **Urdu** is the **second official language**; the **AP Official Languages (Amendment) Act, 2022** extended it to the whole state.

**CESCT** (Classical Telugu) is at **Nellore**.

69.s: Which one of the following is an internal migration?
o: Movement of a refugee across an international border
Movement of an illegal immigrant into another country
Movement from one Indian state to another
Movement from India to the United Arab Emirates
69.x: Internal migration takes place within a country, including movement between states, districts, towns and villages. The other examples involve international migration.
69.tq: Apply the administrative-boundary test to distinguish internal and international migration.
xs: **Movement from one Indian state to another** is **internal migration** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Internal migration is **within the country**: between **states, districts, towns, villages**.
**Refugees**, **illegal immigrants** and moves from India to the **UAE** cross borders — they are **international** migration.
xa: Classification by **administrative boundary** gives **internal / international**.
International migration includes **legal immigrants, illegal immigrants and refugees**.
Census 2011 counted **over 4.1 crore inter-state migrants**.

69.s: Harvest labour migration is generally an example of:
69.x: Migration associated with harvest labour is generally temporary or seasonal because it is linked to a recurring period of agricultural work.
69.tq: Use the duration of stay and the agricultural context to identify the migration type.
xs: Harvest labour is **seasonal or temporary migration** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Classification by **time** gives **temporary/seasonal** (e.g. **harvest labour**) and **permanent**.
**Return migration** is going back once the cause is over — not the same as seasonal work.
xa: **Seasonal labour** migration is typical of **drought-prone Rayalaseema** and **north-coastal** AP districts.

**Srikakulam fishermen** migrate to the **Gujarat coast**.

69.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Basis)
a. Distance
b. Number
c. Cause
d. Will

List-II (Classification)
i. Individual or mass
ii. Economic, social, political or religious
iii. Voluntary or forced
iv. Short-distance or long-distance

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
69.x: Distance corresponds to short- or long-distance migration; number to individual or mass; cause to economic, social, political or religious; and will to voluntary or forced.
69.tq: Start from the sure pair and match each classification with its stated basis.
xs: **a–iv, b–i, c–ii, d–iii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Distance** – long-/short-distance; **Number** – individual/mass.
**Cause** – economic, social, political, religious; **Will** – voluntary/forced.
xa: **Time** – temporary/**seasonal** or permanent, plus **return migration**.
**Administrative boundary** – **internal** or **international**.
**Voluntary** migration weighs **push and pull factors**; **forced** = persecution, development-induced displacement, exploitation.

69.s: A person who leaves a place because of persecution based on race, religion, nationality or membership of a social or political group, and cannot return safely, is called a:
69.x: A refugee is forced to leave and cannot return because of fear of persecution based on race, religion, nationality or social or political group.
69.tq: Identify the precise legal-social definition from its cause and inability to return.
xs: Such a person is a **Refugee** — so option **(4)** is correct.
A refugee is **forced to leave** and **cannot return** for fear of **persecution** (race, religion, nationality, social/political group).
A **voluntary migrant** weighs push and pull factors; a **return migrant** goes back once the cause is over.
xa: Refugees are a part of **international** migration with legal and illegal immigrants.
**World Migration Report 2026** (**IOM**): forced displacement of more than **120 million**.
Disasters caused **65.8 million** internal displacements.

69.s: Which one of the following is NOT a form of forced migration identified in the classification of migration by will?
69.x: Weighing push and pull factors is associated with voluntary migration. Persecution, development-induced displacement and exploitation are causes of forced migration.
69.tq: Find the one item belonging to voluntary rather than forced migration.
xs: **Weighing push and pull factors** is **voluntary**, not forced, migration — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Forced** migration = **persecution**, **development-induced displacement**, **exploitation**.
xa: Push factors at origin: **low farm productivity**, **monsoon failure**, drought, rural unemployment.
Pull factors at destination: **jobs, higher wages**, education, health care.
**Push-pull theory** – **Everett S. Lee** ("A Theory of Migration", **1966**).

69.s: Return migration refers to:
o: Permanent movement across an international boundary
Going back to the original place once the cause of migration is over
Movement from a village to a town for the first time
69.x: Return migration means going back to the previous place after the cause that led to migration has ended.
69.tq: Use the sequence of departure, end of cause and return to identify the concept.
xs: **Return migration** = **going back once the cause is over** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It falls under classification by **time**, with temporary/seasonal and permanent migration.
**Forced movement due to persecution** describes forced migration/refugees.
xa: **Urban to rural** is the **smallest** stream, seen in special cases like **return** and **retirement**.
**Counter-urbanisation** = movement from **urban to rural** areas.
**2026**: **rising LPG prices** pushed migrants back to villages.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about how migrants are identified in India:
1. The Census place-of-birth method identifies lifetime migrants.
2. The Census identifies migrants only by place of birth.
3. PLFS/NSO take the Usual Place of Residence as a place where the person has lived for at least 6 months.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Statement 1 is correct: place of birth gives lifetime migrants. Statement 2 is wrong: the Census also uses place of last residence. Statement 3 is correct: the PLFS/NSO Usual Place of Residence rule is at least 6 months. So '1 only' misses statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 2; '1 and 3 only' is right.
69.tq: Census has two yardsticks (birth and last residence); 'only' makes statement 2 false.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: the **place of birth** method gives **lifetime migrants** — correct.
Statement 2 is wrong: the Census also uses **place of last residence**.
Statement 3: **PLFS/NSO Usual Place of Residence** = lived at least **6 months** — correct.
xa: Census 2011: **455.8 million** migrants by **place of last residence** (about **37.6%**).
The **MoSPI** survey also uses the **6-month** UPR rule.
**Census 2027** will also record migration.

69.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Internal migration — between villages, towns, districts or states
Permanent migration — classification by administrative boundary
International migration — legal immigrants, illegal immigrants and refugees
69.x: Permanent migration is a classification by time, not by administrative boundary. Administrative boundary distinguishes internal and international migration.

xs: **Permanent migration** is classified by **time**, not administrative boundary — so option **(3)** is the wrong match.
**Administrative boundary** gives **internal** and **international** migration.
Mass migration – **number**; internal – between villages, towns, districts or states; international – **legal, illegal immigrants, refugees**: all correct.
xa: Time: **temporary/seasonal**, permanent, **return**.
Will: **voluntary / forced**.
Cause: **economic, social, political, religious**.

69.s: Which one of the following is the largest stream of internal migration in India?
69.x: Rural-to-rural migration is the largest stream of internal migration in India. It was also the stream contributing most to migration in 2011.
69.tq: Use the direct largest-share recall method and distinguish the dominant stream from urbanisation-linked migration.
xs: **Rural to rural** is the **largest stream** in India — so option **(1)** is correct.
It contributed most in **2011** (CGPSC 2018 PYQ) and is **female-dominated because of marriage**.
**Urban to rural** is the **smallest**; **rural to urban** is male, job-led.
xa: ⚠ UPPSC 2017: "rural-urban is the largest share" = **false**; "rural-rural is mainly female (marriage)" = **true**.

**Urban to urban** is typical of **developed** countries (**USA, Japan**).

69.s: Rural-to-urban migration in India is generally characterised by which one of the following combinations?
o: Male movement for employment and growth of urbanisation
Female movement for marriage and declining urbanisation
International movement of skilled workers and suburbanisation
Retired persons moving to villages and rural rejuvenation

**Female movement for marriage** marks **rural-to-rural** migration.

69.s: Urban-to-urban migration is especially typical of which of the following countries mentioned in the context of migration streams?
69.x: Urban-to-urban migration is identified as typical of developed countries such as the USA and Japan.
69.tq: Use the country-example association to distinguish developed-country urban migration patterns.
xs: Urban-to-urban migration is typical of **developed countries** like the **USA and Japan** — so option **(3)** is correct.

69.s: Which one of the following is the most appropriate description of urban-to-rural migration in India?
o: A small stream occurring in circumstances such as return migration or retirement
A stream dominated by inter-state male employment migration
The largest stream, caused mainly by marriage
A stream found exclusively in developed countries

xs: Urban-to-rural is the **smallest** stream, in **special circumstances** like **return migration or retirement** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Inter-state male employment** migration is **rural to urban**.
The **largest** stream, caused by **marriage**, is **rural to rural**.
xa: **Counter-urbanisation** = movement from **urban to rural** areas.
**Urban to urban** – typical of **USA, Japan**.
**2026**: **rising LPG prices** pushed migrants back to villages.

69.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the gender pattern in intra-state and inter-state migration?
o: Intra-state rural-to-urban migration is dominated by men, whereas inter-state rural-to-rural migration is dominated by women.
Intra-state rural-to-rural migration is dominated by women, whereas inter-state rural-to-urban migration is dominated by men.

Both intra-state and inter-state migration are dominated by men in urban-to-rural movements.
