77.s:
Assertion (A): Flash floods in Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada are linked to urban environmental and drainage problems.
Reason (R): Loss of wetlands and blocked drains reduce the capacity of urban areas to absorb and convey excess water.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
77.x: Both statements are true, and the loss of wetlands and blocked drains directly explain the increased flood vulnerability of the two cities.
77.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the urban-flood assertion.
xs: **A** is true: **flash floods** in **Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada** stem from urban drainage problems.
**R** is true and is the correct **explanation** of A: **lost wetlands + blocked drains** cause the flash floods — so option **(1)** is correct.
xa: Other causes: **unplanned growth** and **concretisation**.
Vijayawada floods are linked to the **Budameru** rivulet.
The AI flood-forecasting system is by **RTGS + APSDMA + IIT Gandhinagar**.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the present construction of the Human Development Index?
o: Arithmetic mean of health, education and employment indices
Geometric mean of health, education and income indices
Geometric mean of health, agriculture and expenditure indices
Weighted mean of literacy, poverty and urbanisation indices
78.x: Since 2010, the HDI has used the geometric mean of health, education and income dimensions.
78.tq: Confusable-concept discrimination between arithmetic and geometric means.
xs: Since **2010**, HDI is the **geometric mean** of **health, education and income** indices — so option **(2)** is correct.
Employment, agriculture, expenditure, literacy, poverty and urbanisation are not HDI dimensions.
xa: Health = **life expectancy**; education = **mean + expected years of schooling**; income = **GNI per capita, PPP, log**.
HDI comes from **UNDP**; first HDR in **1990**.
Conceived by **Mahbub ul Haq** with **Amartya Sen**.

78.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the components of the Human Development Index:
1. Health is represented by life expectancy.
2. Education includes mean years and expected years of schooling.
3. Income is measured through GNI per capita based on PPP and logarithmic transformation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements correctly describe the health, education and income components of the HDI.
78.tq: Statement combination testing a definition and its component details.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **health** = **life expectancy**.
Statement 2 is correct: **education** = **mean + expected years of schooling**.
Statement 3 is correct: **income** = **GNI per capita, PPP, log** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: The three indices are combined by a **geometric mean** (since **2010**).
⚠ HDI hides intra-state inequality → hence **IHDI** and district-level indices.

xa: ⚠ Lowest literacy = **ASR**, but lowest population, urbanisation and density = **Polavaram**.
AP does better on health (**MMR 30, IMR 19**) than on literacy.

78.s: With reference to the population density of the old 13 districts of Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following is correct?
o: Prakasam had the highest density, while Krishna had a density below 200.
Krishna had the highest density, while YSR Kadapa and Prakasam had densities below 200.
YSR Kadapa had the highest density, while Krishna had the lowest density.
All the three districts had densities above 500.
78.x: Krishna had the highest density at 518, whereas YSR Kadapa and Prakasam had densities below 200.
78.tq: Test the highest-and-lowest comparison within a local administrative region.
xs: In the old 13 districts, **Krishna** had the highest density (**518**), while **YSR Kadapa and Prakasam** were **below 200** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The other options swap the highest and lowest districts.
xa: In the 28-district map, **Visakhapatnam (1,870)** is densest and **Polavaram (54)** least dense.
Most populous of the 28: **SPSR Nellore**.

78.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Talliki Vandanam:
1. It is described as the successor to Amma Vodi.
2. It covers children studying in Classes 1 to 12.
3. It is restricted to government schools and excludes private schools.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: Talliki Vandanam is the successor to Amma Vodi and covers Classes 1 to 12 in government and private schools. Statement 3 is false because private schools are also covered.
78.tq: Find the reversed coverage statement; the word “restricted” is the trap.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Talliki Vandanam** succeeded **Amma Vodi**.
Statement 2 is correct: it covers **Classes 1-12**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it covers **government + private schools** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Benefit: **₹15,000 per child per year** to the mother, from **2025-26**.
**₹10,090 crore** paid to mothers of **67.27 lakh** students.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva?
o: A school assistance scheme providing ₹15,000 per child per year
A district development programme covering 112 districts and 49 indicators
A housing scheme covering 7.60 lakh houses through PMAY convergence
A cashless healthcare scheme covering 1.43 crore families and 3,257 procedures
78.x: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva, formerly Aarogyasri, provides cashless care to 1.43 crore families and covers 3,257 procedures.
78.tq: Use the renamed-scheme trap and match the scheme with its distinctive coverage figures.
xs: **Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva** (former **Aarogyasri**) gives **cashless care** to **1.43 crore families**, covering **3,257 procedures** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **₹15,000 per child per year** scheme is **Talliki Vandanam**, not Vaidya Seva.
xa: AP Budget 2026-27 gives Vaidya Seva **₹4,000 crore**.
AP's health figures: **MMR 30**, **IMR 19**.

78.s: In the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27, the allocation mentioned for Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva is:
78.x: The AP Budget 2026-27 allocation mentioned for Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva is ₹4,000 crore.
78.tq: Test the budget figure separately from the scheme’s beneficiary and procedure counts.
xs: AP Budget **2026-27** allots **₹4,000 crore** to **Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The notes give no other allocation for the scheme.
xa: It covers **1.43 crore families** and **3,257 procedures**.
Vaidya Seva is the former **Aarogyasri**.

78.s:
With reference to Talliki Vandanam, consider the following statements:
1. It benefits the mother of every school-going child studying in a government or private school.
2. The assistance is ₹15,000 per child per year.
3. The assistance is calculated per mother irrespective of the number of children.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: Talliki Vandanam provides ₹15,000 per school-going child per year to the mother. Unlike Amma Vodi, it is calculated per child, not per mother.
78.tq: Separate the closely related per-child and per-mother designs to detect the reversed comparison.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the mother of every child in **government or private** school benefits.
Statement 2 is correct: **₹15,000 per child per year**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the amount is **per child**, not per mother — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Covers **Classes 1-12**, from **2025-26**.
**₹10,090 crore** to mothers of **67.27 lakh** students (1 Jan 2026).

78.s: In the March 2026 Aspirational Districts Programme rankings, which Andhra Pradesh district stood first in India in the Basic Infrastructure theme?
78.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju district stood first in India in the Basic Infrastructure theme in the March 2026 ADP rankings.
78.tq: Match the district with the specific ADP theme and ranking distinction.
xs: **Alluri Sitarama Raju (ASR)** topped the **ADP Basic Infrastructure** theme (Mar 2026 rankings) — so option **(1)** is correct.
The notes name no other AP district for this ranking.
xa: ⚠ ASR also has AP's **lowest literacy** (**44.67%**).
Lowest population, urbanisation and density in the 28-district map: **Polavaram**.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the cited human-development indicators of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Health indicators are weaker than literacy, with MMR 44.67 and IMR 30
The State performs better on literacy, while MMR is 19 and IMR is 30
The State performs better on health, with MMR 30 and IMR 19, while the lowest district literacy is 44.67%
MMR, IMR and the lowest district literacy are all approximately 30
78.x: The comparative figures given are MMR 30 and IMR 19 for health, while the lowest district literacy figure cited is 44.67 percent, indicating relatively better performance on health than literacy.
78.tq: Check both the direction of comparison and the exact figures before selecting the option.
xs: AP does **better on health** (**MMR 30, IMR 19**) than on literacy (lowest district **ASR 44.67%**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (2) swaps MMR and IMR and wrongly says literacy is the stronger side.
xa: Highest district literacy: **Visakhapatnam (79.05%)**.
**Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva** covers **1.43 crore families**.

78.s: Why are IHDI and district-level indices considered useful alongside the Human Development Index in assessing Andhra Pradesh?
o: Because HDI hides inequality within a State
Because district-level indices measure only population size
Because IHDI replaces all district-level data with national averages
Because HDI measures only infrastructure and excludes health
78.x: HDI can conceal inequalities within a State; therefore, the Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index and district-level indices provide a more differentiated assessment.
78.tq: Apply the limitation of an aggregate index to the need for disaggregated measures.
xs: **HDI hides intra-state inequality**, hence **IHDI** and **district-level indices** — so option **(1)** is correct.
District indices show the gaps, e.g. literacy **79.05%** (Visakhapatnam) vs **44.67%** (ASR).
xa: HDI = **geometric mean** of health, education and income (since **2010**).
⚠ **Polavaram** is lowest in population, urbanisation and density.

79.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
79.x: Cement manufacturing is a secondary-sector activity. Transport is tertiary, research and development is quaternary, and top decision-making is quinary.
79.tq: Use the activity-to-sector match and watch for neighbouring-sector substitutions.
xs: **Cement manufacturing** is a **secondary sector** activity — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Transport** is **tertiary** (APPSC-GS 2018 key); **research and development** is **quaternary**; top government decision-making is **quinary**.
xa: Primary = **agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining and quarrying** (direct use of nature).
Quaternary also covers **IT, education, consulting** (knowledge).
Quinary workers are called "**gold collar**".

79.s: Top executives and top decision-makers in government and other institutions are associated with which sector?
79.x: The quinary sector comprises top decision-making activities, including government leadership and top executives. Such workers are also described as gold-collar workers.
79.tq: Distinguish the knowledge-producing quaternary sector from the decision-making quinary sector.
xs: Top executives and government decision-makers form the **Quinary sector** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its workers are called "**gold collar**".
**Quaternary** is knowledge work: **R&D, IT, education, consulting**.
xa: In developed countries, **quaternary + quinary** sectors are growing.
**Green collar** = environment and renewable-energy jobs.

79.s: Mining is classified differently in two commonly used contexts. Which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Mining is a secondary activity and has no separate weight in the IIP.
Mining is a primary activity, but GVA reporting places it in the broad Industry sector.
Mining is a quinary activity because it involves technical expertise.
Mining is a tertiary activity and is reported under services in GVA.
79.x: By the nature of the activity, mining is primary because it extracts resources from nature. In GVA reporting it is included in the broad Industry sector.
79.tq: Separate classification by activity from classification used in economic reporting.
xs: **Mining** is a **primary** activity, but **GVA reporting** places it in the broad **Industry** sector (AP Survey) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) is wrong: mining has its own weight in the revised **IIP** — **11.05%**.
xa: The **APPSC-G2 2008** key left this question unanswered.
Mining is an **extractive industry**, like capture fishing, hunting and lumbering.

79.s: Which of the following pairs represents the oldest primary activities?
79.x: Hunting and gathering are regarded as the oldest primary activities because they involve direct dependence on nature for subsistence.
79.tq: Identify the historically earliest activities through their direct dependence on nature.
xs: **Hunting and gathering** are the **oldest primary activities** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Manufacturing is secondary; banking and trade tertiary; research and consulting quaternary.
xa: **Extractive industries** take what nature provides: **mining, capture fishing, hunting, lumbering**.
**Genetic industries** breed plants and animals: **agriculture**, animal husbandry, fish farming.

79.s: Which one of the following is NOT an extractive industry?
79.x: Animal husbandry is a genetic industry because it involves breeding and rearing animals. Mining, capture fishing and lumbering take resources provided by nature and are extractive industries.
79.tq: Find the activity that involves breeding rather than extraction.
xs: **Animal husbandry** is a **genetic** industry (breeding animals), not extractive — so option **(2)** is the answer.
**Capture fishing, mining, lumbering** (and hunting) are **extractive** — they take what nature provides.
xa: Genetic industries: **agriculture**, animal husbandry, **fish farming** (UPPSC 2016 key: **Agriculture**).
⚠ **Capture fishing** = extractive, but **fish farming** = genetic.

79.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Agriculture — Genetic industry
b. Mining — Extractive industry
c. Fish farming — Genetic industry
d. Hunting — Extractive industry
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
79.x: Agriculture, fish farming and animal husbandry are genetic industries, while mining, capture fishing, hunting and lumbering are extractive industries. Therefore, all the listed pairs are correctly matched.
79.tq: Separate breeding-based genetic activities from nature-extracting activities.
xs: **Agriculture** and **fish farming** are **genetic** industries (breeding plants and animals).
**Mining** and **hunting** are **extractive** industries — so all four pairs match: **a, b, c and d**, option **(4)**.
xa: The oldest primary activities: **hunting and gathering**.
UPPSC 2016 key gave **Agriculture** as a genetic industry.

79.s:
Consider the following pairs of collar-colour terms and workers:
1. Red collar — Primary-sector outdoor workers
2. Blue collar — Office and professional service workers
3. Pink collar — Nursing, teaching and clerical jobs
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
79.x: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct: red collar means primary-sector outdoor workers and pink collar means service jobs long held mostly by women, such as nursing, teaching and clerical work. Pair 2 is wrong: blue collar means manual, factory and construction workers; office and professional workers are white collar. So A, C and D, which include pair 2, are wrong.
79.tq: Blue = manual/factory; white = office. Watch for the blue-white swap.
xs: Pair 1 is correct: **red collar** = primary-sector (outdoor) workers.
Pair 2 is wrong: **blue collar** = **manual, factory and construction** workers; office and professional workers are **white collar**.
Pair 3 is correct: **pink collar** = **nursing, teaching, clerical** jobs long held mostly by women — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Green collar** = environment and renewable-energy jobs; **gold collar** = quinary decision-makers.
In **2025** the **UAE** overtook Saudi Arabia as the top destination for Indian blue-collar workers.

79.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the collar-colour term?
o: Green collar — Environment and renewable-energy jobs
Red collar — Office and professional services
79.x: Green-collar work is associated with environmental protection and renewable energy. White-collar work refers to office and professional services, red-collar work to primary-sector outdoor activities, and gold-collar work to top decision-makers and experts.
79.tq: Use elimination by matching each colour with its occupational domain.
xs: **Green collar** = **environment and renewable-energy jobs** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**White collar** = office and professional services; **red collar** = primary-sector outdoor work; **gold collar** = top decision-makers and experts, not manual workers.
xa: **Blue collar** = manual, factory and construction workers.
**Pink collar** = nursing, teaching, clerical jobs.

79.s: In 2025, which country overtook Saudi Arabia as the top destination for Indian blue-collar workers?
79.x: The United Arab Emirates overtook Saudi Arabia in 2025 as the top destination for Indian blue-collar workers.
79.tq: Test the precise country in a current-affairs comparison.
xs: In **2025**, the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)** overtook **Saudi Arabia** as the top destination for Indian **blue-collar** workers — so option **(4)** is correct.
The notes do not name Qatar, Oman or Kuwait in this context.
xa: **Blue collar** = manual, factory and construction workers.
**White collar** = office and professional service workers.

79.s: Which of the following is a characteristic of the organised sector?
o: Registration, regular terms and application of labour laws
Irregular payment and absence of security
No minimum-wage provisions under any circumstances
79.x: The organised sector consists of registered establishments with regular terms of employment and applicable labour laws, including provisions related to PF, minimum wages and leave.
79.tq: Identify the regulated and registered side of the organised–unorganised distinction.
xs: The **organised sector** means **registration, regular terms** and **labour laws** (PF, minimum wages, leave) — so option **(1)** is correct.
Small scattered units, irregular pay and no security describe the **unorganised** sector.
xa: This is the standard **NCERT** distinction.
**Public vs private** is a different split, based on **ownership**.
**e-Shram**: **31 crore+** registered unorganised workers.

79.s:
Consider the following statements about the unorganised sector:
1. It commonly consists of small and scattered units.
2. Its workers may face irregular pay and lack of social security.
3. It is defined primarily by public ownership rather than by regulation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: Small scattered units, irregular pay and lack of security are features of the unorganised sector. Public versus private is a separate classification based on ownership, not the organised–unorganised distinction.
79.tq: Reject the ownership-based confusion and retain the regulatory characteristics.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the unorganised sector has **small scattered units**, **irregular pay** and **no security**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **ownership** defines **public vs private**, not organised vs unorganised — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: AP informal employment: **62.3% rural** vs **45.6% urban** (AP Survey 2025-26).
**e-Shram**: **54%** of registered workers are women.

79.s: Public-sector and private-sector classification is primarily based on
79.x: Public versus private is a separate sectoral division based on ownership. Organised versus unorganised classification is primarily concerned with registration, regulation and employment conditions.
79.tq: Distinguish two classifications that use the word ‘sector’ but have different bases.
xs: **Public vs private** is based on the **ownership** of the enterprise — so option **(2)** is correct.
Whether **labour laws apply** decides **organised vs unorganised**, a different split.
xa: Organised = registered, regular terms, **PF, minimum wages, leave**.
Unorganised = small scattered units outside regulation.

79.s: As of January 2026, the e-Shram portal had registered over 31 crore unorganised workers. Roughly what share of them are women?
79.x: About 54 per cent of the 31 crore+ workers registered on e-Shram are women. The other percentages are not the cited figure.
79.tq: e-Shram: 31 crore+ unorganised workers, 54% women.
xs: About **54 per cent** of the **31 crore+** e-Shram registrants are **women** (Jan 2026) — so option **(3)** is correct.
The notes cite no other share.
xa: AP informal employment: **62.3%** rural, **45.6%** urban.
⚠ **45.6%** is also AP's **agriculture employment** share.

79.s: Who proposed the 1935 part of the Fisher-Clark thesis?
79.x: Allan Fisher advanced the thesis in 1935, while Colin Clark developed the argument further in 1940.
79.tq: Use the author-year association to separate the two contributors.
xs: **Allan Fisher** proposed the thesis in **1935**; **Colin Clark** followed in **1940** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Colin Clark is the **1940** half, not the 1935 one.
xa: **Fisher-Clark thesis**: as income rises, labour and output move **primary → secondary → tertiary**.
⚠ India's deviation is called **premature deindustrialisation**.

79.s: The Fisher-Clark thesis describes structural transformation as the movement of labour and output from
79.x: The thesis states that as income rises, labour and output generally move from the primary sector to the secondary sector and then to the tertiary sector.
79.tq: Test the direction of structural transformation as an ordered sequence.
xs: The **Fisher-Clark thesis**: as income rises, labour and output move **primary to secondary to tertiary** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (4) reverses the order.
xa: Proposed by **Allan Fisher (1935)** and **Colin Clark (1940)**.
Developed countries: services ≈ **70-80% of GDP** (World Bank).

79.s: India’s experience of ‘premature deindustrialisation’ refers primarily to the fact that India
o: moved directly from agriculture to a large manufacturing base
skipped the mass factory-job stage to a considerable extent
79.x: Premature deindustrialisation indicates that India did not pass through a large mass factory-employment phase before the expansion of services.
79.tq: Apply the concept to the structural sequence rather than interpreting the term literally.
xs: **Premature deindustrialisation** means India **skipped the mass factory-job stage** — so option **(4)** is correct.
India has only **2.9%** of global **manufacturing value added**.
xa: Counterpoint: organised manufacturing jobs rose **6% in FY24** (about **10 lakh**) (Economic Survey 2025-26).
AP's manufacturing is about **11% of GSDP** — the "**missing middle**".

79.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh’s structural transformation:
1. Andhra Pradesh has a services-led economy.
2. Manufacturing accounts for only about 11 per cent of GSDP.
3. Industrial Policy 4.0 for 2024–29 seeks to help fill the manufacturing gap.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: AP is described as services-led, with manufacturing at about 11% of GSDP. Industrial Policy 4.0 for 2024–29 is intended to address this ‘missing middle’.
79.tq: Combine the structural diagnosis, numerical share and policy response.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: AP is **services-led**.
Statement 2 is correct: manufacturing is only about **11% of GSDP**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Industrial Policy 4.0 (2024-29)** aims to fill this "**missing middle**" — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: AP GVA 2025-26: agriculture **33%**, industry **24%**, services **43%**.
India's manufacturing = **14.7%** of the economy (new GDP series).

79.s: In developed countries, services generally account for approximately what share of GDP?
79.x: Services account for about 70–80% of GDP in developed countries, while quaternary and quinary activities are also growing.
79.tq: Match the country-development category with its characteristic sectoral range.
xs: In **developed countries**, services are about **70-80% of GDP** (World Bank) — so option **(4)** is correct.
Their **quaternary + quinary** sectors are also growing.
xa: India's services share of GVA: **52.9%** (2024-25).
AP's services share of GVA: **43%** (2025-26).

79.s: Which one of the following best describes the sectoral pattern of developing countries?
o: Services account for 70–80% of GDP in every developing country.
Quinary activities dominate employment and primary activities are negligible.
The primary sector remains large in employment, while services are growing faster than industry.
Industry always grows faster than services.
79.x: Developing countries generally retain a large primary-sector employment share, while their services sector is growing faster than industry.
79.tq: Contrast the employment structure and growth trend of developing countries with developed countries.
xs: In developing countries the **primary sector remains large in employment**, while **services grow faster than industry** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **70-80%** services share applies to **developed** countries, not every developing one.
xa: India and AP: **services lead in GVA, agriculture in jobs**.
About **46.1%** of India's workers are in agriculture.

79.s: Which sector accounted for the largest share of India’s GVA in 2024–25, on the new 2022–23 base?
79.x: The tertiary or services sector accounted for 52.9% of India’s GVA in 2024–25. The primary and secondary shares were 21.4% and 25.8% respectively.
79.tq: Match the sector with its correct GVA percentage rather than its employment share.
xs: The **tertiary sector** had the largest share of India's GVA in 2024-25: **52.9%** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Primary was **21.4%** and secondary **25.8%**.
**45.6%** is AP's **agriculture employment** share (PLFS 2023-24), not India's GVA.
xa: The base year moved to **2022-23** (Feb 2026).
AP's GVA: agriculture **33%**, industry **24%**, services **43%**.

79.s:
With reference to Andhra Pradesh’s GVA in 2025–26 at current prices, consider the following statements:
1. Agriculture and allied activities accounted for about 33 per cent.
2. Industry accounted for about 24 per cent.
3. Services accounted for about 43 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: The reported AP GVA shares were approximately 33% for agriculture and allied activities, 24% for industry and 43% for services.
79.tq: Check whether the three sectoral shares form the complete AP GVA distribution.
xs: All three are correct: AP GVA 2025-26 (current) = **agriculture 33%**, **industry 24%**, **services 43%** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
AP's agriculture share is well above India's **21.4%**.
xa: AP employment (PLFS 2023-24): **45.6%** agri, **22.8%** industry, **31.6%** services.
AP agriculture is led by **livestock + fisheries**.

79.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the broad sectoral pattern in both India and Andhra Pradesh?
o: Industry leads in both GVA and employment.
Agriculture leads in GVA, while services lead in employment.
Services lead in GVA, while agriculture leads in employment.
Services lead in both GVA and agriculture remains negligible in employment.
79.x: Services have the largest GVA share, whereas agriculture accounts for the largest share of employment in both India and Andhra Pradesh.
79.tq: Compare the leading sector in output with the leading sector in employment.
xs: In both India and AP, **services lead in GVA** while **agriculture leads in employment** — so option **(3)** is correct.
India: services **52.9%** of GVA; about **46.1%** of workers in agriculture.
AP: services **43%** of GVA; agriculture **45.6%** of employment.
xa: AP services employ only **31.6%** of workers.
e-Shram has **31 crore+** unorganised workers registered.

79.s: The new GDP series released in February 2026 is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: GDP levels 3–4% higher, manufacturing 21.4%, FY26 growth 6.2%
GDP levels 3–4% lower, manufacturing 14.7%, FY26 growth 7.6%
GDP levels unchanged, manufacturing 11%, FY26 growth 7.6%
GDP levels 3–4% lower, manufacturing 25.8%, FY26 growth 8.1%
79.x: The new GDP series placed GDP levels 3–4% lower, measured manufacturing at 14.7% of the economy and reported FY26 growth at 7.6%.
79.tq: Link several figures to the correct statistical series instead of mixing indicators.
xs: The **new GDP series (Feb 2026)**: GDP levels **3-4% lower**, manufacturing **14.7%**, FY26 growth **7.6%** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**21.4%** and **25.8%** are India's **primary** and **secondary** GVA shares; **11%** is **AP's** manufacturing share.
xa: Base year moved to **2022-23**.
The **IIP revision** added a **water supply and waste management** sector.

79.s: The base year of the GDP series was moved to
79.x: The GDP base year was moved to 2022–23 in the new series released in February 2026.
79.tq: Test the exact base year and avoid confusing it with the release year.
xs: The GDP base year was moved to **2022-23** (Feb 2026) — so option **(1)** is correct.
The notes cite no other base year for the new series.
xa: New series: GDP levels **3-4% lower**; FY26 growth **7.6%**.
India GVA 2024-25 on the new base: services **52.9%**.

79.s: Which new sector was added in the revision of the Index of Industrial Production mentioned in June 2026?
79.x: The revised IIP added a water supply and waste management sector. The other options are not the sector added in the cited revision.
79.tq: Identify the precise institutional change rather than a broadly related service activity.
xs: The **IIP revision** (Jun 2026) added a **water supply and waste management** sector — so option **(1)** is correct.
The notes name only **water supply and waste management** as the added sector.
xa: Mining's weight in the revised IIP: **11.05%**.
The GDP base year moved to **2022-23**.

79.s: Which statement best explains why Andhra Pradesh is described as more agrarian than India as a whole?
o: AP has no significant livestock or fisheries activity.
Agriculture contributes about 33% of AP GVA compared with about 21% nationally, with livestock and fisheries leading within AP agriculture and allied activities.
Agriculture contributes about 21% of AP GVA compared with about 33% nationally, while services are absent in AP.
Industry contributes 43% of AP GVA and agriculture contributes less than 10%.
79.x: Agriculture accounts for about 33% of AP GVA against about 21% nationally, and AP’s agricultural and allied sector is led by livestock and fisheries.
79.tq: Compare the two GVA shares and connect the state-level composition with the conclusion.
xs: AP is more agrarian: **agriculture ~33% of GVA vs ~21% nationally**, led by **livestock + fisheries** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses the figures; option (4) misstates **43%**, which is AP's **services** share.
xa: AP employment in agriculture: **45.6%** (PLFS 2023-24).
AP's manufacturing is only about **11% of GSDP**.

80.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the geographical origin of crops:
1. Coffee is included among the Old World crops.
2. Cocoa is included among the New World crops.
3. Rubber is included among the Old World crops.
4. Chilli is included among the New World crops.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: Coffee is an Old World crop, while cocoa, rubber and chilli are New World crops. Therefore, statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, whereas statement 3 is false.
80.tq: Split the statements by checking each crop against the Old World–New World classification.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **coffee** is an **Old World** crop.
Statements 2 and 4 are correct: **cocoa** and **chilli** are **New World (Americas)** crops.
Statement 3 is wrong: **rubber** is a **New World** crop — so **1, 2 and 4 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Old World: **wheat, barley, rice, sugarcane, tea, coffee**.
New World: **maize, potato, tomato, tobacco, cocoa, rubber, cassava, groundnut, chilli**.
This is the standard **Columbian-exchange** pattern.

80.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
80.x: Groundnut is a New World crop of the Americas, not an Old World crop. Rice and sugarcane are Old World crops, while tobacco is a New World crop.
80.tq: Find the single reversed classification in the crop-origin pairs.
xs: **Groundnut — Old World crop** is wrong: groundnut is a **New World (Americas)** crop — so option **(1)** is the answer.
**Rice** and **sugarcane** are Old World; **tobacco** is New World — correctly matched.
xa: Other New World crops: **maize, potato, tomato, cocoa, rubber, cassava, chilli**.
Other Old World crops: **wheat, barley, tea, coffee**.

80.s: Which of the following is the most appropriate description of plantation farming?
o: A single crop grown on estates with capital investment and an export orientation
Multiple crops grown on small plots mainly for family consumption
Nomadic livestock movement over seasonal pastures
Crops and livestock combined mainly in densely populated monsoon regions
80.x: Plantation farming is characterised by a single crop grown on estates with substantial capital and production mainly intended for export. Tea, rubber and coffee are examples.
80.tq: Distinguish plantation farming through its crop pattern, estate structure and market orientation.
xs: **Plantation** farming = **single crop**, **estates**, **capital**, **export** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Small plots for family use = **intensive subsistence**; crops plus livestock = **mixed** farming.
xa: Examples: **tea** (India, Sri Lanka), **rubber** (Malaysia), **coffee** (Brazil).
**Commercial grain** farming: mechanised, **extensive** wheat on the Prairies, Steppes, Pampas, Downs.

80.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Type of farming)
a. Plantation farming
b. Mixed farming
c. Commercial grain farming
d. Intensive subsistence farming

List-II (Characteristic region)
i. North-West Europe and eastern North America
ii. Monsoon Asia
iii. Prairies, Steppes, Pampas and Downs
iv. Malaysia, Brazil and India

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
80.x: Plantation farming is associated with Malaysia, Brazil and India; mixed farming with north-west Europe and eastern North America; commercial grain farming with the listed grassland regions; and intensive subsistence farming with monsoon Asia.
80.tq: Start with the distinctive plantation and mixed-farming pairs, then complete the code.
xs: **Plantation** — Malaysia, Brazil, India (iv); **Mixed** — NW Europe, eastern North America (i).
**Commercial grain** — Prairies, Steppes, Pampas, Downs (iii); **Intensive subsistence** — Monsoon Asia (ii) — so **a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii**, option **(1)**.
xa: Intensive subsistence: small plots, heavy labour, **high yield per ha** (wet paddy).
Commercial grain farming is **wheat**, mechanised and **extensive**.

80.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes intensive farming from extensive farming?
o: Intensive farming uses large areas with low input, whereas extensive farming uses small plots with high input.
Intensive farming uses high input per unit of land, whereas extensive farming uses large areas with relatively low input.
Extensive farming is confined to plantation estates, whereas intensive farming is confined to deserts.
Both systems necessarily use equal labour and capital per unit of land.
80.x: Intensive farming applies high labour and capital input to a unit of land, while extensive farming operates over larger areas with comparatively low input per unit of land.
80.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap by checking input per unit of land against area.
xs: **Intensive** = **high input per unit of land**; **extensive** = **large areas with low input** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the two.
xa: Intensive subsistence farming: **Monsoon Asia** (wet paddy).
Extensive commercial grain farming: **Prairies, Steppes, Pampas, Downs**.

80.s: Derwent Whittlesey’s classification of world agricultural regions, published in 1936, identified how many regions?
80.x: Derwent Whittlesey mapped 13 agricultural regions in 1936. His classification remains a standard reference in agricultural geography.
80.tq: Use the distinctive classification count and publication year as paired numerical clues.
xs: **Derwent Whittlesey (1936)** mapped **13** agricultural regions — so option **(3)** is correct.
**4** is the number of **macro agricultural regions of India** (**Sengupta and Sdasyuk**).
xa: Whittlesey's **Mediterranean** region: winter rain, **viticulture**, citrus, olives.
His **Oriental intensive** region: Monsoon Asia, wet paddy.

80.s:
Consider the following statements about Mediterranean agriculture in Whittlesey's scheme:
1. It is found in the Mediterranean basin, California, central Chile, the south-western Cape and south-western Australia.
2. These regions receive most of their rain in summer.
3. Viticulture, citrus fruits and olives are typical of this agriculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the listed areas form the Mediterranean region, and viticulture, citrus and olives are its typical crops. Statement 2 is wrong: Mediterranean regions get winter rain, not summer rain. So A, B and D, which include statement 2, are wrong.
80.tq: Mediterranean = winter rain + grapes, citrus, olives; the Prairies are not part of it.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Mediterranean basin, California, central Chile, the SW Cape and SW Australia**.
Statement 2 is wrong: these regions get **winter rain**, not summer rain.
Statement 3 is correct: **viticulture, citrus, olives** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: **Viticulture** = grape cultivation.
Whittlesey mapped **13** regions (**1936**).

80.s: Oriental intensive farming is primarily associated with which of the following regions and characteristics?
o: The Mediterranean basin; winter rainfall and olives
The Prairies; mechanised wheat and high output per worker
The Pampas; extensive cattle ranching and low labour input
Monsoon Asia; wet paddy, high output per hectare and low output per worker
80.x: Oriental intensive farming belongs to monsoon Asia. It is characterised by wet-paddy cultivation, high output per hectare and relatively low output per worker.
80.tq: Contrast output per hectare with output per worker to identify the oriental intensive system.
xs: **Oriental intensive** farming = **Monsoon Asia**, **wet paddy**, **high output per hectare, low output per worker** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Winter rain and olives = **Mediterranean**; mechanised wheat = **commercial grain** (Prairies).
xa: It matches the **intensive subsistence** type: small plots, heavy labour.
**IRRI** (Los Baños, Philippines, **1960**) released **IR8** "miracle rice".

80.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Vertical farming allows crops to be grown year-round in non-tropical regions.
2. Hydroponics is a soil-free method of growing crops.
3. Aquaponics combines hydroponics with fish rearing and is classed as an agroecological practice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: vertical farming permits year-round cropping in non-tropical regions (APPSC-GS 2021 key), and hydroponics is soil-free. Statement 3 is wrong: aquaponics does combine hydroponics with fish, but neither it nor hydroponics is agroecological (UPSC trap). So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' leaves out statement 2, and the options with statement 3 include a wrong statement.
80.tq: Hydroponics and aquaponics are NOT agroecological.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **vertical farming** allows **year-round crops in non-tropical regions** (APPSC-GS 2021 key).
Statement 2 is correct: **hydroponics** is **soil-free**.
Statement 3 is wrong: aquaponics = hydroponics + fish, but ⚠ **neither** is **agroecological** (UPSC) — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Permaculture** = self-sustaining ecological food systems.
**Organic farming** bans synthetic inputs + **GMOs**.

80.s: Which one of the following statements regarding world crop production is correct?
o: India is the leading producer of cocoa and Côte d’Ivoire occupies the second position.
Brazil is the leading producer of cocoa and India occupies the second position.
Côte d’Ivoire is the leading producer of cocoa and Ghana occupies the second position.
Ghana is the leading producer of cocoa and Côte d’Ivoire occupies the second position.
80.x: Côte d’Ivoire ranks first in cocoa production, followed by Ghana. Andhra Pradesh is identified as the leading cocoa-producing state in India.
80.tq: Separate the global ranking from the Indian state-level ranking.
xs: **Côte d'Ivoire** is 1st in **cocoa** and **Ghana** 2nd — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (4) swaps the two; **India** and **Brazil** are not the cocoa leaders.
xa: **AP is 1st in India** in cocoa.
AP is also 1st in **oil palm, papaya, chillies**.

80.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Brazil is the leading producer of sugarcane.
2. India ranks second in sugarcane production.
3. India is both the largest producer and consumer of sugar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: Brazil is the first producer of sugarcane, India is second, and India is described as the largest producer and consumer of sugar.
80.tq: Combine production rank with the separate producer-consumer distinction.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Brazil** is 1st in **sugarcane**.
Statement 2 is correct: **India** is 2nd.
Statement 3 is correct: India is the **largest producer and consumer of sugar** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: India has a **virtual world monopoly** in **castor**.
**Sugarcane** is an **Old World** crop.

80.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding India’s position in selected agricultural commodities?
o: India is the fourth producer of tea and the second producer of natural rubber.
India is the first producer of tea and the seventh producer of coffee.
India is the seventh producer of tea and the sixth producer of coffee.
India is the second producer of tea, the seventh producer of coffee and the sixth producer of natural rubber.
80.x: India ranks second in tea, seventh in coffee and sixth in natural rubber production. It is also the fourth-largest exporter of tea.
80.tq: Read the numerical ranks as a combined comparison rather than isolating one commodity.
xs: India is **2nd in tea**, **7th in coffee** and **6th in natural rubber** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**4th** is India's rank as a tea **exporter**; India is **2nd** in rubber **consumption**, not production.
xa: **Kerala** grows **70-75%** of India's rubber; **Karnataka 71%** of its coffee.
AP is **4th** in India in coffee (**Araku**).

80.s:
Consider the following statements about coffee varieties:
1. Robusta (Coffea canephora) is a hardier lowland coffee with more caffeine.
2. Arabica is a mild highland coffee that originated in Ethiopia.
3. Mocha is a Robusta coffee named after a port in Brazil.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Robusta is Coffea canephora, a hardier lowland coffee with more caffeine, and Arabica is a mild highland coffee from Ethiopia. Statement 3 is wrong: Mocha is an Arabica coffee named after the Yemeni port of Mocha. So B, C and D, which include statement 3, are wrong.
80.tq: Mocha = Arabica + Yemeni port; Robusta = canephora, lowland, more caffeine.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Robusta (Coffea canephora)** is a **hardier lowland** coffee with **more caffeine**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Arabica** is a mild **highland** coffee from **Ethiopia**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Mocha** is an **Arabica**, named after the **Yemeni** port of Mocha — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: India is the **7th** coffee producer; **Karnataka** grows **71%**.
AP is **4th** in India (**Araku**).

80.s: India has a virtual world monopoly in the production of which of the following crops?
80.x: India has a virtual world monopoly in castor. In cocoa Cote d'Ivoire and Ghana lead, and India is only 6th in natural rubber and 7th in coffee.
80.tq: Castor = India's near-monopoly crop.
xs: India has a **virtual world monopoly** in **castor** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Cocoa is led by **Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana**; India is **6th** in natural rubber and **7th** in coffee.
xa: India is **2nd** in tea and **2nd** in sugarcane.
India is the largest **producer and consumer of sugar**.

80.s:
Which of the following statements about the global Green Revolution is correct?
1. Norman Borlaug bred semi-dwarf wheat in Mexico.
2. The Rockefeller Foundation associated with this work was American.
3. Borlaug received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.
4. The term ‘Green Revolution’ was coined by William Gaud in 1968.
80.x: Norman Borlaug bred semi-dwarf wheat in Mexico with support from the American Rockefeller Foundation, received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970, and William Gaud coined the term in 1968.
80.tq: Link the pioneer, institutional support, award and terminology through their separate dates and places.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **Norman Borlaug** bred **semi-dwarf wheat** in **Mexico** with the **American** **Rockefeller Foundation** ("British" is WRONG).
Statement 3 is correct: Borlaug won the **Nobel Peace Prize in 1970**.
Statement 4 is correct: **William Gaud** coined "Green Revolution" in **1968** — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
xa: ⚠ Term **1968** (Gaud) vs Nobel **1970** (Borlaug).
India's key figures: **M.S. Swaminathan** and **C. Subramaniam**.

80.s: CIMMYT is primarily associated with research on which crops?
80.x: CIMMYT, located in Mexico, works mainly on maize and wheat. IRRI is the institute associated with rice research in the Philippines.
80.tq: Separate the two major Green Revolution institutes by their crop specialisation.
xs: **CIMMYT** (Mexico) works on **maize and wheat** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rice** research is **IRRI**'s domain (Los Baños, Philippines).
xa: CIMMYT's JV with **ICAR** = **BISA (2011)**, with stations in Punjab, MP, Bihar.
**Borlaug** bred semi-dwarf wheat in **Mexico**.

80.s: IRRI was established at Los Baños in the Philippines in 1960 and released which variety known as ‘miracle rice’?
80.x: The International Rice Research Institute (IRRI), established at Los Baños in the Philippines in 1960, released IR8, popularly called miracle rice.
80.tq: Combine the institute’s location and year with its signature crop variety.
xs: **IRRI** (Los Baños, Philippines, **1960**) released **IR8**, the "**miracle rice**" — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Arabica** is a coffee variety and **Coffea canephora** is Robusta coffee.
xa: **CIMMYT** (Mexico) works on **maize + wheat**.
Oriental intensive farming of Monsoon Asia rests on **wet paddy**.

80.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with India’s Green Revolution?
o: M. S. Swaminathan and C. Subramaniam — key Indian figures; Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh — core region
William Gaud and Norman Borlaug — key Indian figures; Kerala and Tamil Nadu — core region
J. C. Weaver and Bhatia — key Indian figures; eastern India — core region
Subhash Palekar and C. Subramaniam — key Indian figures; the Western Ghats — core region
80.x: M. S. Swaminathan and C. Subramaniam were key Indian figures in the Green Revolution, whose core region was Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.
80.tq: Match the national figures with the geographical core instead of the global pioneers.
xs: **M.S. Swaminathan + C. Subramaniam** were India's key Green Revolution figures; core = **Punjab, Haryana, western UP** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Gaud** and **Borlaug** are global figures, not Indian; **Weaver** and **Bhatia** are regionalisation geographers; **Palekar** pioneered **ZBNF**.
xa: **Borlaug** = father of the global Green Revolution (**Nobel Peace Prize 1970**).
**William Gaud** coined the term in **1968**.

80.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Integrated Pest Management — bio-pesticides, pheromone traps and natural predators
Natural farming — compulsory dependence on synthetic fertilisers and chemical pesticides
Organic farming — synthetic inputs and genetically modified organisms are avoided
80.x: Natural farming does not require compulsory dependence on synthetic fertilisers and chemical pesticides. Organic farming avoids synthetic inputs and GMOs, permaculture designs self-sustaining systems, and IPM combines biological and ecological controls.
80.tq: Find the option that reverses the defining principle of the practice.
xs: **Natural farming — compulsory dependence on synthetic fertilisers and chemical pesticides** is wrong — so option **(3)** is the answer.
Natural farming (e.g. **APCNF**) is **agro-ecological**; it does not rest on synthetic inputs.
**Permaculture**, **IPM** (bio-pesticides, **pheromone traps**, predators) and **organic farming** (no synthetic inputs, no **GMOs**) are correctly matched.
xa: Organic farming relies on **crop rotation + manures**.
**Subhash Palekar** pioneered **ZBNF**.

80.s: Who pioneered Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF)?
80.x: Subhash Palekar pioneered Zero Budget Natural Farming. It is distinct from the broader organic-farming framework and from the Green Revolution breeding programme.
80.tq: Use the person-practice association while distinguishing natural farming from organic farming and crop breeding.
xs: **Subhash Palekar** pioneered **Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Weaver** = crop combination; **Swaminathan** = Indian Green Revolution; **Borlaug** = semi-dwarf wheat.
xa: **APCNF**: **10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha** — world's largest agro-ecological programme.
**National Mission on Natural Farming**: **8.80 lakh ha** + **18.19 lakh** farmers by Mar 2026.

80.s: Which programme is described as the world's largest agro-ecological programme, covering about 10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh hectares?
80.x: APCNF (Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming) is the world's largest agro-ecological programme, with 10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha. The National Mission on Natural Farming is the national mission (8.80 lakh ha), and IPM is a pest-control approach, not a programme of that size.
80.tq: APCNF = world's largest agro-ecological programme.
xs: **APCNF** is the **world's largest agro-ecological programme**: **10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha** (Jul 2026) — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **National Mission on Natural Farming** is the national scheme: **8.80 lakh ha**, **18.19 lakh** farmers by Mar 2026.
**IPM** is a pest-control method (bio-pesticides, pheromone traps, predators), not a programme.
xa: **ZBNF** was pioneered by **Subhash Palekar**.
⚠ **Hydroponics** and **aquaponics** are not agroecological.

80.s: Who is associated with the crop-combination method of agricultural regionalisation introduced in 1954?
80.x: J. C. Weaver introduced the crop-combination method in 1954. Doi and Rafiullah subsequently modified the method.
80.tq: Associate the method with its principal geographer and retain the year as a differentiator.
xs: **J.C. Weaver (1954)** devised the **crop combination** method — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was later modified by **Doi** and **Rafiullah**.
**Bhatia** = diversification and concentration; **Kendall** = efficiency; **Sengupta** = macro regions of India.
xa: ⚠ **Bhatia** = both crop diversification and crop concentration.
**Sengupta and Sdasyuk** = **4** macro agricultural regions (APPSC-G1 2023 key).

80.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Method or index)
a. Crop diversification
b. Crop concentration
c. Agricultural efficiency
d. Four macro agricultural regions of India

List-II (Associated scholar or scholars)
i. Kendall, Enyedi and Shafi
ii. Sengupta and Sdasyuk
iii. Bhatia
iv. Bhatia and Jasbir Singh; Gibbs-Martin

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
80.x: Crop diversification is associated with Bhatia, Jasbir Singh and Gibbs-Martin; crop concentration with Bhatia; agricultural efficiency with Kendall, Enyedi and Shafi; and the four macro agricultural regions with Sengupta and Sdasyuk.
80.tq: Begin with the unique four-region association and verify the remaining method-scholar pairs.
xs: **Crop diversification** — Bhatia, Jasbir Singh; Gibbs-Martin (iv); **crop concentration** — Bhatia (iii).
**Agricultural efficiency** — Kendall, Enyedi, Shafi (i); **4 macro regions** — Sengupta and Sdasyuk (ii) — so **a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii**, option **(1)**.
xa: **Crop combination** = **J.C. Weaver (1954)**, modified by Doi and Rafiullah.
**Sengupta and Sdasyuk** was an APPSC-G1 **2023** key.

80.s: The ranking coefficient is associated with which method of agricultural regionalisation?
80.x: Kendall’s ranking coefficient is associated with the measurement of agricultural efficiency. Enyedi and Shafi are also linked with agricultural-efficiency studies.
80.tq: Match the technical index with the regionalisation method in which it is used.
xs: **Kendall**'s **ranking coefficient** measures **agricultural efficiency** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Enyedi** and **Shafi** also worked on agricultural efficiency.
Crop combination = **Weaver**; crop concentration = **Bhatia**; diversification = **Bhatia, Jasbir Singh**.
xa: ⚠ **Bhatia** appears under both concentration and diversification.
**Whittlesey (1936)** mapped **13** world agricultural regions.

80.s: The term ‘sericulture’ refers to:
o: Rearing of silkworms for silk production
Rearing of bees for honey production
80.x: Sericulture is the practice associated with silk production, particularly the rearing of silkworms. Floriculture, apiculture and pisciculture relate respectively to flowers, bees and fish.
80.tq: Discriminate among similar agriculture-related terms by linking each to its specific produce.
xs: **Sericulture** = **silk** (rearing of silkworms) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Flowers = **floriculture**; fish = **pisciculture**; bees = **apiculture**.
xa: **Viticulture** = grapes; **horticulture** = fruits, vegetables, flowers.
**Hydroponics** is soil-free; **aquaponics** = hydroponics + fish.

80.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Viticulture — Grapes
2. Floriculture — Flowers
3. Apiculture — Fish
4. Pisciculture — Bees
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
80.x: Viticulture means grape cultivation and floriculture means flower cultivation. Apiculture concerns bees, while pisciculture concerns fish; hence pairs 3 and 4 are interchanged and incorrect.
80.tq: Use confusable-pair discrimination to separate apiculture from pisciculture.
xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct: **viticulture = grapes**, **floriculture = flowers**.
Pairs 3 and 4 are swapped: **apiculture = bees**, **pisciculture = fish** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: **Sericulture** = silk.
**Horticulture** output (**362-367 MT**) now exceeds foodgrains (2026).

80.s: With reference to agricultural output in India, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Horticulture output is restricted to about 100 MT and remains below foodgrain output.
Foodgrain output has now exceeded horticulture output of 362–367 MT.
Horticulture and foodgrain output are reported to be exactly equal at 362–367 MT.
Horticulture output is now in the range of 362–367 MT and exceeds foodgrain output.
80.x: Horticulture output is stated to be approximately 362–367 million tonnes and has surpassed foodgrain output.
80.tq: Check both the quantitative range and the direction of comparison.
xs: **Horticulture** output is now **362-367 MT** and **exceeds foodgrain** output (2026) — so option **(4)** is correct.
Option (2) reverses the comparison.
xa: **AP** is India's **largest fruit producer**.
AP is 1st in **oil palm, papaya, cocoa, chillies**.

80.s: The United Nations has designated 2026 as the:
o: International Year of the Woman Farmer
International Year of Sustainable Rice Cultivation
80.x: The year 2026 has been identified as the UN International Year of the Woman Farmer.
80.tq: Use the year–designation association and reject nearby but unsupported themes.
xs: **2026** is the **UN International Year of the Woman Farmer** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The notes name no other designation for 2026.
xa: AP is pushing farmers from **paddy** to **drought-hardy crops** amid a **rain deficit** (28 Aug 2026).
**APCNF** covers **10.20 lakh farmers**.

80.s: A policy in Andhra Pradesh seeks to move farmers away from paddy towards drought-hardy crops. This policy response is primarily associated with:
o: A surplus of perennial river water
80.x: The shift from paddy to drought-hardy crops in Andhra Pradesh is being promoted amid a rain deficit.
80.tq: Link the agricultural decision to the stated climatic pressure rather than to an unrelated geographical condition.
xs: AP is shifting farmers from **paddy** to **drought-hardy crops** amid a **rain deficit** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The notes link the shift to rain deficit alone.
xa: AP is India's **largest fruit producer**.
**2026** is the UN International Year of the **Woman Farmer**.

80.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh agriculture is NOT correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh is identified as India’s largest fruit producer.
Podu cultivation has been stated to occur exclusively in the coastal plains of Andhra Pradesh.
Podu cultivation persists in the agency tracts.
Andhra Pradesh ranks first in oil palm among the listed agricultural distinctions.
80.x: Podu cultivation persists in the agency tracts, not exclusively in the coastal plains. The other three statements correctly describe the stated agricultural features of Andhra Pradesh.
80.tq: Identify the wrong location by testing the extreme word “exclusively.”
xs: "**Podu** occurs **exclusively in the coastal plains**" is wrong: podu **persists in agency tracts** — so option **(2)** is the answer.
AP is India's **largest fruit producer** and 1st in **oil palm** — both correct.
xa: AP is also 1st in **papaya, cocoa, chillies**.
Cocoa: **Côte d'Ivoire** 1st, **Ghana** 2nd in the world; **AP 1st in India**.

81.s: Which of the following combinations regarding wheat cultivation is correct?
o: Zaid crop; hot nights and waterlogged soils
Perennial crop; uniform rainfall throughout the year
Rabi crop; cool growing season, 50–75 cm rainfall and warm sunny ripening
Kharif crop; very high humidity and rainfall above 150 cm
81.x: Wheat is a rabi crop requiring a cool growing season, about 50–75 cm rainfall and warm, sunny conditions during ripening.
81.tq: Match the crop season with its growth and ripening requirements.
xs: Wheat is a **rabi** crop needing a **cool growing season**, **50-75 cm** rainfall and **bright warm sun at ripening** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Wheat is not kharif: very high humidity and heavy rainfall describe **rice** (above **100 cm**), which is the **kharif** cereal.
Wheat is the **2nd** most important cereal in India, grown on the alluvium of the **Ganga-Satluj plains**.
xa: Wheat also grows on the **black soil of the Deccan** — the APPSC-G1 2024 trap called it unsuitable, which is incorrect.
⚠ Rice **above 100 cm** vs wheat **50-75 cm**; rice = **kharif**, wheat = **rabi**.
Leading wheat states (2026 order): **Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana**.
India is **2nd** in the world in wheat with **117.94 MMT**.

81.s: Which of the following statements about pulses in India is correct?
o: India is the world's largest producer and consumer of pulses; gram is a rabi crop and tur is a kharif crop.
Pulses are grown only in irrigated regions and cannot be cultivated in both seasons.
Tur is a rabi crop, whereas gram is cultivated only as a kharif crop.
India is the world's largest importer but not a major consumer of pulses; gram is a kharif crop.
81.x: India is the world's largest producer and consumer of pulses. Gram is generally a rabi pulse, while tur or arhar is a kharif pulse.
81.tq: Separate the country-level status from the season-wise distinction between gram and tur.
xs: India is the world's **largest producer and consumer of pulses**; **gram** is a **rabi** pulse and **tur (arhar)** a **kharif** pulse — option **(1)** is correct.
Pulses are grown in **both seasons** and are **rain-fed, low-moisture** crops, so "only irrigated" (option 2) is wrong.
Option (3) reverses the seasons: tur is kharif, gram is rabi.
xa: Pulses **fix atmospheric nitrogen** and are used in **crop rotation**.
Leading pulse states: **Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, UP, Karnataka**.
**Dalhan Aatmanirbharta Mission (Oct 2025)**: **100% MSP procurement of tur, urad, masoor for four years**.
Pulses, oilseeds and coarse cereals **lagged** during the Green Revolution.

81.s: Which one of the following cereals ranks first in India in terms of importance and is a staple food for more than half of the country's population?
81.x: Rice is the first-ranking cereal in India and is the staple food of more than half of the country's population.
81.tq: Use the rank and population-share clue to identify the cereal.
xs: **Rice** is India's **1st** cereal and the staple of **over half of India** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Wheat** is the **2nd** most important cereal; **maize** and **millets** are kharif crops of lesser rank.
Rice needs **20-35°C** (above **25°C** ideal), high humidity and **above 100 cm** rainfall.
xa: **West Bengal** is the "**Rice Bowl of India**" and the largest producer.
India (**150.18 MT**) has now **surpassed China** (**145.28 MT**) as the world's largest rice producer.
India is the **largest rice exporter**, with **~40%** of world trade.
Rice suits **clayey/loamy**, deltaic and coastal alluvium soils.

81.s:
With reference to the cultivation of rice in India, consider the following statements:
1. Rice requires high humidity.
2. A temperature above 25°C is considered ideal for rice.
3. Rice requires more than 100 cm of rainfall, though irrigation can compensate for inadequate rainfall.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: All three statements are correct. Rice grows best under high humidity, temperatures above 25°C and rainfall exceeding 100 cm, or equivalent irrigation.
81.tq: Test a cluster of climatic requirements by checking each statement independently.
xs: Statement 1 correct: rice needs **high humidity**.
Statement 2 correct: **20-35°C** suits rice, with **above 25°C** ideal.
Statement 3 correct: rice needs **above 100 cm** rainfall, or **irrigation** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Rice is the **kharif** (main) crop and India's **1st** cereal.
⚠ Rice **above 100 cm** vs wheat **50-75 cm**.
Soils: **clayey/loamy**, **deltaic and coastal alluvium**.
Irrigated rice is important in **Punjab**; **West Bengal** is the largest producer.

81.s: Rice is especially suited to which of the following soil and geographical environments?
o: Clayey or loamy soils of deltaic and coastal alluvial areas
Laterite soils of upland plateaus only
81.x: Rice is well suited to clayey or loamy soils, particularly the deltaic and coastal alluvium.
81.tq: Match the crop with its characteristic soil and landform.
xs: Rice suits **clayey or loamy soils** of **deltaic and coastal alluvium** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Sandy soils** of the driest tracts suit **bajra**, not rice; **red soils** are linked with **ragi**.
Rice needs **above 100 cm** rainfall, so desert and arid soils are unsuitable.
xa: **AP and TN rice deltas** gained in the Green Revolution through irrigation.
Wheat grows on the alluvium of the **Ganga-Satluj plains** and the **black soil of the Deccan**.
**Lower Gangetic Plains** (West Bengal) zone: **rice, jute**.
AP paddy output **127.15 lakh MT** (2024-25).

81.s: Which one of the following statements regarding wheat cultivation in India is NOT correct?
o: It requires a cool growing season and bright warm sunshine at the time of ripening.
It is mainly a rabi crop.
Wheat is the second most important cereal in India.
The black-soil region of the Deccan is unsuitable for wheat cultivation.
81.x: The statement is NOT correct. Wheat is grown not only in the Ganga-Satluj plains but also in the black-soil region of the Deccan.
81.tq: Find the reversed suitability statement, especially where a known crop-soil association is denied.
xs: The NOT-correct statement is that the **black-soil region of the Deccan is unsuitable for wheat** — option **(4)**; black soil does suit wheat.
Statements 1-3 are true: wheat needs a **cool growing season** and **bright warm sun at ripening**, is a **rabi** crop and the **2nd** most important cereal.
This was the **APPSC-G1 2024** trap: black soil is listed with **cotton, jowar, oilseeds** as a wheat-suitable soil.
xa: Wheat's main belt is the **Ganga-Satluj plains** (Indo-Gangetic "**wheat bowl**").
Wheat rainfall: **50-75 cm**.
Wheat states: **UP, MP, Punjab, Haryana** (2026 order).
The first Green Revolution phase (mid-1960s-1980s) was largely **wheat**.

81.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Pulses — high-moisture crop requiring continuous heavy rainfall
Millets — mainly kharif crops suited to dryland and rainfed tracts
Wheat — crop of hot and humid monsoon season
Rice — crop requiring low-input dryland conditions
81.x: Millets are mostly kharif crops and are climate-resilient, low-input crops of dryland and rainfed tracts.
81.tq: Eliminate pairs that reverse the characteristic climate or season of the crop.
xs: **Millets** are **mostly kharif**, **climate-resilient, low-input** crops of **dryland/rainfed tracts** — option **(2)** is correct.
Pulses are **rain-fed, low-moisture** crops, not heavy-rainfall crops; wheat is **rabi**, not monsoon.
Rice needs **above 100 cm** rainfall or irrigation, not dryland conditions.
xa: Some millets are **rabi in the south**.
Major millets: **Bajra** (~**60%** of India's millet output), **Jowar**, **Ragi**; minor: foxtail, little, kodo, proso.
India is the **largest millet producer**, **42.75%** of world output (**18.59 MMT**).
**2023** was the UN **International Year of Millets**; millets branded **Shree Anna**.

81.s: Which one of the following pairs of food crop and its characteristic growing condition is correctly matched?
o: Bajra — red soils of humid tracts
Ragi — sandy soils of the driest tracts
Pulses — fix atmospheric nitrogen and are used in crop rotation
Rice — less than 50 cm rainfall without irrigation
81.x: Pulses are leguminous and fix atmospheric nitrogen, which is why they are used in rotation. Bajra suits the driest conditions and sandy soils, not humid red soils; ragi is associated with red soils; rice needs above 100 cm of rainfall or irrigation.
81.tq: Pulses = nitrogen fixers; bajra = sandy, driest; ragi = red soils.
xs: **Pulses** **fix atmospheric nitrogen** and are **used in rotation** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Bajra** suits the **driest** tracts and **sandy soils**; **ragi** suits **red soils** — options 1 and 2 swap them.
**Rice** needs **above 100 cm** rainfall or irrigation, not under 50 cm.
xa: A **pulse-cereal rotation** leaves fixed nitrogen for the next crop.
**Intercropping** example: **tur with jowar or maize**.
Pulses grow in **both seasons**: kharif (**tur/arhar**) and rabi (**gram**).
**Rajasthan** leads bajra; **Karnataka** leads ragi.

81.s:
Arrange the following wheat-producing states in descending order of production:
A. Haryana
B. Madhya Pradesh
C. Uttar Pradesh
D. Punjab
81.x: The stated order is Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Haryana.
81.tq: For an order question, first identify the leading state and then compare the middle positions.
xs: The 2026 order of wheat states is **Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana** — i.e. **C, B, D, A**, option **(1)**.
Wheat is the **2nd** cereal and a **rabi** crop of the **Ganga-Satluj plains**.
xa: **Punjab, Haryana, western UP** were the **core Green Revolution** states.
India is **2nd** in world wheat output (**117.94 MMT**).
⚠ For pulses the order starts with **MP**, then **Rajasthan**; for rice **West Bengal** leads.
Wheat also grows on the **black soil of the Deccan**.

81.s: Which of the following correctly gives the order of the leading pulse-producing states?
o: Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka
Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra
Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Karnataka
81.x: The stated order for leading pulse-producing states is Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka.
81.tq: Treat production order as a ranking problem and preserve the first two positions carefully.
xs: Leading pulse states: **Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka** — option **(1)**.
India is the world's **largest producer and consumer of pulses**.
xa: Pulses grow in **both seasons**: **tur/arhar** (kharif) and **gram** (rabi).
**Dalhan Aatmanirbharta Mission (Oct 2025)**: **100% MSP procurement of tur, urad, masoor** for four years; target **350 lakh tonnes** a year.
⚠ Wheat order is **UP, MP, Punjab, Haryana** — do not confuse with the pulse order.
Pulses **fix atmospheric nitrogen** and fit **crop rotation**.

81.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the distribution of major food crops in India:
1. Rice is produced in West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha, Bihar and Tamil Nadu.
2. Wheat is chiefly associated with Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana and Madhya Pradesh.
3. Rice is exclusively a rainfed crop in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because rice is grown with both rainfall and irrigation, including irrigated Punjab.
81.tq: Use the word exclusively as a warning and verify the crop's stated regional distribution.
xs: Statement 1 correct: rice states include **West Bengal, UP, Punjab, AP, Telangana, Odisha, Bihar, TN**.
Statement 2 correct: wheat leaders are **UP, MP, Punjab, Haryana**.
Statement 3 wrong: rice needs **above 100 cm** **or irrigation** and **Punjab** grows irrigated rice — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: **West Bengal** = "**Rice Bowl of India**", largest producer (2026).
**Rajasthan** leads **bajra**; **Karnataka** leads **ragi**.
Rice-wheat is the dominant **double cropping** system of the **Indo-Gangetic plains**.
MSP and free power favour rice-wheat, e.g. **paddy in Punjab**.

81.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Maize — Tamil Nadu; exclusively winter cultivation
Bajra — Rajasthan; driest conditions and sandy soils
Jowar — West Bengal; humid deltaic conditions
81.x: Rajasthan is the leading bajra-producing state, and bajra is suited to the driest conditions and sandy soils. Ragi is led by Karnataka, while jowar is associated mainly with Maharashtra and Karnataka.
81.tq: Check the crop-soil-climate relationship before accepting the state match.
xs: **Bajra** is led by **Rajasthan** and suits the **driest** conditions and **sandy soils** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Maize** is a **kharif** crop led by **Karnataka, MP**, not a winter crop of Tamil Nadu.
**Jowar** is led by **Maharashtra, Karnataka**; **ragi** by **Karnataka** on **red soils**.
xa: **Bajra** (pearl millet) gives ~**60%** of India's millet output.
Millet leaders: **Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Karnataka** (2026).
**Andhra Pradesh** was marked a major **jowar** state in the APPSC 2025 key.
El Nino and conflict are pushing farmers to **bajra/jowar** (2026).

81.s: Which of the following correctly describes the leading states associated with millets?
o: Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Karnataka, with Rajasthan leading in bajra production
West Bengal, Bihar and Odisha, with West Bengal leading in bajra production
Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, with Punjab leading in ragi production
Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Assam, with Kerala leading in all millet production
81.x: The leading millet states listed are Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Karnataka. Rajasthan is the largest producer of bajra, while Karnataka leads in ragi.
81.tq: Use the crop-specific leader to distinguish the broader millet-producing group.
xs: Millet leaders are **Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Karnataka**, with **Rajasthan largest** in **bajra** — option **(1)**.
**Ragi** is led by **Karnataka**, not Punjab; West Bengal is the **rice** leader.
xa: India is the **largest millet producer**: **18.59 MMT** on 12.86 million ha, **42.75%** of world output.
Major millets: **bajra, jowar, ragi**; minor: **foxtail (kangni), little (kutki), kodo (kodon), proso (chena)**.
Millets are branded **Shree Anna**; **2023** was the **International Year of Millets**.
Bajra = ~**60%** of India's millet output.

81.s: Which of the following statements about maize production is correct?
o: West Bengal and Odisha lead maize production, which is concentrated only in deltaic soils.
Rajasthan and Punjab are the only leading states, and Andhra Pradesh has no significant maize region.
Tamil Nadu and Kerala lead maize production, and maize is grown only as a rabi crop.
Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh are leading states, while production is rising in the Godavari–Krishna districts of Andhra Pradesh.
81.x: Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh are listed as leading maize-producing states, with rising production in Andhra Pradesh's Godavari–Krishna districts.
81.tq: Combine the national leaders with the specified emerging regional centre.
xs: **Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh** lead maize, and output is **rising in AP's Godavari-Krishna districts** — option **(4)** is correct.
Maize is a **kharif** crop driven by **feed/starch demand**, so "only rabi" is wrong.
xa: In AP, maize is surging in **Godavari and Krishna** for **poultry feed**.
Maize is covered under **NFSNM**.
**Intercropping** example: **tur with jowar or maize**; **parallel cropping**: **maize + green gram**.
**West Bengal** leads **rice**, **Rajasthan** leads **bajra**.

81.s: Which State is known as the 'Rice Bowl of India' and is currently the largest producer of rice?
81.x: West Bengal is called the Rice Bowl of India and is the largest rice producer. Uttar Pradesh, Punjab (irrigated rice) and Andhra Pradesh are also important rice states, but none leads West Bengal.
81.tq: Rice Bowl = West Bengal (largest producer).
xs: **West Bengal** is the "**Rice Bowl of India**" and the **largest producer** (2026) — option **(3)**.
**UP, Punjab** (irrigated), **AP** are also rice states but trail West Bengal.
xa: Other rice states: **Telangana, Odisha, Bihar, TN**.
India produced **150.18 MT**, **surpassing China** as world's largest rice producer.
India is the **largest rice exporter**, **~40%** of world trade.
**Lower Gangetic Plains** zone (West Bengal): **rice, jute**.

81.s: Among the following States, which one was marked in the APPSC 2025 key as a major producer of jowar?
81.x: The APPSC 2025 key marked Andhra Pradesh as the major jowar state among the options. Rajasthan is known for bajra, West Bengal for rice and Uttar Pradesh for wheat.
81.tq: APPSC 2025: jowar → Andhra Pradesh (textbooks: Maharashtra, Karnataka).
xs: The **APPSC 2025 key** marked **Andhra Pradesh** as the major **jowar** state among UP / Rajasthan / AP / West Bengal — option **(3)**.
**Rajasthan** is the largest **bajra** state; **West Bengal** is the **rice** leader; **UP** tops **wheat**.
xa: Textbook jowar leaders: **Maharashtra, Karnataka**.
Jowar is a **kharif/rabi**, dry, rainfed crop (sorghum).
Jowar is a **major millet** with bajra and ragi.
⚠ Black soil is listed with **cotton, jowar, oilseeds** — and also suits wheat.

81.s: Which phase of agricultural development is marked by a price policy based on minimum support price and procurement?
81.x: The third phase of agricultural development is marked by a price policy based on MSP and procurement.
81.tq: Associate the policy characteristic with the correct phase of agricultural development.
xs: The **third phase** is marked by a **price policy based on MSP and procurement** (PYQ 2017) — option **(3)**.
The **first phase** (mid-1960s-1980s) was largely **wheat**; the **second phase (1980s)** spread east and west.
xa: Second-phase output growth was **3.4% vs 2.3%** earlier.
Inputs included **HYV seeds**, fertilisers, irrigation, mechanisation and **MSP**.
The New Agricultural Strategy began **1965** (dated **1968** in current notes).
Procurement is confined to **rice, wheat, sugarcane**, which use over two-thirds of India's urea.

81.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Green Revolution:
1. The first phase from the mid-1960s to the 1980s was largely centred on wheat.
2. Rice benefited in a later and wider phase.
3. Pulses and coarse cereals were the principal crops of the first phase.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because wheat was central to the first phase, while pulses and coarse cereals lagged.
81.tq: Find the crop-imbalance trap in the statement that reverses the first-phase beneficiaries.
xs: Statement 1 correct: the first phase (**mid-1960s-1980s**) was largely **wheat**.
Statement 2 correct: **rice** gained in a **later, wider phase**.
Statement 3 wrong: **pulses, oilseeds, coarse cereals lagged** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: The crops most benefited were **wheat and rice** (APPSC 2025 key).
Second phase (**1980s**): spread east and west; growth **3.4% vs 2.3%**.
Third phase: **MSP and procurement** price policy.
Crop imbalance — **pulses, oilseeds, millets neglected** — is a key limitation.

81.s: Norman Borlaug is especially associated with which contribution to the Green Revolution?
o: Development of IR-8 rice in the Philippines
Introduction of canal irrigation in Punjab
Formulation of India's minimum support price policy
81.x: Norman Borlaug is associated with HYV Mexican dwarf wheat and received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.
81.tq: Discriminate between the scientist associated with wheat and the institution associated with rice.
xs: **Norman Borlaug** developed **HYV Mexican dwarf wheat** — option **(2)**.
He is the **Father of the Green Revolution in the world** and won the **Nobel Peace Prize 1970**.
MSP policy belongs to the **third phase**, not to Borlaug.
xa: ⚠ Father in **world** = **Borlaug**; father in **India** = **M.S. Swaminathan**.
**Swaminathan** brought **HYV wheat** to India.
**C. Subramaniam**, Union Agriculture Minister, backed the strategy.
The strategy began **1965** as the **New Agricultural Strategy**.

81.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu gained from the spread of irrigated rice cultivation.
2. The Green Revolution helped India move from PL-480 wheat imports towards food self-sufficiency.
3. The Green Revolution completely eliminated regional imbalance in Indian agriculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because rainfed and hill areas remained comparatively neglected, creating regional imbalance.
81.tq: Reject the absolute claim that a major agricultural transformation eliminated every imbalance.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **AP and TN rice deltas** gained via **irrigation**.
